senses.text: alphabetical letter The eighteenth letter of the alphabet: called EayonN . It is [one of the letters termed majohuwrap , or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, not with the breath only; and] of the letters termed Haloqiy~ap [or faucial]; these being E and H and h and x and g [and A^ ]; the lowest of which in its place of utterance is E ; wherefore Kh [in the composition of his lexicon entitled “ Kitáb el-'Eyn ”] and several other lexicographers [after him] began their books with [words having] this letter [in their roots], giving the next place to H , the next to h , the next to x , and the next to g . (L, TA.) It is substituted for ' [in what is termed the EanoEanap of Temeem]; as in Eano for A^ano : and for H ; as in Eat~aY for Hat~aY , and SuboEN for SuboHN : and for g ; as in EulaA

and ↓ (but the latter is rarely used, Ibn-'Arafeh) Angry. (L.) And (both words) Disdaining, or disdainful; scorning, or scornful. (L.) [a rel. n. from EabodN ]. Ald~araAhimu AlEabodiy~apu Certain Dirhems, which were superior to those of late times, and of greater weight. (O, K, TA.)

[dim. of EabodN . ― -b2- And, used as a proper name,] The son of the desert, or of the waterless desert: thus expl. by El-Kanánee to Fr. (O.) ― -b3- And [hence] A^um~u EubayodK The desert, or waterless desert, (Fr, O, K,) that is vacant, or desolate: (K:) or the land that is vacant, or desolate: (El-Kaná- nee, Fr, O:) or the land that the rain has missed. (O, K.) And sometimes it is used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Great calamity: (TA:) it is said in a prov., waqaEuwA fiY A^um~i EubayodK taSaAyaHu Hay~aAtuhaA [for tataSaAyaHu , lit. They became, or found themselves, in the desert, &c., of which the serpents were hissing, one at another ], meaning (assumed tropical:) [ they fell ] into a great calamity. (Meyd, TA.)

(S, IKtt, A, IAth, L, K) and ↓ and ↓ (IKtt, K) and ↓ (Fr, K) and ↓ and ↓ (L) [all said by some to be inf. ns., except the fourth,] Religious service, worship, adoration, or devotion; (L;) obedience: (S, IKtt, A, K:) obedience with humility or submissiveness; humble, or submissive, obedience: (IAth, L:) or EibaAdapN signifies the Doing what God approves: and ↓ , the approving what God does: and the primary signification of ↓ is humility, and submissiveness: (S, A, O:) EibaAdapN is rendered only to God, or a false god, or the Devil. (TA.)
: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places: ― -b2- and see Eubuwdiy~apN .
The [ portion, or appertenance, of the stomach, of a ruminant, called ] faHiv , (O, K, TA,) also called Hafiv [q. v.]. (TA.)
The state, or condition, of a slave; slavery; servitude; (S, O, L, Msb;) as also ↓ (S, O, L) and ↓ (O, Msb) and ↓ . (L.) ― -b2- See also EibaAdapN , in two places.

and EabaAbiydu , each a pl. having no sing., Parties of people (S, O, K) going in every direction: (S, O:) and horsemen going in every direction. (K.) One says, SaAra Alqawomu EabaAdiyda and EabaAbiyda The people became divided into parties going in every direction. (S, O.) And *ahabuwA EabaAdiyda and EabaAbiyda They went away in parties in every direction. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (both words, K, or the latter [only], TA,) Far-extending roads: (K:) or diverse and far-extending roads: said to be used in this sense not with respect to coming, but only with respect to dispersion, and going away. (TA.) ― -b3- Also (or the former [only], TA) Hills such as are called A_ikaAm or A=kaAm [pls. of A^akamapN ]. (K, TA.) ― -b4- And one says, mar~a raAkibFA EabaAdiydahu He passed, or went away, riding upon t

A server, a worshipper, or an adorer, of God: (L:) an obeyer of God with humility, or submissiveness: (L, Msb:) [ a devotee: ] a unitarian: (L:) by a secondary application, used of him who takes for his god other than the True God, such as an idol, and the sun, &c.: (Msb:) pl. Eub~aAdN and EabadapN (L, Msb) and EubudN and Eub~adN , all of which are also pls. of EabodN [q. v.]: (L:) [and quasi-pl. n. ↓ (like as xadamN is of xaAdimN ), accord. to a reading of a phrase in the Kur v. 65, as expl. by some.] ― -b2- And A servant: a meaning said to be tropical. (TA.) ― -b3- See also EabidN , in two places.

A shovel, or spade, of iron; syn. misoHaApN : (K:) pl. maEaAbidu . (TA.)
, and the pl. maEaAbidu : see EabodN , last quarter: -A2- and for the former see also EibaAdapN .

, applied to a camel, Rendered submissive, or tractable; broken, or trained; syn. mu*al~alN : (A, L:) or anointed with tar, (S, O, K,) and rendered submissive, or tractable: (S, O:) or whose whole skin is anointed with tar: (Sh:) or mangy, or scabby, whose fur has fallen off by degrees, and which is set apart from the other camels to be anointed with tar: or rendered submissive by the mange, or scab: or affected with the mange, or scab

; or with incurable mange or scab. (L. [And, applied to a camel, it has other meanings, which see in what follows.]) [And hence, app.,] safiynapN muEab~adapN A ship, or boat, tarred: (AO, S, O, L, K:) or smeared with fat, or oil. (AO, L.) ― -b2- Applied to a road, Beaten; syn. mu*al~alN ; (S, A, O, K;) trodden; (Az, TA;) or travelled by many passengers going to and fro: (TA:) and syn. with mu*al~alN as applied to other things also. (K.) ― -b3- And [hence] A wooden pin, peg, or stake. (Az, O, K, TA. [In the CK, Almuw^at~adu is erroneously put for Alwatidu .]) So in the following verse of Ibn-Mukbil: waDam~anotu A^arosaAna AljiyaAdi muEab~adFA A_i*aA maA DarabonaA raA^osahu laA yuran~aHu [ And I made a wooden peg to be a guarantee for the ropes of the coursers: when we beat its head, it did
Also, applied to a country, or tract of land, In which is no footprint, or track, nor any sign of the way, nor water: (O, K:) you say baladN muEab~adN . (O.)
and maEobuwdaA='u : see EabodN , last quarter.
[and ↓ ] A place appropriated to religious services or exercises, or acts of devotion. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. EaborN and EubuwrN , [the latter of which is the more common,] (S, O, Msb, K,) He crossed it, went across it, or passed over it, (Mgh, Msb, K,) from one side thereof to the other; (Msb, K;) namely, a river, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, *) and a valley, (K, TA,) &c. (S, Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Eabara bihi AlmaA='a : see

2. ― -b3- Eabara Als~abiyla , (Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. EubuwrN , (TA,) He travelled, or passed along, the way, or road; (Msb, K; *) as though he cut it, or furrowed it. (K, * TK.) ― -b4- And hence, (TA,) Eabara , (aor. as above, S,) (tropical:) He died: (S, O, Msb, K:) as though he travelled the road of life: or, as F says in the B, as though he crossed over the bridge of the present world or life. (TA.) A poet says, faA_ino naEoburo faA_in~a lanaA lumaAtK waA_ino nagoburo fanaHonu EalaY nu*uwri i. e. (tropical:) So if we die, there are others like to us; and if we remain alive, we are waiting for that which must necessarily come to pass, as though we were bound by vows to meet it. (S, O.) ― -b5- And Eabarati Als~aHaAy^ibu , aor. as above, inf. n. EubuwrN , The clouds travelled, or passed

; or I made the birds to fly away in order that I might augur from their flight, &c.]. (O, K.) ― -b3- And Eabara AlkitaAta , aor. , inf. n. EaborN , (As, S, A, * O, K, *) He meditated upon, endeavouring to understand it, or he considered, examined, or studied, (As, S, O, K,) or he read mentally, (A,) the book, or writing, not raising his voice in doing so, (As, S, A, O, K,) i. e. in reading it. (K.) And you say, baEoDa ↓ AlkitaAbi bibaEoDK , meaning Eabarahu [i. e. He considered and compared one part of the book, or writing, with another part, in order to understand it ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And Eabara AlmataAEa , and Ald~araAhima , (K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. EaborN , (TA,) He examined what was the weight of the goods, and of the dirhems, and what they were. (K, TA.) And you say, Ald~araAhima fawaja

2 , (Lh, K,) inf. n. taEobiyrN ; (TA;) and bihi AlmaA='a ↓ , (Lh, K,) and Aln~ahora ; (TA;) He made him to cross, go across, or pass over, or he conveyed him across, the water, (Lh, K, TA,) and the river. (TA.) -A2- Eb~r Alr~uw^oyaA , (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. as above; (S, O;) and ↓ , (S, A, O, Msb, K,) [which is less common, but more chaste,] aor. , (S, O,) inf. n. EibaArapN (S, A, O, Msb, K) and EaborN ; (A, Msb, K;) He interpreted, or explained, the dream, (S, A, O, Msb, K,) and told its final sequel or result: (A, O, K:) or the former verb has an intensive signification: (Msb:) and taEobiyrN has a more particular [or more restricted] meaning than taA^owiylN : it is said to be from Eabara AlkitaAba [q. v.]

; or, as some say, it is from EiborN signifying the “ side ” of a river, because the interpreter of the dream considers the two sides thereof, and meditates upon every particular of it from its beginning to its end. (TA.) In the phrase of the Kur [xii. 43], A_ino kunotumo lilr~uw^oyaA ↓ , the l is termed laAmu Alt~aEoqiybi [the l of succedaneousness], because it is succedaneous to the connection termed A_iDaAfap [i. e. the phrase is succedaneous to A_ino kunotumo EaAbiriY Alr~uw^oyaA If ye be interpreters of the dream ]: (O, TA:) or it is inserted as an explicative: (Zj, TA:) the phrase is similar to A_ino kunota lilomaAli jaAmiEFA . (S, O.) ― -b2- Eb~r Eam~aA fiY nafosihi , (A, K, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He declared, spoke out clearly or plainly, or explained, what was in his mind. (

Hence, yuEab~iru Eano ka*aA , said of a word or phrase, It expresses the meaning of, signifies, or denotes, such a thing. And yuEab~aru bihi Eano ka*aA The meaning of such a thing is expressed thereby

; or such a thing is signified, or denoted, thereby. ] ― -b3- Eb~r Ald~anaAniyra , (A,) or Al*~ahaba , (K,) inf. n. as above, (A, K,) He weighed the deenárs, (A,) or the gold, (K,) deenár by deenár: (A, K:) or Eb~rhu signifies he weighed it (a thing), or measured it, without extraordinary care: (K, * TA:) and taEobiyru Ald~araAhimi , the weighing of the dirhems collectively, after making divisions of them. (S, O, TA.) -A3- Eb~r bihi , (K, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) signifies A^araAhu Eubora Eayonihi (K, TA, in the CK Eayonayohi ,) i. e. He showed him what would make his eye to weep: or what would make his eye hot. (TA.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, EalaY malaqiy~aAtK yuEab~irona bAlgufori [ Upon swiftly-running mares that show the mountain kids, in the swiftness of their pace, what makes their eye

8 He became admonished, or reminded; he took warning, or example: in this sense the verb is used in the Kur lix. 2: and you say, AiEotabara bimaA maDaY He became admonished or reminded, or he took warning or example, by what passed: (Msb:) and Als~aEiydu mina A@Eotabara bigayorihi waAl$~aqiY~u mani A@Eotabara bihi gayoruhu [ The fortunate is he who takes warning by others, and the unfortunate is he by whom others take warning ]. (Kull p.

60.) And EabarN [as inf. n. of ↓ , aor. ,] signifies the same as AiEotibaArN [as inf. n. of AiEotabara in the sense expl. above]: (Fr, O, L, K, TA:) whence the saying of the Arabs, Aall~`hum~a A@joEalonaA mim~ano yaEobaru Ald~unoyaA walaA yaEoburuhaA , (Fr, O, L, TA,) with fet-h to the b of yEbr in the first case, and with damm to it in the second case, (TA,) meaning O God, make us to be of those who take warning, or example, by the present world, and do not [ pass through it or] die quickly, or soon, until they content Thee by obedience: (Fr, O, L, TA:) in the copies of the K, mim~ano yaEoburu Ald~unoyaA walaA yaEomuruhaA , the former verb with b [and damm], and the latter with m [and damm]: and in the A is given, as a trad., AuEoburuwA Ald~unoyaA walaA taEomuruwhaA : but the reading give

60.) See, again, EiborapN . Ibn-Seereen used to say, A^aEotabiru AlHadiyva [ I judge by comparison with what has been transmitted by tradition from the Prophet]; meaning I interpret a dream according to what has been transmitted by tradition, like as I do according to the Kur-án; as when a crow is interpreted as meaning an unrighteous man, and a rib as meaning a woman, in imitation of forms of speech used by the Prophet. (O, * TA.) ― -b3- See also 1, latter half, in two places. ― -b4- Also He accounted, or esteemed, or regarded, a thing, in respect of predicamental order. (Msb.) See, again, EiborapN . ― -b5- [And He esteemed a person, or thing; held him, or it, in high estimation or regard. ― -b6- And He took a thing into account, regarded it, or included it in a mental view or an examinat

(See AlgumayoSaA='u .)] -A2- AstEbrhu Alr~uw^oyaA He asked him to interpret, or explain, the dream; (K;) he related to him the dream in order that he might interpret, or explain, it. (S, O.) ― -b2- laqado A^asoraEota A@sotiEobaAraka Ald~araAhima is a saying mentioned by As as meaning [ Assuredly thou hast hastened ] thy drawing forth of the dirhems. (O.) -A3- See also 1, last quarter, in two places. ― -b2- [Accord. to Golius, AstEbr is also syn. with AEtbr in the first of the senses assigned to the latter above; but for this I do not find any authority.]
: see EiborN . -A2- Eaboru A^asofaArK and Eaboru safarK : see what here follows.

and AsfArK ↓ (S, K) and AsfAr ↓ (K) and Euboru safarK and sfrK ↓ and sfrK ↓ (TA) A he-camel, and a she-camel, and camels, like a ship [or ships ], i. e. upon which journeys are continually made: (S:) or a she-camel that is strong (K, TA) to journey, (TA,) [ as though ] cutting. or furrowing, what she passes over, (K, TA,) and upon which journeys are made: (TA:) and likewise a man (K, TA) bold to undertake journeys, vigorous and effective therein, and strong to make them: and in like manner a he-camel, and camels: (TA:) applied to a sing. and to a pl. (K, TA) and to a fem.: (TA:) and in like manner also ↓ , applied to a he-camel, (K,) meaning strong (O, TA) to journey; and so ↓ , with kesr, [app. pl. of EaborN ,] applied to camels. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence one says, likul~i EamalK ↓ Verily such a

, (S, O, K, TA, in the CK Eiborap ,) and ↓ , (S, O,) or ↓ , (Kr, A, K, TA, accord. to the CK Eaborap ,) The bank, or side, (S, A, O, K,) of a river, (S, A, O,) and of a valley. (A, K.) En-Nábighah Edh-Dhubyánee says, of the Euphrates, taromiY A^awaA*iy~uhu AlEiborayoni biAlz~abadi [ Its waves casting foam upon the two banks ]. (S, O.) And one says, fulaAnN fiY *`lika AlEibori Such a one is upon that side. (TA.) -A2- See also the next preceding paragraph, in three places.
inf. n. of Eabira [q. v.]. (AZ, T, &c.) ― -b2- See also EuborN , in two places: ― -b3- and EaborapN .
; and its fem., with p ; see EaAbirN .
: see EuborN , in two places.

: see EibaArapN . -A2- Also A tear: (TA:) or a tear before it overflows: or a [ sobbing, or] reiteration [ of the sound ] of weeping in the bosom: (A, K:) or an overflowing of tears without the sound of weeping: (TA:) or a flowing, or an oozing, of tears: (S, O:) or grief without weeping: (A, K:) pl. EabaraAtN (O, K) and ↓ , (so in the O, [but this, if correct, is a quasi-pl. n.,]) or EibarN . (Thus in copies of the K.) Of the first meaning, the following is an ex.: waA_in~a $ifaAy^iY EaborapN lawo safaHotuhaA [ And verily my cure would be a tear if I shed it ]: and of the last, the following is an ex.: laka maA A^abokiY walaA Eaborapa biY or, as some relate it, wlA Ebrp liY ; and the meaning is, For thy sake I weep, but there is grief in me for myself: so says As: (TA:) or in this saying,

a subst. from AlAiEotibaAru ; An admonition, or exhortation: (Bd in iii. 11): an admonition, or exhortation, by which one takes warning or example: (Jel in xxiii. 21:) a thing by the state, or condition, of which one is admonished, or reminded, and guided, or directed: (Bd in xxiii. 21:) i. q. ↓ [lit. a being admonished, or reminded, &c.; but meaning a cause of being admonished, &c.; i. e. a warning, or an example ]: (Jel in xvi. 68:) or AiEotibaArN bimaA maDaY i. e. Ait~EaAZN and ta*ak~urN [meaning, in like manner, a cause of being admonished, or reminded, by what has passed ]: (Msb:) an indication, or evidence, (Bd and Jel in xxiv. 44, and Bd in xvi. 68,) whereby one passes from ignorance to knowledge: (Bd in xvi. 68:) a state [ of things or circumstances ] whereby, from the knowledge of

, applied to the [species of lote-tree called] sidor , means That grows on the banks of rivers, and becomes large: (S, O:) an anomalous rel. n. from EiborN : (TA:) [or a regular rel. n. from EuborN as syn. with EiborN :] or, accord. to 'Omárah, such as is large in the leaves, having few thorns, and taller than the DaAl : or, as Aboo-Ziyád says, that has no thorns except such as hurt [ not (see sidorN )]; the thorns [that hurt] being of the sidor called DAl : he does not say, as others do, that it is that which grows upon the water: some assert that it is also called EumoriY~N , the b being changed into m : (O:) or, as some say, such as has no trunk; and such is only of those that are near to the Eibor [or bank of a river ]: Yaakoob says that the terms EuboriY~ and EumoriY~ are applied to t

[ Hebrew: and a Hebrew ]. AlEiboriy~uwna is an appellation of The Jews [i. e. the Hebrews ]. (O.) ― -b2- And AlEiboriY~u and ↓ , (S, A, K,) or AlEiboriy~apu (O) and ↓ , (O, TA,) [ The Hebrew language; ] the language of the Jews. (S, A, O, K, TA.)
; and its fem. EaboraY : see EaAbirN , in six places.
and AlEiboraAniy~apu : see EiboriY~N .
: see Euboru A^asofaArK .

[ The star Sirius; ] a certain bright star; (TA;) one of the $iEorayaAni , which [ in the order of rising ] is after, or behind, [in the TA, erroneously, “ with, ”] AljawozaA=' [here meaning Gemini ]: (S, O:) called AlEbwr because of its having crossed the Milky Way. (S, O, TA.) [See also Al$~iEoraY in art. $Er . ― -b2- Hence the saying, EaSafato dabuwruhu wasaqaTato Eabuwruhu , expl. in art. dbr .]

A certain mixture (As, S, O, Msb, K) of perfumes, (Msb, K,) compounded with saffron: (As, S, O:) or, (K,) with the Arabs (S, O, TA) of the Time of Ignorance, (TA,) accord. to AO, it means saffron (S, O, K, TA) alone: but in a trad., mention is made of smearing with Ebyr or with saffron; and this shows Ebyr to be different from saffron: (S, O, TA:) IAth says that it is a sort of perfume, having colour, compounded of certain mixtures. (TA.) [See a verse cited voce *abiyHN ; and another cited voce raqoraqa .]
: see the next paragraph, in two places.

Speech that passes from the tongue of the speaker to the ear of the hearer. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence, A passage in a book or writing. ] ― -b3- [Hence also,] A word, an expression, or a phrase. (Kull p.

60.) ― -b4- And [ An explanation, or interpretation; ] a subst. from Eab~ara Eanohu ; as also ↓ , (L, K, TA, [the former only in the CK,]) and ↓ or ↓ , accord. to different copies of the K. (TA.) You say, huwa Hasanu AlEibaArapi , and, accord. to the M, ↓ also, i. e. He has a good faculty of explaining, or of diction, or of speaking perspicuously. (Msb.) [And h`*aA EibaArapN Eano ka*aA This is a word, or an expression, or a phrase, for, or denoting, such a thing; lit., an explanation of such a thing. ] -A2- Also A thing that is made a condition: or a thing that is made account of, or esteemed, or regarded as being of importance. (Msb.)
: see Euboru A^asofaArK . -A2- Also An interpreter, or explainer, of dreams. (TA.)

A wayfarer; a passenger; a person passing along a way or road; (S, O, TA;) a traveller: (TA:) or one who passes through without abiding: (Mgh:) pl. EaAbiruw sabiylK and Eub~aAru sabiylK . (TA.) And EaAbiru Als~abiyli The wayfarer; the passer along the way or road. (Msb.) A_il~aA EaAbiriY sabiylK , in the Kur [iv. 46], means Except those who, wanting something in the mosque, and their houses or tents being distant, [merely pass through, or] enter the mosque and go forth quickly: (TA:) or except travellers; for the traveller sometimes wants water [which is found in the mosque]: or, as some say, except passers through the mosque, not meaning to pray. (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- Hence EaAbirN signifies (tropical:) Dying, or dead. (TA. [See

1.]) ― -b3- [And Passing, or having currency. Hence,] lugapN EaAbirapN An allowable form of word or expression: (S, K, TA:) from Eabara signifying “ he passed over ” a river. (TA.) -A2- EaAbirN also signifies Examining a thing: examining a book, or writing, and considering and comparing one part of it with another, so as to understand it. (TA.) -A3- Also Shedding tears, (S, O, *) applied to a man, and likewise to a woman: and ↓ weeping, applied to a man; and so [its fem.] ↓ applied to a woman: (S, O:) or ↓ signifies weeping and grieving, applied to a man; as also ↓ ; (K, * TA;) and EaAbirN and ↓ and ↓ are applied to a woman in the same sense, (K,) or as meaning grieving: (TA:) pl. A stranger (Az, S, Z, O, K) among a people: (O, K:) occurring, in the accus. case, in a trad., in which some read gariyrFA , with the pointed g ; and some say that the right reading is gariy~FA , i. e. muloSaqFA [here meaning “ an adherent ”]: but Hr and IAth agree with Az [and the S] and Z and the [O and] K. The tree called sarow [which is the common, or evergreen, cypress; but the former name is generally applied in the present day to the juniper-tree ]; (S, O, K;) a Pers. word: (K:) it is a kind of great tree, of the trees of the mountains: (O:) some say that it is the [ tree called ] saAsam , and also [ said to be ] called $iyzaY : others, that it is a great kind of mountain-tree, evergreen, called by the Persians sarow : (TA:) AHn says that he had been informed by an Arab of the desert, of the people of the Saráh ( Als~araAp ), who are possessors of the EaroEar , that it is the A^abohal [q. v., a name now applied to the juniper-tree, like EaroEar ; and particularly to the species thereof called the savin ]; and he adds that he knew it in his own country, and afterwards saw it in the provin
: see EaroEaArN , in art. rE .

A camel having the mange, or scab; as also ↓ ; (A'Obeyd, S, O;) which latter [in some of the copies of the K written ↓ ] is applied in this sense to a man; and ↓ to a camel: (K:) or this last signifies having, or affected with, the disease called Eur~ . (S, O, K.) ― -b2- See also muEotar~N .

Hence, AlmaEar~apu The region of the sky that is beyond the Milky Way ( Almajar~ap ) in the direction of the North Pole; so called because of the multitude of the stars therein; (O, * TA;) like as the sky is called AljarobaA='u because of its numerous stars; these being compared to scabs on the body of a man: (TA:) and to this and the majar~ap a man alluded, when, being asked respecting the place where he alighted and abode, he informed the inquirer that he alighted and abode between two tribes, (O, TA,) great and numerous; (O;) saying, nazalotu bayona AlmaEar~api waAlmajar~api [ I have alighted between the maEar~ap and the majar~ap ]: (O, TA:) or, as some say, (O,) AlmaEar~apu is the name of a certain star, or asterism, [ which is ] below the majar~ap [or Milky Way, app. meaning when the

One who addresses, or applies, himself to obtain favour, or bounty, without asking; (I'Ab, S, O, * Msb, K;) one who comes to another, and seeks his favour, or bounty

And A poor man. (K, TA.) It occurs in the Kur xxii. 37: accord. to some, having the last of these meanings: accord. to others, the first thereof. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , [aor. ,] inf. n. EuruwbapN , His tongue [or speech ] was, or became, Arabic, (S, O,) or chaste Arabic. (Msb.) ― -b2- See also 4, first sentence, in three places. -A2- Eariba , aor. , inf. n. EarabN , He (a man) became disordered in the stomach by indigestion. (TA.) And Earibato maEidatuhu , inf. n. as above, His stomach became in a corrupt, or disordered, state, (S, O, Msb, K,) from being burdened. (TA.) ― -b2-

Also, (O, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) said of a camel's hump, (O, TA,) It became swollen and purulent. (O, K, TA.) ― -b3- And, said of a wound, (S, O, K, TA,) It became corrupt: (TA:) or it broke open again
; or became recrudescent: (S, O:) or it had a scar remaining after it had healed. (K.) ― -b4- Said of a river, It abounded with water. (K.) And Earibati Albiy^oru The well contained much water

; or its water became abundant. (K.) ― -b5- And, (K, TA,) inf. n. EarabN (O, * K, * TA) and EaraAbapN , said of a man, (TA,) He was, or became, brisk, lively, or sprightly. (K, TA.) -A3- Earaba , (O, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. EarobN , (TK,) He ate (O, K) food. (TK.)

2 , (S, O,) inf. n. taEoriybN , (S,) He (an Arab) arabicized a foreign word; spoke it, or pronounced it, agreeably with the ways of Arabic speech; (S;) as also ↓ , (S, O, *) inf. n. A_iEoraAbN . (TA.) ― -b2- And He taught another the Arabic language. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b3- See also 4, in fourteen places. ― -b4- The inf. n. signifies also The showing, or declaring, one's saying, (K, TA,) and one's deed, (TA,) to be bad, evil, abominable, or foul. (K, TA.) One says, Er~b Ealayohi He showed him, or declared to him, that his saying, and his deed, was bad, &c.; and upbraided him for it. (TA.) And faEalotu ka*aA waka*aA famaA Ear~aba EalaY~a A^aHadN I did so and so, and no one upbraided me

; or charged me with having acted disgracefully. (AZ, TA.) And Er~b Ealayohi fiEolahu , (S, O,) and qawolahu , (TA,) He showed him, or declared to him, that his deed was bad, evil, abominable, or foul, (S, O,) and so his saying. (TA.) taEoriybN is The saying to a man who has uttered what is foul, or erroneous, “ It is not so, but so; ” telling him what is more correct. (Sh, TA.) And The replaying against a speaker; (K, TA;) and so ↓ . (TA.) One says, Er~b Ealayohi He replied against him, denying or disallowing or disapproving what he said: (S:) or he prevented, hindered, or forbade, him: or he did so, and denied or disallowed or disapproved [ what he said or did ]. (TA.) [See what next follows.] ― -b5- Also The treating medically, to remove his disease, one whose stomach is in a corrupt, o

; or pruning it by cutting off some of its branches. (S, O, K. *) ― -b7- And The scarifying a horse or similar beast in the parts of the skin next the hoofs and then cauterizing those parts: (K, TA:) or the cauterizing a horse in several places in those parts, and then gently scarifying them without producing any effect upon the sinews, or tendons, (Az, O, TA,) in order to strengthen the parts, (Az, TA,) or in order that the hair may become strong: (O:) or Er~b Alfarasa signifies he made an incision in the bottom of the horse's hoof; and the verb implies that, by this operation, what was concealed becomes apparent to the eye, so that one knows the state of the hoof, whether it be hard or soft, sound or diseased. (L, TA. See also
1 in art. bzg .) -A2-

What I find in the TA, on this subject, is as follows.] The former of these two divisions consisted of nine tribes, descendants of Irem [or Aram] the son of Sám [or Shem] the son of Nooh [or Noah]; namely, 'Ád, Thamood, Umeiyim, 'Abeel, Tasm, Jedees, 'Imleek [or Amalek], Jurhum, and Webári; and from them Ismá'eel [or Ishmael is said to have] learned the Arabic language: and the ↓ are [said to be] the descendants of Ismá'eel, the descendants of Ma'add the son of 'Adnán the son of U

; or what modern logicians call a mode; whether it be, in their language, an essential mode or an accidental mode; which latter only they term “ an accident; ”] as colour, and taste: (B:) or, in the conventional language of the Muslim theologians ( Almutakal~imuwn [expl. in the TA as signifying “ the philosophers, ” from whom, however, they are generally distinguished]), a thing that subsists in, or by, another thing; (O, K;) as colours, and tastes, and smells, and sounds, and powers, and wills: (O: [and the like is said in the Msb:]) or, in philosophy, a thing that exists in its subject, or substance, and ceases therefrom without the latter's becoming impaired or annihilated; and also such as does not cease therefrom: the former kind being such as tawniness occasioned by an altered state

Hence, An appertenance of any kind. ― -b5- Hence also,] The frail goods ( HuTaAm ) of the present world or state; (As, O, K;) and what a man acquires thereof: (As, O:) [so called as being not permanent:] or worldly goods or commodities, (AO, Msb,) of whatever kind, are thus called, with fet-h to the r : (AO:) and any property or wealth, little or much, (S, O, K,) is thus called, (K,) or is called EaraDu Ald~unoyaA . ; or he was, or became, acquainted with it; syn. Ealimahu : (K:) or he knew it ( Ealimahu ) by means of any of the five senses; (Msb;) [and also, by mental perception: ] Er-Rághib says, AlmaEorifapu is the perceiving a thing by reflection, and by consideration of the effect thereof [ upon the mind or sense ], so that it has a more special meaning than AlEilomu , and its contr. is AlA_inokaAru ; and one says, fulaAnN yaEorifu A@ll~`ha warasuwlahu [ Such a one knows God and his apostle ], but one does not say yaEolamu A@ll~`ha , making the verb [thus] to have a single objective complement, since man's maEorifap [or knowledge] of God is [the result of] the consideration of his effects, without the perception of his essence; and one says, Aall~`hu yaEolamu ka*aA , but not yaEorifu k*A , since

; or as meaning I attained its Eurof i. e. limit: (TA:) it is said in the B that AlmaEorifapu differs from AlEilomu , in meaning, in several ways: the former concerns the thing itself [which is its object;] whereas the latter concerns the states, or conditions, or qualities, thereof: also the former generally denotes the perceiving a thing as a thing that has been absent from the mind, thus differing from the latter; therefore the contr. of the former is AlA_inokaAru , and the contr. of the latter is Aljaholu ; and the former is the knowing a thing itself as distinguished from other things; whereas the latter concerns a thing collectively with other things: (TA in art. Arab., pp. cxxiii. and 177;)] a sort of trees of the [ description termed ] EiDaAh , (S, O, K,) which exudes [ the gum called ] mugofuwr , and of which the fruit ( baramap ) is white and round: (S:) it has a gum of disagreeable odour ; and when bees eat it, somewhat of its odour is found in their honey: (TA:) AHn says that, accord. to Aboo-Ziyád, it is of the EDAh , and spreads upon the ground, not rising towards the sky, and has a broad leaf, and a sharp, curved thorn; it is of those trees of which the bark is stripped off and made into well-ropes; (O, TA;) and there comes forth from its fruit ( baram ) what is termed Eul~afapN , [i. e. a pod, ] resembling a bean, (O, * TA,) which is eaten by the camels and the
Camels that eat the [ kind of trees called ] EurofuT . (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b2- Earaqotu maA EalaY AlEuraAqi mina All~aHomi I pared off what was on the bone, of flesh, with a miEoraq , i. e. a large, or broad, knife or blade. (TA.) ― -b3- And [hence,] Earaqatohu Als~inuwna , aor. as above, i. e. [ The years, or droughts, or years of drought, ] took from him [ his flesh, or rendered him lean ]; namely, a man. (TA.) AlxuTuwbu ↓ , also, signifies the like, i. e. [ Afflictions, or calamities,

Hence, app.,] TariyqN yaEoruquhu Aln~aAsu (K, TA) A road which men travel [as though they pared it]. (TA.) -A2- Earaqa fiY AlA^aroDi , (S, O, K,) aor. , (S, O, TA,) not , as seems to be required by the method of the K, (TA,) inf. n. EuruwqN (S, O, TA) and EaroqN , (TA,) He (a man, S, O, TA) went away into the country, or in the land; syn. *ahaba [which, followed by fY AlArD , often means he went into the open country, or out of doors, to satisfy a want of nature ]. (S, O, K, TA.) -A3- Earaqa AlmazaAdapa , (K, TA,) and Als~uforapa , aor. , inf. n. EaroqN , (TA,) He made to the mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag ], (K, TA,) and to the suforap [or round piece of skin in which food is put and upon which one eats ], (TA,) what is termed an EiraAq [q. v.]. (K, TA.) -A4- Eariqa , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor

2 see 4, third sentence. ― -b2- Er~q Al$~araAba , (S, O, K,) inf. n. taEoriyqN , (S, O,) He mixed the wine, [ with water, ] not doing so immoderately: (S, O:) or he put a little water into it; as also ↓ ; (K;) or the latter signifies he put into it some water, not much: (S:) [but] accord. to Lh, AlkaA^osa ↓ signifies I filled the cup of wine: or, accord. to IAar, Ear~aqotu AlkaA^osa signifies I put little water to the cup of wine; and so ↓ : but the former of these two phrases is also expl. as meaning I mixed the cup of wine; whether with little or much water not being specified: (TA:) and Alxamorapa ↓ signifies I mixed [ with water the wine, or portion of wine ]. (Ham p.

561.) ― -b3- Er~q fiY Ald~alowi , (S, O, K, TA,) inf. n. as above; (O, K;) and fiyhaA ↓ ; (O, K, TA;) He put into the bucket less water than what would fill it, (S, O, K,) on the occasion of drawing: (S, O:) or he put little water into the bucket; and so fiY Als~iqaA='i [ into the skin ]: (TA:) and Ear~iqo fiY AlA_inaA='i Put thou less than what would fill it into the vessel. (S.) ― -b4- bar~aqota waEar~aqota Thou madest a sign with a thing, that had nothing to verify it, [or madest a false display, or a vain promise, ] and didst little. (IAar, TA in this art and in art. brq .) -A2- Er~q Alfarasa , (O, TA,) inf. n. as above; and ↓ ; (TA;) He made the horse [ to sweat, or] to run in order that he might sweat, and become lean, and lose his flabbiness of flesh. (O, * TA.) -A3- See also 4, aga

; or wine with a little mixture [ of water ]. (Ham p.

561.) ― -b4- See also 2, in four places. -A3- AErq Alfarasa : see 2, last sentence but one. -A4- AErq Al$~ajaru , (S, O, K,) and Aln~abaAtu , (S,) The trees, (S, O, K,) and the plants, (S,) extended their roots into the earth; (S, O, K, * TA;) in the K, Ai$otad~ato is erroneously put for Aimotad~ato , and so [in one place] in the O; (TA;) as also ↓ , said of trees, (M, O, TA,) and ↓ , (M, TA,) and in like manner, ↓ , and ↓ , said of trees, i. e., struck their roots into the earth, as in the A: (TA:) [but accord. to Mtr,] in the phrase fiY ↓ miloki gayorihi , meaning [ A man of whom a tree ] whereof the root crept along beneath the ground [ into the property of another ], in [one of the books of which each is entitled] “ the Wáki'át, ” tEr~qt should correctly be ↓ . (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] o

10 He exposed himself to the heat in order that he might sweat: (IF, O, K:) he stood in a place on which the sun shone, and covered himself with his clothes [ for that purpose ]. (Z, TA.) -A2- See also 4, former half. -A3- AstErqt AlA_ibilu The camels pastured near to the sea or a great river, i. e., in a place of pasture such as is termed EiraAq : so says AZ: or, as AHn says, the camels came to a piece, or tract, of land, such as is termed Eiroq , i. e., one exuding water and producing salt and giving growth to trees. (TA.)

(S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ (K) [the latter also a pl.] A bone of which the flesh has been taken: (S, O:) or a bone of which the flesh has been eaten: (Msb, K:) or a bone of which most of the flesh has been taken, some thin and savoury portions of flesh remaining upon it: (TA:) or the former signifies a bone upon which is flesh: and one upon which is no flesh: or, as some say, whereof most of that which was upon it has been taken, some little remaining upon it: (Mgh:) or, as some say, a piece of flesh-meat; as also ↓ : (TA:) or EaroqN signifies a bone with its flesh: and ↓ , a bone of which the flesh has been eaten: (K:) thus they are correctly expl. accord. to Ez-Zejjájee; and the like is said by AZ respecting ↓ : (TA:) but accord. to A'Obeyd, this signifies a piece of flesh-meat; and IAmb says
A certain appertenance of a tree; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) the root thereof

; or the part thereof that is beneath the ground; (MA;) or its branching roots [ collectively ]: (TA:) pl. [of mult.] EuruwqN (S, O, Msb, K) and EiraAqN and [of pauc.] A^aEoraAqN . (K.) ― -b2- It is said in a trad., layosa liEiroqK ZaAlimK Haq~N , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) i. e. li*iY EiroqK ZaAlimK , (Mgh, O, Msb,) meaning (tropical:) [ There is no right pertaining ] to him who plants, (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) or sows, (S,) in land, (Mgh, Msb,) or in land which another has brought into cultivation (S, O, Msb) after it has been waste, (S, O, Msb, *) wrongfully, in order that he may have a claim to that land: (S, Mgh, O, Msb:) the epithet being tropically applied to the Eiroq , (Mgh, Msb,) as it properly applies to the owner thereof: (Mgh:) but some, in relating this trad., say liEiroqi ZaAlimK , making t
; or to Ishmael, as, accord. to some, the root, or source, of all the Arabs: (see “ Le Diwan d'Amro'lkais, ” p.
33 of the Ar. text, and p.
103 of the Notes:) and the pl.] A^aEoraAqN signifies the ancestors of a man. (Har p.

634.) [And A quality, or disposition, possessed by a parent or by an ancestor or by a collateral of such person, considered as the source of that quality of a disposition in a descendant or in a collateral of a descendant: and such a quality, or disposition, when transmitted; a strain; i. e. a radical, a hereditary, an inborn, or a natural, disposition: and a radical, or hereditary, share in some quality or the like: pl. A^aEoraAqN .] One says, tadaArakahu A^aEoraAqu xayorK [ Good qualities or dispositions possessed by a parent or by an ancestor or by a collateral of such a person, or strains of a good kind, extended to him ]; and A^aEoraAqu $ar~K or sawo'K [ evil qualities or dispositions &c., or strains of an evil kind ]. (TA.) And AlEiroqu das~aAsN [ The natural disposition is wont to e

Hence, app., A little, or modicum, or small quantity or admixture, of something]. One says, fiyhi EiroqN mino HumuwDapK , and muluwHapK , i. e. In it is a little, or a modicum, of acidity, and of saltness. (TA.) And fiY Al$~araAbi EiroqN mina AlmaA='i In the wine is a small quantity [or admixture ] of water. (S, O, K.) ― -b11- Also A certain appertenance of the body; (O, Msb, K, TA;) i. e. the hollow [ canal ] in which is the blood; (TA;) [ a blood-vessel; a vein, and an artery: also any duct, or canal, in an animal body: and sometimes, though improperly, a nerve: or any one of the appertenances of the body that resemble roots: ] pl. [of mult.] EuruwqN (O, Msb, K) and EiraAqN (K) and [of pauc.] A^aEoraAqN . (Msb, K.) [Hence it may be applied to A spermatic duct: and hence, app.,] it is sai

Sweat; i. e. the moisture, or fluid, that exudes (S, * O, * K, TA) from the skin of an animal; (K, TA;) or the water of the skin, that runs from the roots of the hair: a gen. n.; having no pl.; (TA;) or no pl. of it has been heard: (Msb:) Lth says, I have not heard a pl. of AlEaraqu ; but if it be pluralized, it should be, accord. to analogy, A^aEoraAqN . (O, TA.) ― -b2- It is metaphorically used [in a similar sense] in relation to other things than animals. (K.) [Thus] it signifies The [ exuded ] moisture of a well: (K:) and in like manner of earth, or land, when the dew, or rain, has percolated in it ( nataHa fiyhaA ) so that it has met the moisture thereof. (TA.) ― -b3- And The dibos [or honey ] of dates; (K;) because it flows, or exudes, from them. (TA.) ― -b4- And Milk; because it flo

; or it means a safiyfap [or plaited suspensory ] which the carrier of the qrbp puts over his chest [ when carrying the qrbp on his back ]: (K:) accord. to IAar, it signifies the suspensory ( miEolaAq ) by means of which the qrbp is carried; as also EalaquhaA ; (O, TA;) the r being substituted for l : (TA: see art. r :]) but he says also that Earaqu Alqirobapi means one's sweating with the qrbp by reason of the difficulty, or trouble, of carrying it; and EalaquhaA , that by which it is tied, or bound, and then suspended: (L, TA:) the former is also said to signify the ↓ [q. v.] of the qrbp , that is sewed around it: (TA:) or it means that one has imposed upon himself difficulty, or trouble, or fatigue, like that of the carrier of the qrbp , who sweats beneath it by reason of its heaviness.

(O, K) and ↓ and ↓ (K) A root, race, stock, or source; syn. A^aSolN : (O, K:) or a source of wealth or property: or the main portion of the root of a tree. from which the Euruwq [or minor roots ] branch off: (K:) or, as some say, EiroqaApN has this last meaning

; or, as others say, ↓ . (Ltl., O.) They said, AisotaA^oSala A@ll~`hu ↓ and EiroqaAtihimo ; if they pronounced the first letter with fet-h, they so pronounced the last letter [before the pronoun]; and if they pronounced the former with kesr, they thus pronounced the latter, regarding the word as pl. of ↓ : (K:) or, accord. to Lth, the Arabs are related to have said, AisotaA^oSala A@ll~`hu EiroqaAtahumo , meaning $aA^ofatahumo [i. e. May God utterly destroy their race, stock, or family ], pronouncing the t with nasb because regarding the word as [a sing.] like siEolaApN

; or holding it to be pl. of ↓ , but pronouncing the ta thus like as they do in saying raA^ayotu banaAtaka : it is said, however, that this is a mistake; that only he should pronounce it thus who makes the word to be a sing. like siEolaApN . (O.) [The saying is a prov., mentioned by Meyd, who adds another reading, namely, EaraqaAthm , holding this to be from ↓ meaning “ the Tur~ap that is woven around the fusoTaAT : ” and Freytag, in his Lexicon, adds also EariqAtah , with nasb, as on the authority of Meyd; in whose “ Proverbs ” I do not find it.]
[accord. to general analogy without tenween and having for its fem. EaroqaY , or accord. to the dial. of the Benoo-Asad with tenween and having for its fem. EaroqaAnapN ,] Sweating. (Msb.)

is thus, (S, O, K,) with fet-h to the E , (S, O,) like taroquwap , (K,) and should not be pronounced with damm to the first letter; (S, O, K;) and ↓ signifies the same; (K, TA; [in the CK, erroneously, EaraqaAtuhA ; but expressly stated in the TA to be with fet-h and then sukoon;]) i. e. The piece of wood that is put across the dlw [or leathern bucket, from one part of the brim to the opposite part ]: (TA:) the EaroquwataAni being the two pieces of wood that are put athwart the dlw [ to keep it from collapsing and for the purpose of attaching thereto the well-rope ], like a cross: (As, S, O, K:) pl. (K.) ― -b3- And A copious rain: (K:) or so ↓ [only]. (TA.) ― -b4- And EuraAqu Algayovi The herbage that has come forth after the rain. (Ibn-'Abbád, A, O, K.)

The double suture that is in the lower part of the [leathern water-bag called] mazaAdap and raAwiyap ; (Lth, O, K;) and this is of the firmest kinds of suture therein: (Lth, O:) or the suture that is in the middle of the qirobap [or water-skin]: (TA:) or the piece [or strip ] of skin that is put upon the place where the two extremities, or edges, of the [ main ] skin meet when it is sewed in, or upon, the lower part of the mzAdp : (K:) or the appertenance of the qrbp , and of the mzAdp , &c., which is [ a strip of skin ] doubled and then sewed [ thereon thus ] doubled: (Msb:) or, accord. to AZ, the [ piece of ] skin that is doubled, and then sewed upon the lower part of the [water-skin or milk-skin called] siqaA=' : (S:) and, (K,) accord. to As, (S, O,) i. q. TibaAbapN ; (S, O, K;) i. e. t

, (S, O, K,) applied to a man and to a horse, means [ Rooted, i. e.] having a radical, or hereditary, share, ( lahu Eiroq , S, O,) in generousness or nobleness [of origin, which, accord. to the S and O, and common usage, seems to be implied by the epithet when used absolutely], (S, O, K,) and also in meanness or ignobleness [thereof

; or having a strain of, i. e. an inborn disposition to, generousness or nobleness, and also meanness or ignobleness]. (S, * O, * K.) And you say also fiY Alkarami ↓ and fiY All~uw^omi [ Such a one is rooted, &c., in generousness or nobleness and in meanness or ignobleness ]; and lahu fiY ↓ Alkarami ; (S, O;) and lahu fiY Alkarami ↓ , [the part. n. being formed] on the supposition of the suppression of the augmentative letter [in its verb, which is A^uEoriqa ]: (TA:) and in like manner, (S, O, TA,) in a trad., (O, TA,) a man of whom there is no living ancestor between him and Adam is said to be lahu fiY Almawoti ↓ (S, O, TA) i. e. Made to have a radical, or hereditary, share ( EiroqN ) in death; (O, TA;) meaning that he will inevitably die. (S, O, TA.) [In the Ham p. 438, ↓ is expl. as syn

Of, or belonging to, the country called AlEiraAq . (Msb.) ― -b2- A_ibilN EiraAqiy~apN means Camels that pasture upon what are termed EiraAq , i. e. remains of the [ plants, or trees, called ] HamoD : (K, * TA:) or, app., accord. to Az, camels of, or belonging to, AlEiraAq as meaning the waters of Benoo-Saad-Ibn-Málik and Benoo-Mázin: or, as some say, of, or belonging to, the EiraAq as meaning the side, or shore, of water: and it is also said that the epithet in this phrase is a rel. n. from AlErq [thus in my original, without any syll. sign and without explanation]. (TA.)

, with teshdeed [to the r ], A thing [app. a cloth for imbibing the sweat ] that is put beneath the tklp [app. meaning pad ] of the saroj [or horse's saddle ] and the baro*aEap [q. v.]. (TA. [The word tklp , which I have not found anywhere except in this instance, I can only suppose to be an arabicized word from the Pers. or Turkish taGalotuw , which is commonly pronounced by the Turks takalotiY , with k and Y , and which means a pad, or a piece of felt, put beneath the saddle to prevent its galling the beast's back. ])

[act. part. n. of Earaqa ]. A poet says, A^akuf~u lisaAniY Eano SadiyqiY faA_ino A^ujaA^o A_ilayohi faA_in~iY EaAriqN kul~a maEoraqi [ I restrain my tongue from my friend; but if I be compelled to have recourse to him in a case of need, I am one who gnaws to the utmost: maEoraq being here an inf. n.]. (S, O: mentioned in both immediately after the explanation of Earaqotu AlEaZoma .) ― -b2- And [the pl.] AlEawaAriqu signifies The A^aDoraAs [i. e. teeth, or lateral teeth, &c.]: (K:) an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates. (TA.) ― -b3- And The sinuwn [i. e. years, or droughts, or years of drought ]; so called lA^an~ahaA taEoruqu AlA_inosaAna , (K, TA, in some copies of the K AlA^asonaAna ,) i. e. because they take from the man [his flesh, or render him lean]. (TA.)

, The night, in the year, most abundant in milk. senses.text: 1 He hocked, houghed, hamstrung, or cut the hock-tendon of, the beast. (S, A, O, K, *) ― -b2- And Earoqabahu He raised his hocks, (namely, a camel's, O,) in order that he might stand up: (O, K:) he assisted him (i. e. a camel) to stand up, by raising [ his hocks ]. (TA.) Thus the verb has two contr. meanings. (K.) ― -b3- And Earoqaba (assumed tropical:) He practised artifice, craft, or cunning. (O, K.) One says, A_i*aA A^aEoyaAka gariymuka faEaroqibo (assumed tropical:) [ When thy debtor wearies thee, ] practise artifice, &c. (AA, O, TA.)

2 He mounted a beast from behind. (O, TA.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) He took his course along the narrow roads, or ways, of the mountain, which are called EaraAqiyb . (S, O, K.) ― -b3- And tErqb lixaSomihi (assumed tropical:) He pursued a way hidden from his adversary: said when one adopts another and easier course of speech. (TA.) ― -b4- And tErqb Eani AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) He turned away, or declined, from the affair. (K.) ― -b5- A_i*aA maTala taEaqoraba waA_i*aA waEada taEaroqaba (assumed tropical:) [ When he puts off the fulfilment of his promise, he acts like 'Akrab (a man notorious for putting off the fulfilment of his promises); and when he promises, he acts like 'Orkoob ] (A, TA) is a prov. (TA. [See the following paragraph, last sentence but one.])

[The tendo Achillis, or heel-tendon; ] a certain tense, (T, A, Mgh, Msb,) or thick, (K,) or thick and tense, (S, O,) tendon, (T, S, A, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) behind the two ankle-bones, (T, A, Mgh, Msb,) above the heel; (S, O, K;) the thing that conjoins the shank and the foot; (As, TA;) in a human being: (S, O, K:) pl. EaraAqiybu . (TA, &c.) The saying of the Prophet, wayolN liloEaraAqiybi mina Aln~aAri [ Woe to the heel-tendons from the fire of Hell] means, to him who neglects the washing of them (Mgh, Msb) in the [ablution termed] wuDuwo' . (Msb.) ― -b2- [In a beast, it is in some instances applied to The hock, or hough; i. e.] the Euroquwb of a beast is that which, in its hind leg, corresponds to the rakobap [or knee ] in its fore leg: (S, O, K:) [in other instances, it is applied to the ten

; or a stratagem, or trick. (O, K. [See Q. 1, last signification.]) ― -b9- And (assumed tropical:) Knowledge ( EirofaAn ) of an argument, a plea, an allegation, or a proof. (O, K.) -A2- Also the name of a certain man of the Amalekites, (S, O, K, TA,) or, (so says Ibn-El-Kelbee, O,) of the Benoo-Abd-Shems-Ibn-Saad, (Jm, O, TA,) but this is said to be of no authority, (O,) or of El-Ows, (Jm, TA,) the greatest liar of his time, (K,) proverbial for breach of promises: (S, O:) El-Ashja'ee (whose name was Jubeyhà, O, K) says, waEadota wakaAna Alxulofu minoka sajiy~apF mawaAEiyda EuroquwbK A^axaAhu biyatorabi (S, O, K, TA) i. e. (tropical:) Thou promisedst, but breach of promise was an inherent quality of thee, like the promises of 'Orkoob to his brother in Yetreb; which is in El-Yemámeh
; or, as some relate it, biyavorib , i. e. El-Medeeneh, or, as some say, the land of the Benoo-Saad; but the former is the more correct. (TA. [See also Har p.
160.]) And one says, huwa A^ako*abu mino Euroquwbi yatoraba (tropical:) [ He is more mendacious than 'Orkoob of Yetreb ]. (A, TA.)

EarokN , (S, O,) He rubbed it, or rubbed and pressed it, or did so well; syn. dalakahu ; namely, a thing; (S, O;) such as a skin or hide, or a tanned skin or hide, and the like. (TA.) ― -b2- And [ He wore it away by scraping, &c.;] he scraped, rubbed, chafed, or fretted, it, until he erased, or effaced, it. (K.) ― -b3-

Hence, Earaka bijanobihi maA kaAna mino SaAHibihi , aor. and inf. n. as above, meaning (assumed tropical:) [ He acted ] as though he scraped, &c., [ with his side, ] what had proceeded from his companion, until he erased, or effaced, it: (TA;) [like as a camel allays an itching by rubbing with his side the trunk of a tree: i. e. he bore, or endured, what proceeded from his companion: for] yaEoruku AlA^a*aY bijanobihi means yaHotamiluhu [i. e. (assumed tropical:) He bears, or endures, annoyance, or molestation

Where the punishment of the Ea$~aAr , or EaA$ir , is mentioned in traditions, as where it is said that the EaA$ir is to be put to death, the meaning is, he who takes the tenth as the people in the Time of Ignorance used to do: such is to be put to death because of his unbelief

; or because, being a Muslim, he holds this practice to be lawful: but such as performed the like office for the Prophet and for the Khaleefehs after him may be thus called because of the relation of what he takes to the tenth, as the quarter of the tenth, and the half of the tenth, and as he takes the tenth wholly of the produce that is watered [only] by the rain, and the tenth of the property in merchandise [of foreigners, and half the tenth of that] of non-Muslim subjects. One says also, tE$~Y bihi He fed himself with it [ in the evening, or] in the time called the Ei$aA=' : and [in like manner] tataEa$~aAhu is said of camels [as meaning they feed themselves with it, or pasture upon it, in the evening ]. (TA.) And when one says to thee, taEa$~a [ Eat thou the evening-meal ], thou sayest, maA biY taEa$~K , (S,) or maA biY mino taEa$~K , (TA,) [ I have no desire for eating the evening-meal; see
5 in art. gdw ;] and not maA biY Ea$aA='N , (S,) or not mA by mino Ea$aA='K (TA.) -A2- See also
6. -A3- And tE$~Ahu signifies also He gave him an Ei$owap [or Eu$owap , i. e. a firebrand ]. (TA.)

6 He feigned himself A^aEo$aY [i. e. weaksighted, &c.; and so ↓ as used by Bd in xliii. 35]. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And [hence] (tropical:) He feigned himself ignorant, (K, TA,) Eano ka*aA [ of such a thing ], as though he did not see it; like taEaAmaY . (TA.)
8 He journeyed in the time of the Ei$aA=' [or nightfall ]: (K, TA:) like Ahtjr meaning “ he journeyed in the time of the haAjirap . ” (TA.) -A2- See also 1, latter half.

10 He found him to be deviating from the right course, or acting wrongfully, injuriously, unjustly, or tyrannically, ( wajadahu jaAy^irFA , K, TA, in some copies of the K HaAy^irFA ,) fiY Haq~i A^aSoHaAbihi [ in respect of the right, or due, of his companions ]. (TA.) -A2- And AstE$Y naArFA He guided himself by means of a fire. (K.)
A bowl ( qadaH ) of milk which is drunk at the time when the sheep, or goats, return from the pasture in the evening or afternoon, or after that time. (K.)
: see Ea$aA='N .

inf. n. of Ea$iYa : (S, Msb, K:) [used as a simple subst., Weakness of sight: or sightlessness by night with ability to see by day: or] badness of sight by night and by day; as also ↓ : (K:) it is in human beings, and beasts of the equine kind ( dawaAb~ ), and camels, and birds; as is said in the M: (TA:) or it is darkness that happens to the eye: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or blindness; (K, TA;) i. e. absolute destitution of sight. (TA.)

applied to a he-camel, and Ea$iyapN applied to a she-camel, That exceeds the other camels in the [ evening-pasture, or evening-feed, called ] Ea$aA=' ; each after the manner of the possessive epithet, having no verb. (TA. [And Ea$iY~N is said to have a similar meaning.]) -A2- See also A^aEo$aY .

Darkness, (K, TA,) in [any part of] the night and in the saHar [or period a little before daybreak]; (TA;) as also ↓ : (K:) or the first of the darkness of the night: (Az, TA:) or the period between the beginning and [ the end of ] the [ first ] quarter of the night: (AZ, S, K:) thus in the saying, maDaY mina All~ayoli Ea$owapN [ A period between the beginning &c. of the night passed ]: and one says also, A^axa*otu Ealayohimo biAlEa$owapi , meaning [ I laid hold upon them ] in the blackness of night: (AZ, S:) the dim. is ↓ . (Az, TA.) In the saying jaA='a Ea$owapa , meaning Ei$aA='F [i. e. He came at nightfall ], it [is an adv. n. which] may not be used otherwise than thus: you may not say, maDato Ea$owapu . (TA.) ― -b2- AlE$wp [app. AlEa$owapu ] as meaning AlEa$aA='u , like Algdwp [app. A
: see Ea$owapN . -A2-

Also, (S, K, TA,) and ↓ , (K, TA,) A fire which one sees by night from afar, and to which, or towards which, he repairs, or betakes himself, seeking to light himself thereby: (K, TA:) or (TA) a firebrand ( $uEolapN mino naArK ). (S, TA.)
: see Ea$owapN : -A2- and see also Eu$owapN .

A state of perplexity, and of having little guidance: so in the saying, A_in~ahumo lafiY Ea$owaY A^amorihimo [or, perhaps, mino A^amorihimo , i. e. Verily they are in a state of perplexity, &c., in respect of their case, or affair ]. (TA.)
Of, or relating to, the [ time called ] Ea$iy~ap [or Ea$iY~ , q. v.]. (S.)
A species of dates: (IDrd, K, TA:) or of palm-tress, (K, TA,) of such as are late in bearing. (TA.)

, (S, K, TA,) originally Ea$owaAnu , like gadoyaAnu [q. v.] which is originally gadowaAnu , (TA,) A man (S) eating the [ evening-meal, or eveningrepast, i. e. what is called the ] Ea$aA=' ; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ . (TA.)

The meal, or repast, (S, Msb, K,) of the Ei$aA=' [or nightfall ], (S, * Msb,) or of the Ea$iY~ [or late part of the evening, &c.]; (S, * K, TA;) [i. e. supper, in a general sense;] opposed to gadaA='N ; (S;) as also ↓ : (K: [in the CK, AlEi$`Y is erroneously put for AlEi$oYu :]) and in like manner both are used in relation to camels [as meaning their evening-pasture, or evening-feed: see an ex. voce EatamapN , and another voce A^aqoEasu ]: (S, TA:) pl. of the former A^aEo$iyapN ; (K, TA;) to which is added, in [some of] the copies of the K, and Eu$iY~N ; but this is correctly Ea$iYa , [or Ea$aA , as in some copies,] and commences another sentence. (TA.)

[The time of nightfall; i. e.] the first, or beginning, of the darkness (Msb, K) of night: (Msb:) [this is the sense in which it is generally used, and always when it is used as applied to one of the five times of the divinely-appointed acts of prayer; SalaApu AlEi$aA='i , and elliptically AlEi$aA='u alone, meaning the prayer of nightfall: ] or it is [the time ] when the sun has disappeared: (Az, TA:) or [the time ] from sunset (K) [i. e.] from the prayer of sunset (Msb, TA) to the Eatamap [or darkness after nightfall ]; (Msb, K, TA;) [and this is what is meant by its being said that it is] syn. with Ea$iY~N : (S:) or [the time ] from the zawaAl [meaning the declining of the sun from the meridian ] to the rising of the dawn: (S, K:) so some assert, and they cite, as an ex., gadawonaA gudow
6 and xvi. 12:]) this is accord. to the saying that the Ei$aA=' is from the prayer of sunset to the Eatamap . (TA.)

[The late part of the evening: or the evening: or the afternoon: i. e.] the last, or the latter, part of the day; (Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) as also ↓ : (K, TA:) this is the meaning commonly known: (Mgh:) or [the time ] from the prayer of sunset to the Eatamap [or darkness after nightfall ]; (S, Msb, TA;) like Ei$aA='N ; (Msb;) and so ↓ : you say, A^atayotuhu Ea$iY~a A^amosi and A^amosi ↓ [ I came to him late in the evening, or in the time between sunset and nightfall, &c., of yesterday ]: (S, TA:) or Ea$iY~N has the meaning expl. in the K [and mentioned above]; but ↓ relates to one day: and one says, jiy^otuhu Ea$iy~apF [ I came to him late in an evening, &c.] and Ea$iy~apa [ late this evening, &c.], and A^atayotuhu AlEa$iy~apa I came to him in the E$y~p [or late part of the evening, &c.,] of thi
: see Ea$iY~N , in ten places.
dim. of Ea$owapN , q. v.
, pl. Eu$ay~aAnaAtN : see Ea$iY~N , in two places.
and Eu$ayo$iyapN , pls. Eu$ayo$aAtN and Eu$ayo$iyaAtN : see Ea$iY~N ; the latter in two places.
and Eu$ayo$iyaAnN , pl., of the latter Eu$ayo$iyaAnaAtN : see Ea$iY~N .

: see Ea$oyaAnu . The fem., EaA$iyapN , applied to camels, means Eating the [ evening-pasture, or evening-feed, called the ] Ea$aA=' . (ISk, S, K.) It is said in a prov., AlEaA$iyapu tahiyju AlA=biyapa [ Such as are eating the E$A=' excite such as desire not, or refuse

; or she that is eating &c.]: i. e., when the camels that desire not, or refuse, the E$A=' see those that are eating it, they follow them, and eat it with them. (S. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii.

83.]) And [the pl.] AlEawaA$iY , (S, K, TA,) [when indeterminate, EawaA$K ,] as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates, (TA.) signifies Those (S, K, TA) camels, and sheep or goats, (K, TA,) that are pasturing by night. (S, K, TA.) ― -b2- See also 1, former half. ― -b3- [Hence,] EaA$iyapN signifies also Anything [meaning any man or animal ] looking and repairing, by night, towards the fire of a person who entertains guests. (TA.)

Weak-sighted: (Msb:) or sightless by night, but seeing by day: (S:) or having bad sight by night and by day: and so ↓ : (K:) fem. Ea$owaA='u , (S, Msb, K,) applied to a woman; (S, Msb;) [the masc. being applied to a man, and either masc. or fem. to a beast of the equine kind, and a camel, and a bird, (see Ea$FA ,)] and dual masc. A^aEo$ayaAni (TA) and fem. Ea$owaAwaAni : (S, TA:) [and pl. Eu$oYN .] ― -b2- The fem. Ea$owaA='u also particularly signifies. A she-camel that sees not before her, (S, K, TA,) [or that has weak sight, ] and therefore strikes everything with her fore feet, (S, TA,) not paying attention to the places of her feet [ on the ground ]. (TA.) [Hence] one says, rakiba fulaAnN AlEa$owaA='a , meaning (tropical:) Such a one prosecuted his affair without mental perception, or
1 in art. xbT .]) ― -b3- And EuqaAbN Ea$owaA='u An eagle that cares not how it beats the ground, and where it strikes with its talons. (TA.) ― -b4- See also the fem. voce Ea$owapN .
[ A place in which one eats the eveningmeal, or supper. ]

(S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and EuSoEaSN (O, Msb) and EaSoEaSN (IAar, Mgh, O, K) and EuSaEiSN (IAar, K, TA) and ↓ and ↓ and ↓ (IAar, O, K) and ↓ (L, TA) The [ caudal bone called the ] Eajob [q. v.] of the tail; (Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán, ” S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) which is felt by him who feels for it; (Zj ubi suprà;) i. e., the [ os coccygis, or] tail-bone; (S;) the small bone between the two buttocks: (Mgh:) or that of which the upper part is the Eajob , and its lower part the *anab : or the internal extremity of the spine; and the Eajob is its external extremity: (Az, in L, voce quHoquHN :) it is said to be the first part that is created, and the last that wastes away: (S, O:) or i. q. quHoquHN [q. v.]: (IAar, O voce EukodapN :) pl. senses.text: 1 , aor. , (K,) inf. n. EaSobN , (S, A, Mgh, O, K,) He twisted [a thing], or wound [it] round: (A, K, TA:) this is the primary signification: (TA:) and he folded [it]; (A, K;) or he folded [it] tightly: (S, O, TA:) and he bound [it], or tied [it]: (A, Mgh, K, TA:) EaSobN denotes the binding, or tying, a thing with another thing, lengthwise, or [more commonly] around. (O.) See also 2, first sentence. [And see maEoSuwbN .] ― -b2- He twisted, or spun, thread. (K, * TA.) And He put together thread, and bound it, previously to dyeing it. (TA.) ― -b3- EaSaba Alkabo$a , (S, O, Msb, K, *] aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., (S, Msb, K,) He bound, or tied, ( tightly, TA) the testicles of the ram, in order that they might fall, without his extracting them: (S, O, Msb, K:) and in like manner one

; or which He has imposed upon you and attached to you; by his commands and prohibitions. (TA.) ― -b9- EaSaba Al$~aYo'a and EalaY Al$~aYo'i , aor. , inf. n. EaSobN and EiSaAbN , He grasped the thing with his hand. (K, * TA.) A poet, cited by IAar, says, wakun~aA yaA qurayo$u A_i*aA EaSabonaA yajiYo'u EiSaAbunaA bidamK EabiyTi [ And we were, O Kureysh, when we grasped our opponents, such that our grasping brought fresh blood ]; EiSaAbunaA meaning our grasping those whom we opposed with the swords. (TA.) ― -b10- And EaSaba , aor. , inf. n. EaSobN , He clung, or kept, to a thing. (K.) One says, EaSaba AlmaA='a He kept to, or by, the water. (IAar, TA.) And EaSaba Alr~ajulu bayotahu The man remained, or stayed, in his house, or tent, not quitting it. (O, TA.) ― -b11- And He went round, encompas

12.) And EaSaba Alqawomu biAln~asabi i. q. A^aHaATuwA bihi [app. meaning The people, or party, included, or comprehended, the relations, or kinsmen; for Aln~asabu is often used for *awuw Aln~asabi ]. (Msb.) And EaSabati AlA_ibilu biAlmaA='i The camels surrounded, or encircled, the water. (S, O.) ― -b12- EaSaba Alr~iyqu bifiyhi , (S, O, K, * TA,) aor. , inf. n. EaSobN ; (K, TA;) and EaSiba , aor. ; (TA;) The saliva became dry in his mouth. (S, O, K, * TA.) And EaSaba Alr~iyqu faAhu (S, O, TA) The saliva by its drying made his mouth dry: and the saliva adhered to his mouth. (TA.) Aboo-Mohammad El-Fak'asee says, yaEoSibu faAhu Alr~iyqu A^aY~a EaSobi EaSoba AljubaAbi bi$afaAhi AlwaTobi [ The saliva makes his mouth dry, with what a drying ! as the drying of the spume of camels' milk on the lips
; or] very hungry

; or his bowels were almost dried up with hunger: because it is said of the practice of a hungry man's binding round his belly, as expl. voce maEoSuwbN [q. v.]. (TA.) ― -b14- EaSaba AlA^ufuqu The horizon became red. (S, O. [In Freytag's Lex. EaSiba , as from the K, in which I do not find it. See EaSobN .]) -A2- EaSiba , (S, O, K,) with kesr, (S, O,) like fariHa , (K,) said of flesh, or flesh-meat, It had many EaSaba [i. e. sinews, or tendons ]. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- And EaSiba , aor. , inf. n. EaSobN , [so in the TA, and so in a verse there cited, not EaSabN ,] He was, or became, firm and compact in flesh. (TA.) ― -b3- [Other meanings of this verb have been mentioned above.]

2 , (S, A, O, &c.,) inf. n. taEoSiybN , (S, A, O,) [ He bound, or wound round, a thing with several circumvolutions: ] he bound [or wound round ] a man's head with a turban, fillet, bandage, or the like; (S, * O, * Msb, K, * TA;) as also ↓ , inf. n. EaSobN : (MA:) and he bound a broken limb, or a wound, with a piece of rag or a bandage. (L, TA.) He turbaned a man; attired him with a turban. (A, TA.) ― -b2-

Hence, (A, O,) taEoSiybN signifies (tropical:) [The crowning a man: (see the pass. part. n.:)] the making a man a chief: (A, O, K, TA:) for turbans are the crowns of the Arabs: (O:) when a man's people made him a chief, they bound his head with a turban: (A, TA:) as kings wore crowns, so the chiefs of the Arabs wore red turbans: (L, TA:) there were brought to the desert, from Haráh ( haraAp ), red turbans, which the nobles among the Arabs wore. (Az, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] ES~bhu biAls~ayofi i. q. Eam~amahu bihi (assumed tropical:) [ He cut, or wounded, him in the place of the turban, with the sword ]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- And ES~bhu , inf. n. as above, He, or it, [ caused him to bind his waist by reason of hunger: (see the pass. part. n.:) and hence,] made him to hunger: (K:) and EaS~abatohu

12. ― -b2- [Golius explains this v. as meaning “ Firmiter religavit: ” or, as a trans. v. governing an accus., “ constringi jussit: ” as on the authority of the S, in which I do not find it in any sense.]

5 i. q. $ad~a AlEiSaAbapa [i. e. He bound the turban, or fillet, round his (own) head; a meaning well known, whence that explained in the next sentence: (see also 8:) and he bound a bandage of some kind round his (own) body, by reason of hunger: see muEaS~abN ]. (S, O, Msb, * K.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) He was made a chief; quasi-pass. of

2 [q. v.]. (L, TA.) ― -b3- And it has also another signification, from AlEaSabiy~ap ; (S, O;) [i. e.] it signifies also A^ataY biAlEaSabiy~api ; (K, TA;) which means [ He aided his people, or party, against hostile conduct: or he was angry, or zealous, for the sake of his party, and defended them: (see EaSabiY~N and EaSabiy~apN :) or] he invited, or summoned, others to the aid of his party, and to combine, or league, with them against those who acted towards them with hostility, whether they were wrongdoers or wronged. (TA.) And you say, taEaS~abuwA Ealayohimo They leagued, or collected themselves, together against them: and taEaS~abonaA lahu , and maEahu , We [ leagued together for him, and with him, and ] defended him. (TA.) [See also De Sacy's Chrest. Ar., see. ed., i. 445-6; where it i
573.] ― -b4- And tES~b biAl$~aYo'i He was, or became, content with the thing; as also ↓ . bihi . (K.)
7 i. q. Ai$otad~a [app. meaning, as seems to be indicated by the context (both before and after) in the S, It was, or became, hard, firm, or strong ]. (S, O, K.)

8 [ He attired himself, or surrounded his head, with the turban ], and biAlt~aAji [ with the crown ]. (S, O.) And AEtSb Alt~aAja EalaY raA^osihi He encircled his [own] head with the crown. (Az, TA.) ― -b2- AEtSb Aln~aAqapa : see 1, in the middle of the first quarter. ― -b3- AEtSbwA They became formed, or collected, into companies such as those whereof one is called EuSobap : (K:) or, into one of such companies. (M, L, TA.) [See also
12.] ― -b4- AEtSb bihi : see 5, last sentence.

12 The people, or party, collected themselves together: (TA:) or did so, and became companies such as are called EaSaAy^ib , (S, O, TA,) and became one of such companies: [see also 8; and see EuSobapN :] and in like manner, [ did so, and ] strove, or exerted themselves, in journeying, or pace. (TA.) And AESwSbt AlA_ibilu The camels strove, or exerted themselves, in journeying, or pace; as also ↓ : and collected themselves together; (K;) [and] so ↓ and ↓ : (Fr, S, O:) or collected themselves together so as to become one EiSaAbap , and strove, or exerted themselves, in journeying, or pace. (TA.) ― -b2- AESwSb is also said of a day, [app. in relation to heat,] meaning It was, or became, vehement, or severe: (S, O:) and of evil, meaning it was, or became, vehement, or severe, (K, TA,) and conc

: see EiSaAbapN , in two places. ― -b2- And see also EuSobN . ― -b3- Also A particular sort of the garments called buruwd , (S, A, Mgh, O, K,) of the fabric of El-Yemen; (S, Mgh, O;) a burod of which the yarn is dyed, and then woven; (Msb;) or of which the yarn is put together and bound, then dyed, and then woven; (A, Mgh, TA; *) not of the sort called buruwdu Alr~aqomi : (TA:) it has no pl., (Nh, Msb, TA,) nor dual: (Msb:) you say burodu EaSobK (Nh, Mgh, TA) and buruwdu EaSobK (Nh, Mgh, Msb, TA) and yurodaA EaSobK , (Msb,) and also yurodN EaSobN and buruwdN EaSobN , (Nh, TA,) and vawobN , EaSobN , (Msb,) and A^arodiyapu AlEaSobi ; (A, TA;) and sometimes they say EaSobN alone, the burod being known by this name: (TA:) or garments of the kind called buruwd , of the fabric of El-Yemen, the y

; or what are forbidden are the EaSob of El-Yemen, which are said to have been dyed with urine; so in the L &c.: (TA:) or, accord. to Sub, garments of the kind called buruwd of the fabric of El-Yemen; so called because they are dyed with EaSob , which grows only in El-Yemen; [he says that AlEaSobu is a certain dyed that does not grow but in El-Yemen; (Msb;)] but in this he opposes the generality of authorities; for they agree in stating that the garments in question are thus called from AlEaSobu , “ the act of binding, ” because the yarn is bound in order that the dye may not pervade the whole of the burod . (MF, TA.) ― -b4-

Hence, (assumed tropical:) Clouds like such as are termed laTox [q. v.]: (S, O:) or red clouds or mist (K, TA) seen in the western horizon (TA) in a time of drought, or sterility; as also ↓ , (K, TA,) pl. EaSaAy^ibu . (TA.) -A2- In a trad., mention occurs of a necklace made of EaSob : ElKhattábee says, if it do not mean the garments of El-Yemen, I know not what it is; yet I see not how a necklace can be made of these: Aboo-Moosà thinks it may be EaSab , meaning the tendons of joints, as they may have taken the tendons of certain clean animals, and cut them in pieces, and made them like beads, and, when dry, made neck laces of them; but he adds his having been told by some of the people of El-Yemen that EaSobN is the name of A certain beast of the sea, or of the great river, called also far

and ↓ and ↓ (K, TA) Certain trees that twine round other trees, having weak leaves; (TA;) the kind of tree called labolaAb [ dolichos lablab of Linn.]; (K;) said by Sh to be a kind of plant that twines round trees, i. q. labolaAbN : [coll. gen. ns.:] the ns. un. are EuSobapN and EaSobapN and EaSabapN : (TA:) accord. to Abu-lJarráh, (O, TA,) EaSobapN signifies a certain thing [app. meaning plant ] that twines about a qanaAdap [or tragacanth ], (O, K, TA,) thus, correctly, in many copies of the K, but in some fataAp , and in some qanaAp , both of which are wrong, though some assert the latter to be correct, (TA,) not to be pulled off from it but with an effort: (O, K, TA:) [see EiTofapN :] one says of a man strong in struggling for the mastery, qataAdapN luwiyato biEuSobapK (assumed tropical

[The sinews, or tendons; though the following explanation seems rather to denote the ligaments; ] the A^aTonaAb of the joints, (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) which connect and bind together the structure thereof, in man and in others, such as the ox-kind, and sheep or goats, and gazelles, and ostriches; so says AHn; (TA;) i. q. EaqabN : (S and K &c. in art. Eqb :) or such as are yellow of the ATnAb (Mgh, Msb) of the joints; the Eaqab being the white: (Mgh:) [it is also used as meaning ligaments: (see an ex. of its n. un. in an explanation of AlS~adafataAni , voce SadafN :) and sometimes it means nerves: (see a usage of its pl. voce SaroEN :) it is a coll. gen. n.:] the n. un. is with p : (S, O, TA:) and the pl. is A^aEoSaAbN . (S, Mgh, O, Msb.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The best (in a pl. sense)
Flesh, or flesh-meat, having many EaSab [i. e. sinews, or tendons ]. (TA.)
n. un. of EaSobN as syn. with EuSobN [q. v.]. (TA.)

; or thirsty: (S, TA:) or needing water: (Mgh:) or you say, A@loA=na ↓ [ He is thirsting, or thirsty, now ]; (Lh, K;) and huwa gadFA ↓ [ He will be thirsting, or thirsty, tomorrow ]; (Lh, O, K;) and baEoda ↓ h`*aA Alyawomi [ He will not be thirsting, or thirsty, after this day ]: (Lh, TA:) fem. [of the first] EaTi$apN (O, Msb, K) and [of the second] ↓ (TA) and [of the third] ↓ , (S, O, Msb, K,) which is also used as a pl., (S, K,) and ↓ : (Lth, O, K:) pl. masc. [of the first and third and fourth, and perhaps of the second also,] EiTaA$N (S, O, Msb, K) and EuTaA$N [which is irregular] and EaTi$uwna and [of the second] EaTu$uwna (TA) and [of the third] EaTaA$aY : (S, O, K:) pl. fem. EiTaA$N , like the masc., (S, O, K,) and [of the first] EaTi$aAtN , (Lth, O, K,) but this was ignored by Aboo-

; or desiring. (K.) You say, A_in~iY A_ilayoka ↓ (tropical:) [ Verily I am longing for seeing thee ]. (IAar, O.) ― -b3- makaAnN EaTi$N (S, O, Msb) and ↓ (S, O) A place in which is little water: (S, O, Msb:) or in which is no water. (Msb.) ― -b4- Alwi$aAHi ↓ (A) or EaTi$apu Alwi$aAHi (TA) (tropical:) [ Such a woman is slender in the waist
; or in the belly and flanks; like garovaY Alwi$aAHi ].
: fem. EaTo$aY and EaTo$aAnapN : see EaTi$N , throughout.

[ Insatiable thirst; ] a certain disease, (S, O, K, TA,) that attacks a man, (S, O, TA,) or a child, (TA,) the sufferer from which drinks water and cannot satisfy his thirst: (S, O, K, * TA:) or intense thirst: the sufferer thereof is permitted to break his fast. (TA.)
: dims. of EaTi$N , q. v. (ISk, O.)
