senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (O, K,) inf. n. EuTuwfN , (Mgh, Msb,) or EaTofN , (O, TA,) He, or it, (a man, S, O, or a thing, Msb,) inclined; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) or bent: (MF, TA:) and ↓ also has the former meaning, (Mgh, Msb, * TA,) as in the saying AnETf naHowahu i. e. he, or it, inclined towards him, or it; (TA;) [or the latter meaning;] or it became inclined, (Msb,) or became bent, (S, * O, Msb, K,) or both, (TA,) as quasi-pass. of EaTafahu ; (S, O, Msb, TA;) and ↓ likewise has both of these meanings, as quasi-pass. of ET~fhu , or [signifies it became much inclined and bent, for] ET~f is with teshdeed to denote muchness. (TA.) ― -b2-

Hence, (MF, TA,) EaTafa Ealayohi , (S, Mgh, MA, O, K,) [aor. as above,] inf. n. EaTofN ; (MA, MF, TA;) and Elyh ↓ ; (S, MA, O, K;) [and ↓ Elyh ;] (tropical:) He was, or became, favourably inclined towards him

; or affectionate, or kind, to him; (MA, PS;) he regarded him, or treated him, with mercy or pity or compassion; (MA, Mgh;) because in mercy, or pity, or compassion, is an inclining towards its object; (Mgh;) i. q. A^a$ofaqa Ealayohi ; (S, O, K;) and waSalahu , and bar~ahu . (TA in explanation of the second.) And EaTafato EalaY waladihaA , aor. as above, inf. n. EaTofN , said of a she camel, (assumed tropical:) She became favourably inclined, or compassionate, towards her young one, and yielded her milk; (Msb;) and Ealayohi ↓ [signifies the same, or she was made to incline to him, or to affect him ]. (M in art. rA^m , &c) ― -b3- EaTafa Ealayohi also signifies He turned, or returned, against him: (S:) or he charged, or made an assault or attack, upon him, [in battle,] and turned, or returne
; or disaffected, or unkind, to him

; or unmerciful, unpitying, or uncompassionate, to him ]. (MF, TA.) ― -b6- EuTuwfN and EaTofN [as intrans. inf. ns.] also signify A sheep's, or goat's, bending the neck, not by reason of an ailment. (TA.) ― -b7- And EaTofN [app. likewise as an intrans. inf. n.] also signifies The folding of the extremities of the skirt, of the facing, or outer side, upon, or against, the lining, or inner side. (TA.) -A2- EaTafahu , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) [aor. as above,] inf. n. EaTofN , (Mgh, Msb,) He inclined it; (Mgh, Msb, TA;) namely, a thing; (Msb, TA;) as also ↓ : (Mgh:) or he bent it, or doubled it, or folded it: (Msb:) or it signifies also he bent it: and ↓ likewise, inf. n. taEoTiyfN , has both of these meanings: (TA:) or this latter verb is with teshdeed to denote muchness [of the action], or multiplici

765.) And EaTafa Aln~aAqapa EalaY waladihaA (assumed tropical:) [ He made the she-camel to incline to, or affect, her young one ]. (M in art. rA^m ; &c.: see also liqaAHN muEaT~afapN in this art.) And tuEoTafu EalaY Albaw~i (assumed tropical:) [ She (a camel) is made to incline to, or affect, the stuffed skin of a young unweaned camel in order that she may yield her milk, when her young one has died]. (S, O, [See EaTuwfN .]) ― -b3- And EaTafotuhu Eano HaAjatihi (assumed tropical:) I turned him away, or back, from his object of want. (Msb.) ― -b4- And EaTofu Almudomaji i. e. AlqidoHi means The turning round about, or shuffling, of the gaming-arrow. (S voce mudomajN : see a verse there cited.)

2 see 1, latter half, in four places. -A2- EaT~afotuhu , vawobiY , inf. n. taEoTiyfN , I made my garment to be to him an EiTaAf , (O, K, TA,) i. e. a ridaA=' , [ by putting it ] upon his shoulders, as men do in the [season of] heat. (TA.)

5 see 1, former half, in three places. ― -b2- [ tET~f also signifies He (a man) affected a bending of his body; like tavan~aY , with which it is coupled in the S and O and K in art. gwj .] -A2- tET~f biAlEiTaAfi He clad himself (S, O, K *) with the EiTaAf (O) [i. e.] with the ridaA=' ; (S;) as also bihi ↓ . (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K. *) ― -b2-

Hence, in a trad., (TA,) in a prayer of the Prophet, (O,) suboHaAna mano taEaT~afa biAloEiz~i waqaAla bihi , (O, TA,) meaning (tropical:) [ I declare, or celebrate, or extol, the absolute perfection ] of Him who hath clad Himself with might as with a ridaA=' [ and (as expl. in the K in art. qwl and by Sgh) hath predominated thereby ]. (IAth, TA.)
6 means EaTafa baEoDuhumo EalaY baEoDK [i. e. (assumed tropical:) They were, or became, favourably inclined, one towards another

; or affectionate, or kind, one to another; &c.: see 1]. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- And tEATf fiY mi$oyatihi He (a man, Lth, O) shook, or moved about, his head, in his gait: (Lth, O, K:) or he inclined from side to side, therein: or he walked with an elegant and a proud and self-conceited gait. (O, * K.)
7 see 1, first quarter, in two places.
5. ― -b2- [Hence,] AEtTf Alqawosa He hung upon himself the bow, putting its suspensory belt or cord upon his neck or shoulder; (IAar, TA;) and so Als~ayofa the sword. (TA.)

10 , (O, K,) or AstETfhu Ealayohi , (S, [in which the meaning is indicated by the addition of faEaTafa ,]) signifies saA^alahu A^ano yaEoTifa Ealayohi [ He asked him to become favourably inclined towards him; to be affectionate, or kind, to him

; or to regard him, or treat him, with mercy or pity or compassion ]: (O, K:) [or he sought, or endeavoured, to conciliate to him his affection, or good will: ] or AisotaEoTafotuhu signifies saA^alotuhu A^ano yanoEaTifa [ I asked him to incline, or bend: but perhaps ynETf is a mistranscription for yaEoTifa ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- See also 1, latter half, in two places.

: see the next paragraph, last sentence, in two places. ― -b2- [It is used in grammar as meaning Adjunction to an antecedent: this is of two kinds; EaTofu AlbayaAni the explicative adjunction, as in jaA='a A^axuwka zayodN ; and EaTofu Aln~asaqi the ordinal adjunction, as in jaA='a zayodN waEamorNw : (in each of which instances the latter noun is termed ↓ ; and the former noun Ealayohi ↓ :) and hence, Harofu EaTofK , meaning a particle of adjunction
; or what we commonly call a conjunction; (as wa and vum~a , &c.;) also termed ↓ an adjunctive particle. ]

The side of a human being, from the head to the hip, or to the foot: (Mgh:) and the side of a thing: (Msb:) or the dual signifies the two sides of a man, from the part next the head to the hips: (S, O:) and the two sides of the neck of a man: (TA:) and the two sides of anything: (S, O, K:) as relating to a man, (TA,) or a thing. (Msb,) the pl. is A^aEoTaAfN , [properly a pl. of pane.,] (Msb, TA,) and, as relating to a man, EiTaAfN also, and EuTuwfN . (TA.) Hence the phrase, humo A^aloyanu EiTofFA [ They are more pliant, or pliable; properly as meaning flexible, supple, lithe, or limber; but app. here used tropically, as meaning compliant: compare lay~inu AljaAnibi ]. (Mgh.) And lay~inu AlA^aEoTaAfi [ Pliant, or pliable, &c.], applied to a horse: (En-Nadr, TA voce guwojN : [see also EaAjN ,

: see EaTafapN . -A2- Also Length of the edges of the eyelids, (O, K, TA,) and a bending [app. upwards ] thereof: (TA:) occurring in a trad.: or the word, as some relate it, is gaTafN [q. v.]; (O, TA;) which is of higher authority. (TA.)

[as an inf. n. un.] An inclining: hence, in a trad., kaA^an~a EaTofatahumo Hiyna samiEuwA SawotiY EaTofapu Albaqari EalaY A^awolaAdihaA [ As though their inclining, when they heard my voice, were the inclining of the cows (app. meaning wild cows) towards their young ones ]. (O, TA.) -A2- And A certain bead by means of which women captivate men; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ . (K.) -A3-

Also, (K,) or ↓ , for which EaTofap is used by poetic license, (ISh and O, [referring to a verse which will be found at the close of this paragraph, in which verse, however, it is certainly not used as applied to what here immediately follows,]) A tree to which the Habolap [i. e. grape-vine, or branch of a grapevine, ] clings; (ISh, O, K;) and so ↓ , (K,) or thus as written in the “ Book of Plants ” by AHn, who says that it is thus called because of its bending and twining upon trees: (O: [but this remark seems evidently to show that he means thereby one of the plants mentioned below voce EiTofapN or voce EaTafapN , or perhaps what here follows:]) IB says that the EaTofap is the labolaAb [ dolichos lablab of Linn.]; so called because of its twining upon trees: (TA:) [and this, or what will

: see EaTofapN , in two places. ― -b2- Also The extremities [or tendrils ] of the vine, that hang therefrom. (K.) ― -b3- And The tree [or plant ] called EuSobap [n. un. of EuSobN , q. v., said by some to signify the layolaAb , mentioned in the next preceding paragraph]. (K.)

A certain plant which twines upon trees and has no leaves nor branches, fed upon by the oxen [app. meaning the wild oxen,] (K, TA,) but injurious to them: (TA:) some of its Euruwq [app. here meaning root-like stalks] are taken, and twisted, and charmed [by some invocation or otherwise], and cast upon the woman that hates her husband, and she consequently loves him: (K, TA:) so they assert: (TA:) accord. to AA, ↓ signifies one of the strange kinds of trees of the desert: (O, TA:) EaTafapN is the n. un. thereof. (TA.) See also EaTofapN .
: see maEoTuwfN .

[as an epithet applied to a $aAp , i. e. sheep or goat,] Having the horn twisted; like EaqoSaA='u : occurring in a trad. relating to the poor-rate. (TA. [The masc., A^aEoTafu , I do not find mentioned.])

and ↓ [ A garment of either of the kinds called ] a ridaA=' (S, O, K) and a TayolasaAn , and any garment that is worn like as is the ridaA=' , (TA,) and the former also signifies an A_izaAr : (K:) the two words are like A_izaArN and miy^ozarN , &c.: and the rdA=' is said to be called ETAf because it falls against the two sides of the man's neck, which are termed his EiTofaAni : the pl. [of pauc.] of EiTaAfN is A^aEoTifapN and [of mult.] EuTufN and EuTuwfN ; (TA;) and EuTofN [also] is a pl. of EiTaAfN as meaning an A_izaAr : (K, TA:) the pl. of ↓ is maEaATifu ; but As says that he had not heard any sing. of this pl. (O, TA.) ― -b2-

Hence, (S, O, TA,) EiTaAfN signifies also A sword; (S, O, K, TA;) because the Arabs called it [in like manner] ridaA='N [q. v.]; (TA;) and so ↓ . (K.) ― -b3- And one says, Als~ayofu EiTaAfiY waA_ibaATiY , meaning I put, or place, the sword upon my side, and beneath my armpit. (TA in art. AbT .)

, applied to a bow: see muEaT~afapN . ― -b2- Applied to a gaming-arrow, (O, K,) of those used in the game called Almayosir , (O,) as also ↓ , That inclines towards, or upon, the other arrows [ in the receptacle called the ribaAbap ], and comes forth winning, or before the others: [app. because it is the first upon which the hand falls:] (O, K:) an ex. of the former occurs in a verse of Sakhr-el-Gheí cited in art. xD : (O, TA:) [in the TA, in art. xwD , it is expl. as meaning, in that verse, a borrowed arrow, in the luck of which one has confidence:] or the former, accord. to El-Kutabee, (O,) or each, (K,) signifies the arrow to which is assigned no fine and no gain; (O, K;) it is one of the three A^agofaAl ; and is called ETwf because it returns into every ribaAbap with which one plays; an

; or to be affectionate, or kind; and to show mercy or pity or compassion. (O.) (assumed tropical:) A bestower of favour, or bounty; good in disposition; as also ↓ ; (TA;) of both of which EuTofN is pl.; (K, TA;) and ↓ also has this meaning, applied to a man: (Lth, TA:) and also this last, and EaTuwfN , (assumed tropical:) a man who protects, or defends, those who are defeated, or put to flight. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) A woman loving to her husband, affectionate to her child or children. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) A she-camel that is made to incline to, or affect, (S, O,) or that inclines to, or affects, (so in the copies of the K,) the stuffed skin of a young unweaned camel, [when her young one has died,] and that keeps, or cleaves, to it: (S, O, K:) pl. EuTufN . (TA. [See 1, nea

Also, and ↓ , A miSoyadap [or snare, trap, gin, or net ], (O, K, TA,) so called because (O, TA) having in it a piece of wood that bends, or inclines, (O, K, TA,) in its head: (TA:) also called gaATuwfN . (TA in art. gTf .)
(assumed tropical:) A woman having no pride; gentle; very submissive or obedient. (AZ, O, K.)
: see munoEaTafN : ― -b2- and see what here follows.
and ↓ A bow: pl. EaTaAy^ifu . (TA.)
: see EaTuwfN , in three places. ― -b2- AlEaT~aAfuwna is like AlEak~aAruwna , meaning (assumed tropical:) They who return to the fight [after fleeing, or wheeling away]. (TA in art. Ekr .)

A she-gazelle ( ZaboyapN ) inclining, or bending, her neck when she lies down on her breast. (S, O, K.) And EaATifapN A sheep or goat ( $aAp ) bending its neck, not by reason of an ailment. (TA.) ― -b2- See also EaTuwfN , latter half. ― -b3- And see the explanations of the verse of Aboo-Wejzeh Es-Saadee cited in art. Hyn . ― -b4- AlEaATifu is applied to The sixth [ in arriving at the goal ] of the horses that are started together for a race; (MA, TA, and Ham p. 46;) related as on the authority of El-Muärrij; but Az did not find that those who related this as from him were trustworthy persons, though he was himself trustworthy: (TA:) or the fourth thereof. (Har p.
270.) ― -b5- See also EaTofN .

[(assumed tropical:) A bias, or cause of inclining: pl. EawaATifu ]. One says, maA yavoniyniY Ealayoka EaATifapN mino raHimK and qaraAbapK [(assumed tropical:) A bias of relationship does not incline me towards thee
; or no bias of relationship inclines me towards thee ]. (S, O, TA.) ― -b2- [And hence, as being a cause of inclining,] AlEaATifapu signifies [also] Relationship [itself]

; or the tie, or ties, thereof; syn. Alr~aHimu : and epithet in which the quality of a substantive predominates. (TA.) ― -b3- [And] (assumed tropical:) Affection, or kindness; mercy, pity, or compassion. (MA.)
: see EaTuwfN , last sentence.

; and its pl. maEaATifu : see munoEaTafN . [ A place of inclining, or bending, of the body; whence,] saholu AlmaEoTifi and AlmaEaATifi : see EiTofN : [and a place of flexure, or creasing, of the skin; whence it is said that the pl.] maEaATifu signifies the places, of the body, that sweat. (TA in art. ErD .) [And A place of doubling, or folding
; or a duplicature, or fold, of a garment, or piece of cloth.]
: see EiTaAfN , in three places.

, applied to bows ( qisiY~N ), is with teshdeed to denote muchness or multiplicity; (S, O, K, TA;) [so that it may signify either Much bent, or, as applied to a number of bows, simply bent: but it is said that] the meaning is, having one of the curved extremities bent towards the other; and so applied to a single bow ( qawosN ); as also ↓ . (TA.) ― -b2- And in like manner applied to milch camels ( liqaAHN ); [meaning (tropical:) Made to incline to, or affect, a young one: for] sometimes, or often, they made a number of she-camels to incline to, or affect, a single young one, ( Eid~apa *awodK ↓ EalaY faSiylK waAHidK ,) and drew their milk while they were in the condition of doing thus, in order that they might yield it copiously. (S, O, K, TA.)

[ Inclined, or bent: &c.]. ― -b2- qawosN maEoTuwfapN An Arabian bow, (IDrd, S, O, K, *) of which the curved extremity is much bent towards it, and which is used for [ shooting at ] the butts: (IDrd, O, K:) and ↓ signifies the same. (TA.) ― -b3- See also EaTofN , in two places.

A place of inclining, or bending; (S, O, Msb, K;) [as also ↓ , pl. maEaATifu ;] and so ↓ : (TA:) you say munoEaTafu AlwaAdiY the place of inclining, or bending, of the valley: (S, O, Msb, K:) and AlA^awodiyapi ↓ [ the places of inclining, or bending, of the valleys ]. (K voce kusuwrN .)

senses.text: 1 , [in my copy of the Msb said to be of the class of qtl , perhaps a mistranscription for qabila , but see what is said below of EaTala as syn. with baTala , from which it may be inferred that EaTalato is correct in the sense here following as well as EaTilato ,] said of a woman, [aor. ,] inf. n. EaTalN (S, O, K) and EuTuwlN ; (O, K;) and ↓ ; (S, O, K;) She had not upon her any women's ornaments; (K, TA;) and wore not any ornature, or decoration: (TA:) or her neck was destitute of necklaces or the like; (S, O;) as also ↓ : (Har p. 268:) accord. to Er-Rághib, AlEaTalu signifies the being destitute of ornature, or decoration. (TA.) ― -b2- And sometimes AlEaTalu is used [for AlEaTalu mino $aYo'i ] as meaning The being destitute of a thing; though primarily relating to women's ornaments. (S,

5.]) And ETlt AlA_ibilu The camels were without a pastor to tend them. (Msb. [The context there app. indicates that the verb in this case, likewise, is with fet-h to the T ; but I believe it to be more correctly EaTilat .]) ― -b4- And EaTila , (O, K,) with kesr [to the T ], (O,) [i. e.] like fariHa , (K,) signifies also He was, or became, large in the body. (O, K.)

2 and ↓ signify the same [app. in all the senses assigned to the former]. (O.) ― -b2- 'Áïsheh is related, in a trad., to have said respecting a woman who had died, EaT~iluwhaA , meaning Divest ye her of her ornaments. (S, O.) ― -b3- [Hence,] ET~l Alqawosa , inf. n. taEoTiylN , He divested the bow of its string. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence likewise, the inf. n.] Alt~aEoTiylu signifies [also] The rendering vacant, void, or unoccupied, (K, TA,) a place of abode, and the like. (TA.) And The leaving a thing untended, unminded, or neglected. (K, TA. [ DiyAEFA in the CK is a mistake for DayaAEFA .]) One says of the frontier of a hostile country, EuT~ila , meaning It was left without any to defend it. (TA.) And of subjects one says, EuT~iluwA , meaning They were left without any one to govern them. (TA.)

; or unemployed ]. (S, O, K.) One says, EaT~alotu AlA^ajiyra I made the hired man to be unoccupied. (Msb.) And ET~l Alxayola mina Algazowi (S and K in art. bhw ) [ He freed the horses from service in warfare; ] he did not go to war upon the horses. (TA in that art.) ― -b6- [Also The assertion of the tenet, or tenets, of the muEaT~il , q. v.] ― -b7- And taEoTiylu AlHuduwdi means The not inflicting the [ punishments termed ] Hdwd upon him to whom they are due. (TA.)
4 see 2, first sentence.

(See gu$iYa Ealayohi .)] ― -b3- taEaT~alato mina AlAisotiqaA='i bihaA is said of a dalow [or leathern bucket, meaning It was exempted from, i. e. unused for, the drawing of water therewith ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And tET~l is said of a tent [as meaning It became vacant ]. (TA in art. bhw .)
10 see 1, first sentence.

4 in arts. EDl and EZl .
: see EuTulN , last sentence.

(S, O, K.) -A2- Also The denuded, or unclad, part, or parts, of the body; syn. jurodapN : so in the saying AimoraA^apN Hasanapu AlEaTali [ A woman beautiful in respect of the denuded, or unclad, part, or parts, of the body ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And The body, or person; syn. $axoSN ; (S, O, K, TA;) particularly, as some say, of a human being; (TA;) like TalalN : (S, O, TA:) pl. A^aEoTaAlN . (K.) And one says, maA A^aHosana EaTalahu , meaning [ How beautiful is ] his tallness, or justness of stature, and his perfectness [ of make ]! (S, O.) ― -b3- And The neck. (K.) ― -b4- And Beauty of body. (TA.) -A3- Also A stalk of a raceme of a palmtree; (S, O;) as also ↓ , accord. to IDrd: (O:) or the former, (TA,) and ↓ the latter, accord. to IDrd, and accord. to Az, who says that he heard it fro

(Mgh.) [All primarily denote proximate sequence.] You say, EaqabuwnaA and EaqabuwA mino xalofinaA They cam

; or it may perhaps be from the former verb, like taholikapN from halaka ; for] one says, baAEaniY siloEapF waEalayohi taEoqibapN A_ino kaAnat fiyhaA [ He sold me an article of merchandise, and was responsible for an evil consequence, (or for damage afterwards found in it,) should there be any in it ]. (ISh, O, TA. *) ― -b10- Eaqabahu and ↓ and ↓ signify also He took, or received, from him something in exchange, an exchange, a substitute, or an equivalent, for another thing: it is said in a trad., A_ino lamo yaqoruwhu falahu A^ano yaEoqubahumo bimivoli qiraAhu If they entertain him not. he shall have a right to take from them as a substitute the like of his entertainment which they denied him: and one says also minohu xayorFA ↓ , or $ar~FA , He took, or received, from him in exchange good,

4.]) -A4- [The inf. n.] AlEaqobu also signifies Alr~ajoEu , [which generally means The making, or causing, to return, or go back; but this may perhaps be a mistake for Alr~ujuwEu , for it is immediately added,] Dhu-rRummeh says, kaA^an~a SiyaAHa Alkudori yanoZurona EaqobanaA taraATunu A^anobasATK Ealayohi TagaAmi meaning [ As though the crying of the dusky she-camels] looking, or waiting, for our returning from watering that they might go to the water after us [ were the barbarous talk of low, or ignoble, Nabathæans, over it, i. e. over the water]. (TA.) -A5- Eaqiba Aln~abotu , [aor. ,] inf. n. EaqabN , The branches of the plant, or herbage, became slender, and the leaves thereof turned yellow. (IAar, TA. [See also

2 see 1, first three quarters, in seven places. ― -b2- The inf. n., taEoqiybN , signifies also The doing a thing and then returning to doing it: (IAth, TA:) the performing an act of prayer, or another act, and then returning to doing it in the same day: (Sh, TA:) and [particularly] the making a warring, or warring and plundering, expedition, and then another in the same year. (S, O, K.) [See also muEaq~ibN .] You say, Eq~b biSalaApK baEoda SalaApK , and bigazaApK baEoda gazaApK , He followed up one prayer with another, and one warring, or warring and plundering, expedition with another. (TA.) And Sal~aY mina All~ayoli vum~a Eaq~aba He prayed in the night and then repeated the prayer. (IAar, TA.) And Euq~iba AlgaAziyapu biA^amovaAlihaA , and ↓ , The warring, or warring and plundering, party

; or remaining in one's place in prayer waiting for another prayer. (TA.) And you say, Eq~b fiY AlS~alaApi , (S, O,) inf. n. as above, (S, A, O, Msb, K,) He sat after the performing of the [ordinary] prayer for the purpose of a supplication (S, A, O, Msb, K) or a petition. (S, O, Msb.) wal~aY mudobirFA walamo yuEaq~ibo , in the Kur [xxvii.

10 and xxviii. 31], means [ He did did not turn back retreating ] and did not wait; (O, TA;) properly, did not make advancing to follow his retreating: (O:) or and did not turn aside (S, Msb) nor wait in expectation: (S:) or and did not turn aside nor return: (O:) or and did not look aside: (K, * TA.) or and did not return; from Eq~b said of a combatant, meaning He returned after fleeing: (Bd in xxvii. 10:) you say, Eq~b Ealayohi He returned against him; syn. kar~a , and rajaEa : and taEoqiybN signifies also The turning back, or receding, from a thing that one had desired to do. (TA.) ― -b5- Eaq~aba fiY Al$~ayobi biA^axolaAqK HasanapK [app. means He had latterly, in the time of hoariness, good dispositions ]. (O. [The meaning that I have assigned to this phrase seems to be there indicated

5.]) ― -b10- And Eq~b fiY AlA^amori He went repeatedly to and fro, or made repeated efforts, in seeking to accomplish the affair, striving, or exerting himself. (S, O, L, TA.) Euqobapu AlA^jiyri means The hired-man's turn to ride; when the hirer dismounts, for example in the morning, and he ( the former ) rides. (Mgh.) And [the pl.] EuqabN means [particularly] The turns of camels, when they are being watered: the watering of a num

; or thing that is given, or taken, in exchange for another thing; (S, O, L, K;) as also ↓ . (L, TA.) One says, A^axa*otu mino A^asiyriY EuqobapF I took, or received, for my captive, a substitute, or something in exchange. (S, O.) And ↓ occurs in a trad., meaning I will give thee something in exchange [ for her, i. e.] for sparing her life, and liberating her. (L, TA.) ― -b10- And Pasture, or food, of an ostrich, that is eaten after other pasture or food: [and likewise of camels: and of men:] pl. as above. (AA, S, O.) One says of camels, raEato EuqobatahaA i. e. They pastured upon the [ kind of plants termed ] HamoD after the [ kind termed ] xul~ap ; (A, L;) or upon the xul~ap after the HamoD : (L:) and of men one says, A^akaluwA Euqobatahumo They ate their repast of sweetmeat after the ot

663. [But the origin of this I know not.]) ― -b13- One says also, laqiytu minohu Euqobapa AlS~unoEi , meaning I experienced from him, or it, difficulty: [as though lit. signifying, the result of the deed that I had done:] and [simply] laqiYa minohu EuqobapF He experienced from him, or it, difficulty. (TA. [But in a copy of the A, and in my opinion correctly, the last word in this phrase is written ↓ : see EaqabapN , below.]) ― -b14- And kunotu mar~apF nu$obap waA^anaA Alyawoma Euqobap , expl. by IAar as meaning I was such that, when I clung to a man, he experienced evil from me; but now I have reverted from being such, through weakness. (TA. [It is a prov., somewhat differently related in art. n$b , q. v.]) ― -b15- See also the next paragraph, in four places.

(Lh, S, O, K) and ↓ , (Lh, O, K,) but the former is the more approved, (Lh, TA,) and Eqb , (so in the TA, [app., if not a mistranscription, ↓ ,]) A mark, sign, trace, impress, characteristic, or outward indication. (Lh, S, O, K.) One says, Ealayohi Eiqobapu Als~arowi , (S, O,) and ↓ , (O,) and AljamaAli , (S, O,) i. e. Upon him is the mark &c. [ of generosity and manliness, and of beauty ]. (S, O, K.) ― -b2- Eiqobapu Alqamari and ↓ Alqmr mean The return of the moon, when it has set, or disappeared, and then risen: (L:) [or the return of the moon after the change; for] one says, maA yafoEalu *`lika A_il~aA Eiqobapa Alqamari , (S,) or ↓ Alqmr , (so in the O,) meaning He does not that save once in each month: (S, O:) but, accord. to IAar, Alqamari ↓ , with damm, is a certain star, or asterism

[ A mountain-road; ] a road in [or upon ] a mountain: (Bd in xc. 11:) or a road in the upper part of a mountain: (Ham p. 287:) or a difficult place of ascent of the mountains: (K:) or it is in a mountain and the like thereof: (Msb:) or [it sometimes signifies] a long mountain that lies across the way, and over which the way therefore leads; long, or high, and very difficult; so called, too, when it is further impassable after it is ascended; rising high towards the sky, ascending and descending; most difficult of ascent; but sometimes its height is one [or uniform ]; and its acclivity is in appearance like a wall: (TA:) [generally it means a road over, or up, or down, or over some part of, a mountain: ] pl. EiqaAbN . (S, O, Msb, K.) AiqotaHama AlEaqabapa [properly signifying He attempted t
11.) See also EuqobapN , near the end. ― -b2- It is also n. un. of EaqabN [q. v.]. (S, O.)

: see EaqibN , second quarter, in four places. ― -b2- It occurs in a trad. respecting the prayer of fear; in which it is said of that prayer, kaAnato EuqobaY [ It was an affair of turns ]; meaning that it was performed by one company after another; several companies performing it successively, by turns. (TA. [Compare EuqobapN as expl. in the third sentence of the paragraph on that word.]) ― -b3- Also i. q. mrjE [app. marojiEN i. e. A returning, &c.]. (TA.) ― -b4- And The requital, or recompence, of an affair, or action. (S, O, K.) ― -b5- See also EuqobapN , latter half, in two places.
i. q. EuqomiY~u AlkalaAmi , [the b being app. a substitute for m ,] i. e. Obscure speech or language, which men do not know. (TA in art. Eqm .)
: see EaqibN , in four places.
: see EaqibN , in two places.
A rough, coarse, or rude, man; syn. galiyZN : pl. EqbAn [so in the TA, either EiqobaAnN or EuqobaAnN ]: mentioned by Kr: but Az doubted its correctness. (TA.)

[The eagle; ] a certain bird, (S, O, K,) of those that prey, (Msb,) well known: (K:) of the fem. gender: (S, O, Msb:) [though] applied to the male and the female; but with this distinction, that you say of the male, h`*aA EuqaAbN *akarN [ This is a male eagle ]: or it is only female; and a bird of another kind couples with it; whence Ibn-'Oneyn says, satirizing a person named Ibn-Seyyideh, Say thou to Ibn-Seyyideh, maA A^anota A_il~aA kaA@loEuqaAbi faA^um~uhu maEoruwfapN walahu A^abN majohuwlu [“ Thou art not other than the like of the eagle; ” for his mother is known, but he has a father unknown ]: (MF, TA:) the pl. (of pauc., S, O) is A^aEoqubN , (S, O, K,) because it is of the fem. gender and the measure A^afoEulN specially belongs to pls. of fem. nouns [though not to such exclusively],
: see EaqibN , last quarter. -A2- It is also pl. of EaqabapN [q. v.]. (S, &c.) -A3- See also A^aEoqaAbN .
: see EaAqibN , near the end.

Anything that is a sequent, of, or to, another thing; [ in an absolute sense, ] (S, Msb, TA,) as when you say, Als~alaAmu EaqiybN lilt~a$ah~udi [ The salutation is a sequent to the t$h~d (q. v.)], and AlEid~apu EaqiybN lilT~alaAqi [ The Eid~ap (q. v.) is a sequent to divorcement ], i. e., one follows the other; (Msb;) and [ by alternation, ] as when one says of the night and the day, kul~u waAHidK minohumaA Eaqiybu SaAHibihi [ Each of them is the alternating sequent of its correlative ]: (Az, Msb, TA:) you say of the night and the day, humaA EaqiybaAni [ They are two alternating sequents ]; and Eaqiybuka signifies He who does a deed, or work, with thee by turn, he doing it one time and thou another: (A, * TA:) and ↓ signifies the same, (S, Msb,) as also [↓ and ↓ and] ↓ . (Msb.) As for the

Punishment; (S, * MA, Msb, * KL;) i. q. nakaAlN . (MA.) ― -b2- And Detention, confinement, or imprisonment: so in the trad., laY~u AlwaAjidi yuHil~u Euquwbatahu waEaroDahu i. e. [ The solvent man's putting off the payment of his debt with promises repeated time after time renders allowable ] the imprisoning of him and the accusing of him. (IAar, TA. [Accord. to one relation, mentioned in the TA in art. ErD , this trad. ends with waEiroDahu , there said to mean wanafosahu .])

, with teshdeed of the Y , (O,) or Euq~ayobN , like qub~ayoTN , (K,) A certain bird, (O, K,) well known. (O.) [If the name be correctly as in the O, the bird meant is probably an eaglet, or a small species of eagle. ]

, and EabanoqaApN , and baEonaqaApN , (S, O, K,) and qaEonabaApN , (O,) and EabanoqaA='u , (K in art Ebq ,) the vars. of the first being formed by transposition, (O,) An EuqaAb [or eagle ] having sharp talons: (S, O, K:) or having abominable, or hideous, talons: (T, TA:) or quick in seizing, and abominable, or hideous: accord. to IAar, the epithet denotes intensiveness of quality, as in the cases of A^asadN A^asidN and kalobN kalibN : accord. to Lth, EaqonobaApN applied to an EuqaAb signifies cunning: and the pl. is EaqanobayaAtN . (TA.) [See also art. Ebq .]

[act. part. n. of Eaqaba ;] Coming after [&c.]. (Msb.) EaAqibu $aYo'K means Any person [or thing ] that comes after, or succeeds, or comes in the place of, a thing. (S, O, TA.) AlEaAqibu is an appellation applied to the Prophet (S, O, Msb) by himself (S, O) because he came after other prophets, (Msb,) meaning The last of the prophets, (S, O.) And EaAqibN liA@moraA^apK means One who is the last of the husbands of a woman. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] EaAqibapN mino TayorK Birds succeeding one another, this alighting and flying, and then another alighting in the place where the former alighted. (TA.) And A_ibilN EaAqibapN Camels that betake themselves to plentiful pasture where they feed freely, after eating of the [ kind of plants called ] HamoD : [or] they are not so called unless they be camels
a quasi-inf. n.: see 1, first quarter. ― -b2- See also EaqibN , in four places.

pl. of EaqibN [q. v.]. (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- And [hence] Streaks, one behind another; as streaks of fat so disposed. (TA.) ― -b3- And Pottery [or potsherds ] put between the bricks in the casing of a well, in order that it may become strong; said by Kr to have no sing.: (TA:) [or,] accord. to IAar, ↓ , i. e. like kitaAbN , (TA,) or ↓ , (thus written in the O,) signifies pottery [or potsherds ] between the rows, or courses, of bricks, (O, * TA,) in the casing of a well. (O.) [IAar cites an ex., in a verse, in which AEqAb would not be admissible.] And A^aEoqaAbu AlT~aY~i signifies What surround the casing of a well; i. e. what are behind it. (TA. [See 4, latter half.])
[ a modern word signifying A catchword at the bottom of a page: pl. taEaAqiybu .]

[appears, from what here follows, to be used for muEoqabN HaAluhu i. e. One whose state is changed ]. IAar cites as an ex. of this word, kul~u HaY~K muEoqabN EuqabaA meaning [ Every living being ] comes to a state different from that in which he was [ by turns, or time after time ]. (TA.)

[accord. to the O, miEoqabN , but this I think a mistranscription,] A star that succeeds, i. e. rises after, another star, (S, K, TA,) and on the rising of which, he who rides in his turn, after another, mounts the beast: (TA:) a star at the appearance of which two persons who ride by turns during a journey take each the other's place; when one star sets and another rises, he who was walking mounts the beast. (AO.) See EaqiybN . -A2- See also 4, latter half; where an ex. occurs in a verse.

He who is brought up for the office of Khaleefeh after the [ actual ] Imám [or Khaleefeh ]. (O, K.) ― -b2- And A skilful driver. (O, K.) ― -b3- And A camel that is ridden by different persons in turns. (O, * TA.) ― -b4- And A woman's ximaAr [i. e. muffler, or head-covering ]; (IAar, O, * K, TA;) so called because it takes the place of the mulaA='ap . (O, TA.) ― -b5- And An ear-drop; syn. quroTN . (O, K.)

One who is made to go forth, (so in the CK,) or who goes forth, (O, and so in my MS. copy of the K,) from the shop of the vintner when a greater man than he enters. (O, K.) ― -b2- jaA='a muEaq~abFA He came at the end, or close, of the day. (TA.) ― -b3- qidoHN muEaq~abN An arrow which [ in the game called Almayosir ] is returned into the ribaAbap [q. v.] time after time; the prize allotted to which is hoped for. (TA.) ― -b4- jazuwrN saHuwfu AlmuEaq~abi A fat slaughtered camel. (TA.) ― -b5- naEolN muEaq~abapN A sandal having an Eaqib [q. v.]. (O, TA.)

Coming after, or near after, another thing. (O.) See EaqiybN . ― -b2- It is said that it is applied as an epithet to an angel; that one says malaka muEaq~ibN [meaning An angel that follows another ]; and malaAy^ikapN muEaq~ibapN ; and that muEaq~ibaAtN is a pl. pl. (O.) AlmuEaq~ibaAtu means The angels of the night and the day; (S, O, K;) because they succeed one another by turns; and the fem. form is used because of the frequency of their doing so, in like manner as it is in the words nas~aAbapN and Eal~aAmapN : (S, O:) the angles called AlHafaZapu [pl. of HaAfiZN , q. v.]: so in the Kur xiii. 12: in which some of the Arabs of the desert read maEaAqiybu : (TA:) this [may be an anomalous pl. of EaqiybN , like as mahaAjiynu is of hajiynN , or it] is pl. of muEaq~ibN or of muEaq~ibapN , the Y
A woman who usually brings forth a male after a female. (S, O, K.) -A2- And A chamber ( bayot ) in which raisins are put. (K.)

: see EuqiybN , with which it is syn. ― -b2- [Hence,] A_ibilN muEaAqibapN Camels that eat one time, or turn, of the [ kind of plants called ] HamoD , and another of the [ kind called ] xul~ap . (S, O, K.) ― -b3- And naxolapN muEaAqibapN A palm-tree that bears fruit one year, and fails to do so another. (TA.) ― -b4- And muEaAqibN also signifies A revenger of blood: a poet, cited by IAar, says, wanaHonu qatalonaA biAlmaHaAriqi faArisFA jazaA='a AlEuTaAsi laA yamuwtu AlmuEaAqibu meaning [ And we slew, in El-Mahárik, (app. the name of a place,) a horseman, ] taking our bloodrevenge quickly, in the time that elapses between a sneeze and the prayer for the sneezer [which is usually “ God have mercy on thee ”]: the memory of the blood-revenger shall not die. (TA. [It is there also said that AlEqb

, perfectly decl., because it is an Arabic word, not altered, and, although having an augmentative letter at the beginning, not of the measure of a verb; whereas yEqwb as a proper name of foreign origin is imperfectly decl.; (S, O;) The Hajal [or partridge ]: (K:) or the male of the Hajal ; (S, O, Msb;) or of the qaboj ; (Lh, Mgh;) but ISd says, I know not whether Lh mean by this the Hajal or the qaTaA or the karawaAn , nor do I know that the qaboH is the same as the Hajal : (TA:) and the male of the qaTaA [or sand-grouse ]: (TA:) pl. yaEaAqiybu . (S, Mgh, O, Msb.) kaA^an~akumo yaEaAqiybu AlHajali , occurring in a trad., means [ As though ye were the males of partridges ] in your haste, and your flying into destruction: for they are such that, when they see the female in the possession of

[a coll. gen. n., n. un. yaEoquwbiY~N ,] the name of A sect of the xawaArij , followers of Yaakoob Ibn-'Alee El-Koofee. (TA.) ― -b2- And A sect of the Christians; the followers of Yaakoob ElBarádi'ee [or Jacobus Baradæus ], who assert the unity of the divine and human natures [ in the person of Christ ], and who are the most unbelieving and stubborn of the Christians: so says El-Mak- reezee, in one of his tracts. EaqodN (Mgh, L, Msb) and taEoqaAdN [of which see an ex. in a verse cited voce ratamN , and which is properly an intensive or a frequentative form]; and ↓ [which is also intensive or frequentative, inf. n. taEoqiydN ]; and ↓ ; (L;) He tied the cord, or rope; knit it; complicated it so as to form a knot or knots; tied it in a knot or knots; tied it firmly, fast, or strongly; contr. of Hal~ahu ; (L;) syn. $ad~ahu : (K:) the etymologists assert that the primary signification of EaqodN is the contr. of Hal~N : that it was afterwards used in relation to sales, or bargains, contracts, &c.: and then, in relation to a firm determination of the mind. 8. ― -b3- Eaqadato bi*anabihaA , said of a she-camel, (S, O, L,) She twisted her tail, as though tying it in a knot: (L:) this she does to make it known that she has conceived. (S, O, L.) ― -b4- Eaqada liHoyatahu He dressed his beard so as to make it knotted, and crisp, or curly: this they used to do in wars, and their doing so was forbidden by the Prophet: (O, L:) they did it from a motive of pride and self-conceit. And in like manner tEq~d is said of a collection of clouds ( saHaAb ). (L.) ― -b3- Said of an animal's tail, It became twisted [ as though tied in a knot ]. (L.) ― -b4- And said of hair, It became knotted, and crisp, or curly. 1 in the latter half. ― -b3- AEtqd ka*aA , (Msb,) or AEtqd ka*aA biqalobihi , (S, O,) He settled, or determined, his heart, or mind, firmly upon such a thing

; or he held, adhered, or clave, to such a thing with the heart, or mind; i. q. Ealayohi ↓ Alqaloba waAlD~amiyra ; (Msb;) [ he believed, or believed firmly, or was firmly persuaded of, such a thing: this is its most usual meaning;] he was, or became, certain, or sure, of such a thing. (PS.) [It is mostly used in relation to matters of religion, to religious dogmas and the like.] See also EaqiydapN . ― -b4- AEtqd also signifies He acquired, (S, Mgh, O, L, K,) or bought, (A,) an estate consisting of land, or of land and a house, &c., (S, A, O, L, K,) or other property: (S, A, Mgh, O, L, K:) he collected property. (Mgh, * Msb.)

Also, [without any objective complement expressed,] He bought what is termed Euqodap , i. e. an estate, or a property, consisting in land or houses. (L.) ― -b5- And AEtqd A^axFA fiY A@ll~`hi He adopted a brother in God. (A.) ― -b6- AEtqd Ald~ur~a , and Alxaraza , He made the pearls, and the beads, into a necklace; and in like manner, other things. (L.) -A2- AEtqd said of a date-stone, (A,) or other thing, (S, O, L,) [as also ↓ , which frequently occurs in the lexicons &c. in the sense here following,] It became hard. EuquwdN . (O, L.) Agreeably with this explanation, the pl. is used in the Kur v. 1, as meaning Contracts, &c.: or it there means the obligatory statutes, or ordinances, of God: or, accord. to Zj, the covenants imposed by God, and those imposed mutually by men agreeably with the requirements of religion. [as an inf. n.: see 1, last four sentences. ― -b2- Also] A twisting in the tail of a sheep or goat, as though it were knotted, or tied in a knot. (L.) So in the saying of Imra-el-Keys, wayawoma Eaqarotu liloEa*aAraY maTiy~atiY [ And the day when I slaughtered for the virgins my riding-camel ]. (TA.) And so in the trad. laA Eaqora fiY AlA_isolaAmi [ There shall be no slaughtering of camels at the grave in the time of El-Islám ]: for they used to slaughter camels at the graves of the dead, saying, The occupant of the grave used to slaughter camels for guests in the days of his life; so we recompense him by doing the like after his death. (IAth, TA.) ― -b4- Hence also, He slew him; he destroyed him: of this signification we have an ex. in the story of Umm-Zara: waEaqora jaAratihaA And [a cause of] the destruction of her fellow-wife through [the latter's]

; or, as some say, the Y is to mark a pause; (Mgh;) and EaqorFA HaloqFA , (O, K,) which are also inf. ns.; (TA;) and this is accord. to the usage of the Arabs; (Az, TA;) being a form of imprecation, though not meant to express a desire for its having effect, (Az, Msb, TA,) for what is meant by it is only blame; (Msb;) expl. by waEaqarahaA A@ll~`hu taEaAlaY waHalaqahaA , (K,) i. e., [ May God ( exalted be He ) wound her, &c., and ] shave her hair, or afflict her with a pain in her throat: (TA:) or may her body be wounded ( Euqira ), and may she be afflicted with a disease in her throat: (Mgh, O: *) so accord. to A'Obeyd: or may her leg and her throat be cut: or may her leg be cut and her head shaven: (Mgh:) [or may she be destroyed, and may her throat be cut: ] or the two words EqrY and Hlq

Hence, Eaqarota biY Thou hast long detained me, or restrained me; as though thou hadst hocked ( Eaqarota ) my camel and I were therefore unable to journey: ISk cites as an ex. qado Eaqarato biA@loqawomi A^um~u xazoraji [ Umm-Khazraj has long detained the party, or people ]. [or quasi-inf. n., like jadaAdN and SaraAmN and qaTaAfN &c.,] ↓ , T, S, O, TA,) He cut off the head of the palm-tree, (T, S, O, K,) altogether, with the heart ( Aljum~aAr ), (T, S, O,) so that it dried up, (K,) and nothing came forth from its trunk. A [ single ] second draught. (Mgh.) ― -b2- And hence, (Mgh,) A woman's fellow-wife; her husband's wife: (Mgh, Msb, * K:) or, as some say, a step-mother: but the former is the more correct meaning: (Mgh:) pl. Eal~aAtN . (Msb.) Whence, banuw AlEal~aAti The sons of one father by different mothers: as though, when he added by marriage a second wife to the first, he took a second draught. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., AlA^ano

An accident that befalls an object and causes its state, or condition, to become altered. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (TA,) A disease, sickness, or malady; (S, O, K, TA;) because, by its befalling, the state becomes altered from strength to weakness; so says El-Munáwee in the “ Tow- keef: ” (TA:) or a disease that diverts [ from the ordinary occupations; app. regarded as being from what next follows]: pl. EilalN (Msb) [and Eil~aAtN ]. ― -b3- Also An accident, or event, that diverts the person to whom it occurs from his course, (S, O, K,) or from the object of his want: (M:) as though it became a second occupation hindering him from his former occupation. (S, O.) ― -b4- And [hence,] an excuse; an apology; a plea whereby one excuses himself. (TA.)

3.] ― -b5- And A cause: [and particularly an efficient cause: ] (M, K:) one says, h`*aA Eil~apN lih`*aA This is a cause of this: (M:) and h`*ihi Eil~atuhu This is its cause: (K:) [and ↓ Cause and effect; a phrase of frequent occurrence in theological and other works:] and [sometimes Eil~apN signifies a pretext, or pretence: ] it is said in a trad. of 'Áïsheh, fakaAna Eabodu Alr~aHom`ni yaDoribu rijoliY biEil~api Alr~aAHilapi , meaning And 'Abd-Er-Rahmán was beating my leg with the pretence, or pretext, of his beating the side of the camel with his leg. and ↓ [both mentioned in the first paragraph as inf. ns.] The second draught: or a drinking after drinking, uninterruptedly: (K:) or the former signifies a second drinking; one says EalalN baEoda nahalK [ a second drinking after a first drinking ]: (S, O:) or a drinking after drinking: (Msb:) and the second watering of camels; the first being termed the nahal : (As, TA:) these two terms are also similarly used in relation to suckling: and one of the unknown poets says, vum~a A@novanaY mino baEodi *aA faSal~aY ↓ [ Then he turned, or turned away or back, after that, and blessed the Prophet a first time and a second time ]. (TA.) ― -b2-
Also, the former, Food that has been eaten. (Kr, TA.) [See also nahalN .]
: see EuloEulN .
: see 3; of which it is said in the K to be the subst., though app. the inf. n.
Some light food with which the sick person is diverted or occupied [ so as to be rendered contented ]: pl. EululN . (TA.)

Diseased, sick, or ill; (S, Msb;) and so with p applied to a woman: (Mgh:) or, the former, rendered diseased &c. by God; [being used as the pass. part. n. of A^aEal~ahu in the phrase AEl~hu A@ll~`hu ;] (K;) as also ↓ , (Msb, K,) agreeably with rule, but this is seldom used; (Msb;) and ↓ , from Eal~ahu A@ll~`hu ; (Msb;) or this last should not be said, for, though the theologians say it, it is not of established authority. (K, * TA.) -A2- EaliylapN also signifies A woman perfumed repeatedly: (AA, O, K, TA:) and accord. to AA, ↓ , as used in a verse of Imra-el-Keys, signifies perfumed time after time. (O.) [See also muEal~ilN .]

(S, K) and ↓ (S, * K) and ↓ , (K, TA,) with fet-h, (TA, [in the CK AlEil~apu is put for AlEal~apu ,]) A thing with which a person, (S, K,) or a child, (TA,) is diverted, or occupied so as to be diverted, and contented, or satisfied, (S, K, TA,) such as talk, and singing, and food, &c., (Har p. 308,) [or such as a small quantity of food by which the craving of his stomach is allayed, ] in order that he may be quiet. (TA.) It is said in a trad., accord. to different relations thereof, that dates are the ↓ of the child or of the guest. (TA.) ― -b2-

Also, the first, accord. to the copies of the K, What is drawn from the udder after the first fiyqap : but accord. to IAar, what is drawn from the udder before the first fiyqap [or milk that collects in the udder between two milkings ], and before the second fyqp collects: also termed EuraAkapN and dulaAkapN : (TA:) [or] the milking that is between two milkings: (S, O:) [or] it signifies also the middle milking of the camel that is milked in the first part and the middle and the last part of the day: (K:) or, as some say, the milk that she excerns [ into her udder ] after the milking of the copious flow thereof. (TA.) ― -b3- And A remaining portion of milk (S, O, K, TA) in the udder: (TA:) and (assumed tropical:) of other things: [for instance,] (tropical:) of the course [ of a beast ]: (K

Elw , q. v.] ― -b2- huwa mino Eil~iy~api qawomihi and Eul~iy~atihimo , [both mistranscribed in the CK,] and Eiloyatihimo , without teshdeed, [which belongs to art. Elw ,] and ↓ and ↓ , [which are also mistranscribed in the CK,] mean (assumed tropical:) He is of the exalted, or elevated, of his people. (K, TA.) ― -b3- ↓ mentioned in the Kur [lxxxiii.

18 and 19] is [said to be] a pl. of which the sing. is ↓ , or Eil~iy~apN or Eul~iy~apN , or a pl. having no sing., (K, TA,) [or rather it is from the Hebr. signifying “ high, ” or “ higher, ”] and is said to be A place in the Seventh Heaven, to which ascend the souls of the believers: or the most elevated of the Paradises; like as sij~iyn is the most elevated of the places of the fires [of Hell]: or rather it is properly a name of the inhabitants thereof; for this [sort of] pl. is peculiar to rational beings: (TA:) it is mentioned again in art. Elw [in which see other explanations]. (K, TA.)

Ignorant: (O, K:) so in the saying, A^anaA Eal~aAnN biA^aroDi ka*aA waka*aA [ I am ignorant of such and such a land ]: (O:) and so, with p , applied to a woman: (O, K:) mentioned by Aboo-Sa'eed, as being well known: but said by Az to be unknown to him. (O.)

Ell [so in my original, perhaps ↓ ,] and ↓ and ↓ [all of which are anomalous]. (TA.) ― -b2- And The male of the qanaAbir , (S, O,) the male qunobur [or lark ]; as also ↓ . (K.) and [its pls.] EawaAl~u and Eal~aY epithets applied to camels [as meaning Taking, or having taken, a second draught; and so the first applied to a single she-camel]. (TA.) : see EaliylN : -A2- and see Eil~apN : and also 1, last sentence.

A pool of water left by a torrent, white, and flowing in a regular, or continuous, course, one portion following another: (As, O, K, TA:) or, accord. to Suh, in the R, [simply] a pool of water left by a torrent; so called because it waters the ground a second time ( yaEul~u AlA^aroDa bimaAy^ihi [after its having been watered by the rain]): pl. yaEaAliylu . (TA.) ― -b2- And A dye ( Sibog ) that is imbided ( Eul~a ) one time after another: (O, K:) or, accord. to 'Abd-El-Lateef El-Baghdádee, a garment, or piece of cloth, dyed, and dyed again. (TA.) ― -b3- Accord. to AA, [app. as applied to camels,] yaEaAliylu signifies That have drunk one time after another; and has no sing.: but it is said on other authority to signify that go away at random to pasture ( Aal~atiY tahomiY ) one time after ano

(O.) ― -b6- And Clouds disposed one above another; (S, O;) sing. as above: (S:) or [simply] clouds; so in the R; to which ISd adds containing rain: (TA:) or white clouds; (K, TA; a meaning assigned in the K to the sing.;) but this is said by Niftaweyh in explanation of the phrase biyDN yaEaAliylu in a verse of Kaab Ibn-Zuheyr to whic

senses.text: 1 , aor. , (S, O, TA,) inf. n. EalobN (K, * TA) and EuluwbN , (TA,) He made a mark, or an impression, upon it, (S, O, K, * TA,) accord. to Az, like the mark termed EilaAb [q. v.]; (TA;) and he marked him, or it, with a hot iron

; or scratched him, or it, so as to cause bleeding or not so: (S, O, TA;) and taEoliybN [inf. n. of ↓ ] likewise signifies the doing thus [i. e. the making a mark &c.]: (S, TA: *) and, as also EalobN [inf. n. of Ealaba ], the cutting [a thing], syn. jaz~N ; (so in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K;) or inciding [it], or notching [it]; syn. Haz~N . (K accord. to the TA.) laA taEolubo Suwrataka i. e. Make not thou a mark upon thy Swrp [here meaning face, as in some other instances,] occurs in a trad., as said to a man upon whose nose was seen a mark [of dust, or an impression,] made by pressing hard upon it in prostration. (O, TA.) -A2- Ealaba Als~ayofa , aor. (S, O, K) and , (K,) inf. n. EalobN ; (S, O, K;) and ↓ , (O,) inf. n. taEoliybN ; (O, K;) He bound round the hilt of the sword with
10.] ― -b2- And Ealiba , aor. , inf. n. EalabN ; and Ealaba , aor. ; and ↓ ; said of flesh-meat, It became altered in odour [ for the worse ], after having been hard, or firm. (K.)

[And Ealiba and Ealaba are similarly explained.] ― -b2- See also, 1, last sentence. -A2- AstElb Albaqola He found the herbs, or leguminous plants, to be hard, tough, or coarse. (TA.) And (TA) AstElbt Albaqola , said of cattle, They loathed the herbs, or leguminous plants, and found them, or deemed them, thick, or coarse, (O, K, TA,) being withered. (O, TA.)

1 , said of a man, His EalabiY~ [or rather EilobaAA=ni , the former being pl., and the latter dual, of EilobaA=' , q. v.,] became apparent, by reason of old age: (O, K:) or accord. to the T, his EilobaA=' became depressed. (TA.) -A2- EalobaAhu He cut his EilobaA=' [q. v.], (O, K, TA,) i. e., his slave's ElbA' : (K, TA:) or he perforated his (i. e. his slave's) ElbA' , (K, TA,) and put into it a string, or thread. (TA.)
3 , inf. n. AiEolinobaA='N , He (a man) raised himself

; or drew, or stretched, himself up; like as is done on the occasion of altercation, (S, O, K,) and of reviling. (S, O.) ― -b2- And hence, (K,) it is said also of a cock, and of a dog, (S, O,) and other than these,. (S, O, TA,) as a cat, meaning He prepared himself for evil, or mischief, (K, TA,) and fighting: (TA:) [or ruffled his feathers, ] or bristled up his hair: it is from the EilobaA=' of the neck, and quasi-coordinate to AifoEanolala , with Y [for the final l ]: (S, O, TA:) and sometimes it is with ' [in the place of the Y ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And one says also, AiEolanobaA^a biAlHimoli He rose, or raised himself, with the burden. (TA.)

A mark, an impression, or a scar, (S, O, K, TA,) of beating, and of burning with a hot iron, &c.; (TA;) or such as is mangled and bleeding: (K in art. HbT :) [an inf. n. used as a subst. properly so termed:] pl. EuluwbN . (S, O.) Tufeyl El-Ghanawee has used laEob for Ealob in this sense. (IAar, TA.) ― -b2- And A rugged place; (S, O, K, TA;) as also ↓ : (K, TA:) and ↓ the latter, (O,) or each, (K, TA,) a place, (K,) or a rugged (O, TA) and hard (TA) place of the earth, (O, TA,) which, if rained upon for a long time, will not give growth (O, K, TA) to any green thing: (O, TA:) and ↓ the latter signifies also any rough and hard place of the earth. (O.) ― -b3- And A hard thing; as also ↓ ; (K;) each applied in this sense to flesh, or flesh-meat; the former being an inf. n. used as an epithet.
: see EalibN : ― -b2- and EulobapN , last sentence.

: see EalobN , in three places. ― -b2- Also A place where the sidor [ rhamnus nabeca, or rhamnus spina Christi, a species of lote-tree, ] grows: pl. EuluwbN . (AZ, O, K.) [Accord. to Forskål, (Flora Aegypt. Arab., p. cvi.,) Elb (thus written by him, and also “ œlb, ” app. for Eilob ,) is an appel-lation applied by some in El-Yemen to the tree which he calls Rhamnus nabeca rectus. ] ― -b3- And A man such that one should not covet, or hope to get, what he has, (O, K,) whether of words or of other than words. (O.) ― -b4- And one says, A_in~ahu laEilobu $ar~K Verily he is strong to do evil, or mischief. (TA.)
A certain disease of camels, expl. above: see 1, latter half.
: see EalobN , last sentence. ― -b2-

Also, applied to a he-goat, and to a [lizard of the species-called] Dab~ , Advanced in age, and hard, tough, or coarse: (S, O:) and applied to a mountain-goat, (O, K, TA,) in this sense; (TA;) or as meaning advanced in age; (O;) or large, or bulky, (K, TA,) advanced in age; because of his strength; (TA;) and [in the same sense applied to] a Dab~ , as also ↓ : (K:) and applied to a man, as meaning thick, coarse, rough, or rude. (TA.) And A hard, tough, or coarse, plant. (TA.) -A2- And A camel having the disease termed EalabN [q. v.]; as also ↓ . (TA.)

A milking-vessel of skin, (S, O, TA,) or of wood, like a large qadaH [or bowl ]: (TA:) or a large qadaH of camel's skin, or of wood, into which one milks: (K:) or a bowl into which the she-camel is milked: or a qadaH of wood, or of skin and wood: or a vessel of skin, in the form of a bowl, with a wooden hoop: Az says, it is a piece of skin taken from the side of a camel's hide while it is fresh; it is made round, and filled with soft sand; then its edges are drawn together, and perforated with a wooden skewer, and it is bound so as to be closed, [ thus ] contracted, by a cord [ passed through the holes made with the skewer ], and left until it becomes dry and tough; then its upper part is cut off, and it stands by reason of its dryness, resembling a round bowl, as though it were carved out
; or a pl., and, if so, app. a contraction of EulabN , by poetic license: Sgh, however, adds,] but some say that it is ↓ [i. e.] biAlt~aHoriyk . (O.)

A thick knot of wood, (IAar, O, K, TA,) otherwise expl. as a great branch of a tree, (TA,) whereof is made the miqoTarap , (IAar, O, K, TA,) which is a wooden thing having in it holes adapted to the size of the legs of the persons confined [ by it, i. e. a kind of stocks ]: (TA:) pl. EilabN . (IAar, O, TA.) A poet says, fiY rijolihi EilobapN xa$onaA='u mino qaraZK [ Upon his leg was a rough kind of stocks of the wood of the tree called karadh ]. (O, TA.)
: see EulobapN , last sentence.

[perfectly decl., because the ' is a letter of quasi-coordination, i. e., added to render the word quasi-coordinate to the class of qiroTaAsN and the like,] The EaSab of the neck; [app. meaning the upper, cervical, tendinous portion of the trapezius muscle; ] (S, O, K; [in all of which, mention is made of the ElbA=' of the camel, to which it seems to be most commonly applied, and also to that of a man;]) it is one of a pair, and between one ElbA=' and the other is the place of growth of the mane; (S, O;) Az explains it as specially applied to the thick EaSab ; and IAth, as the EaSab in the neck, extending to the kaAhil [or part between the two shoulder-blades ]: ISd says that it is syn. with EaqabN [q. v.]: (TA:) [it is also said that] it signifies the EaSabap [i. e. tendon, or sinew, ] th

pl. of EilobaA='N [q. v.].
: see EalibN , last sentence.
: see the next paragraph.
A sword having its hilt bound (A, O) with the EilobaA=' of a camel; (O;) as also ↓ . (A.) ― -b2- And muEal~abapN A she-camel (S, K) marked with the mark called EilaAb ; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ . (K.)
One who makes the kind of vessel called EulobapN . (S, O.)

, applied to a she-camel, (S, O, K,) and to a he-camel, (O,) accord. to As, (S,) Without a [ cord such as is called ] xiTaAm [q. v.]: (S, O, K:) and, (K,) accord. to El-Ahmar, (S, O,) without a brand: (S, O, K: [see EilaATN :]) like EuTulN : (TA:) pl. A^aEolaATN . (S, O, K.) ― -b2-

Hence, (O,) A^aEolaATu AlkawaAkibi (assumed tropical:) The shining, or brightly-shining, stars, ( Ald~aAraAriY~ , K, TA, [in the O AldaAr~Y` , an evident mistranscription,]) that have no names: (O, K:) or the named, known stars; as though they were maEoluwTap , i. e. marked with brands. ; or evildoing that obliges one to return evil: (TA:) or the branding, or stigmatizing, with evil. (S, * O.)

A_iEolaAfN ; (K;) He fed the beast (S, * Mgh, O, * Msb, * K) with Ealaf [i. e. fodder, or provender ], (S, * Mgh, O, * Msb,) [i. e. he foddered the beast, ] in the miEolaf [or manger]: (Mgh:) or ↓ the latter signifies he repaired to it often, putting Ealaf for it. (TA.) Fr cites the following verse: EalafotuhaA tibonFA wamaA='F baAridFA Hat~aY $atato ham~aAlapF EayonaAhaA [meaning I fed her with straw, and gave her to drink cool water, so that she passed the winter with her eyes flowing abundantly with tears ]: (S, O:) i. e. wasaqayotuhaA maA='F . (S.) ― -b2- And EalofN signifies also The drinking much. (AA, O, K.) [Accord. to the TK, one says, Ealafahu , aor. , inf. n. EalofN , mea

(O.)

A great eater; one who eats much; (AA, O, K;) as also ↓ [perhaps a mistranscription for ↓ , but see 8]. (TA.) -A2- Also A certain tree, or plant, ( $ajarapN ,) of ElYemen, the leaves of which are like [ those of ] the grape [- vine ]: they are pressed [app. in the nosebags of horses, the TA here inserting fY AlmxAbY , for which I read fY AlmaxaAliY , and it is there added wayusaw~aY , app. as meaning and made into a flat mass, ] and dried, and flesh-meat is cooked therewith instead of with vinegar; (K;) and they [i. e. the leaves] are used as a DimaAd [or dressing for wounds ] ( wayuDam~adu bihi ). is for beasts, or horses and the like; (S, O;) a word of well-known meaning; (K;) i. e. Fodder, or provender for beasts; (KL;) food of cattle, or of animals, (TA,) or of quadrupeds; (MA;) food with which the beast is fed (Mgh, Msb *) in the miEolaf [or manger ]: (Mgh:) accord. to ISh, applied to herbs, or leguminous plants, both fresh and dry: (TA voce Ha$iy$N :) said by ISd to be the qaDiym [generally meaning barley ] of the beast: (TA in the present art.:) [see also EaluwfapN :] pl. [of mult.] EilaAfN (S, O, Msb, K) and EuluwfapN (Mgh, O, K) and [of pauc.] A^aEolaAfN . (O, K.) , from EalafN , What a man assigns, on the occasion of the reaping of his barley, to a guardian [ thereof ] from the birds, or to a friend. (El-Hejeree, TA.)

, (K, TA,) applied to a sheep or goat ( $aAp ), (TA,) i. q. ↓ [i. e. Fed with fodder, or provender; foddered ]: (K, TA:) accord. to AZ, applied to a ram; and having for its pl. The seeking, and buying, and bringing, of Ealaf [i. e. fodder, or provender for beasts ]. (Mgh.)

EulufN (K, TA) [and accord. to the CK and my MS. copy of the K EulofN also; but see what is said above, voce EilofN , respecting this latter]. [See also EalafN

[for raHolN EilaAfiY~N ], (S, O,) and riHaAlN EilaAfiy~apN , (S, O, K,) A camel's saddle, (S, O,) and camels' saddles, [ of a particular sort, ] so called in relation to EilaAfN (S, O, K) the son of HulowaAn , (O, TA,) in the K, erroneously, TuwaAr , (TA,) a man of Kudá'ah, (S, O,) because he was the first maker thereof; (O, K;) or, (K,) accord. to Lth, (O,) the largest of riHaAl in the [ hinder part and the fore part which are called ] A=xirap [in the CK Aaxarap ] and waAsiT : in a verse of Homeyd Ibn-Thowr, ↓ occurs as an abbreviated dim. (applied to a man, S, O) Coarse, rough, rude, or churlish, and advanced in age: (Yaa- koob, S, O, K:) and in this sense also applied to a woman: (TA:) or, thus applied, it signifies old, or aged. , (S, Mgh, O,) with kesr (S, Mgh) to the m ; (Mgh;) or ↓ , like maqoEadN ; (K;) [ A manger; thus called in the present day; i. e.] a place of Ealaf [i. e. fodder, or provender for beasts ]: (S, Mgh, O, K:) [pl. maEaAlifu .] ― -b2- [Hence,] AlmiEolafu , (Ibn-'Abbád, O,) or AlmaEolafu , (K,) is the name of Certain stars, disposed in a round form, [ but ] separate; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K;) also called AlxibaA='u : (Ibn-'Abbád, O:) [the latter appellation is app. wrongly identified in the TA in art. xbY with AlA^axobiypu : what is here meant seems to be the group of stars called by our astronomers Præsepe; agreeably with the former appellation, and with the following statement:] in the mjsTY , [i. e. senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. EalaqN (S, O, Msb, KL, TA) and EalqapN (L, TA) [and app. EuluwqN also, as will be seen from what follows]; and ↓ , (S, MA, Mgh, O, Msb,) and ↓ ; (O, Msb, KL;) It hung to it; it was, or became, suspended to it: (so the first and last accord. to the KL, and the second accord. to the MA and common usage: [in the S and Mgh and O, it is merely said that the first and second signify the same:]) [and] it clung, caught, clave, adhered, held, or stuck fast, to it; (Msb in explanation of all, and TA * in explanation of the first;) and so ↓ . (S, * O, * TA.) It is said in a prov., (S, O, TA,) asserted in the K to have been mentioned before, which is not found to be the case, (TA,) waSar~a Aljunodabu ↓ (S, O, K, [in the CK, erroneously, muEAliqahA ,]) [

91.]) And one says, Ealiqa Al$~awoku biAlv~awobi , aor. , inf. n. EalaqN ; and bihi ↓ ; meaning The thorns clung, caught, &c., to the garment. (Msb.) And ZuforiY biAl$~aYo'i ↓ My nail clung, caught, &c., to the thing. (Msb.) And Ealiqa AlZ~aboYu fiY AlHibaAlapi , (S, O,) or AlS~ayodu ; (K;) or Ealiqa AlwaHo$u biA@loHibaAlapi , inf. n. EuluwqN , (Msb,) [ The gazelle, or the animal of the chase, became caught, or stuck fast, in the snare

; or the wild animal became caught, or held fast, thereby, or] became withheld from getting loose [ thereby ]: whence the saying, Ealiqa AlxaSomu bixaSomihi and bihi ↓ [ The antagonist became held fast, or withheld from getting loose, by his antagonist; and also the antagonist clung, or held fast, to his antagonist ]. (Msb.) [― -b2- The primary significations are those mentioned above in the first sentence: and hence several other significations here following. ― -b3- Ealiqa EalaY ka*aA and Ealayohi ↓ It depended upon such a thing, as a condition. ― -b4- Ealiqa bihi and ↓ It pertained to him, or it: it concerned him, or it. And He had a hold upon it: he had a concern in it. ] ― -b5- EaliqahaA , (S, O,) or Ealiqahu , (K,) and Ealiqa bihaA , (S, O,) or bihi , (K,) inf. n. EuluwqN (S, O, K) a

172.) ― -b9- Ealiqato maraAsiyhaA bi*iY ramoraAmK [ Their anchors have clung to a place having the species of herbage called rmrAm , meaning they are abiding therein, (see mirosaApN , in art. rsw ,)] is said of camels when they are at rest, or at ease, and their eyes are refreshed by the pasturage; and is a prov., applied to persons in the like condition by reason of their means of subsistence. (TA.) ― -b10- Ealiqa bihi , inf. n. EalaqN , He contended with him in an altercation [as though clinging to him]; disputed with him

; or litigated with him. (TA.) ― -b11- laA yaEolaqu bika means lA yaliyqu bk [ It will not be suitable to thee; it will not befit thee ]. (S and K in art. lyq .) ― -b12- Ealiqa yafoEalu ka*aA He set about, began, or betook himself to, doing such a thing. (S, O, K.) faEaliquwA wajohahu DarobFA occurs in a trad., meaning They set about, or betook themselves to, smiting his face. (TA.) And a rájiz says, Ealiqa HawoDiY nugarN mukib~u [ Nughar (a species of birds) bending down their heads ] betook themselves to coming for the purpose of drinking to my HwD [or watering-trough ]: or, as some say, liked it, and frequented it. (S, O.) ― -b13- And maA Ealiqotu A^aqowluhu means I did not cease saying it; like mA na$ibotu . (A in art. n$b .) [Thus Ealiqa has two contr. meanings.] ― -b14- Ealiqati AlA_

Hence, (TA,) it is said in a trad., A^arowaAHu Al$~uhadaA='i fiY HawaASili TayorK xuDorK taEoluqu mino waraqi Aljan~api , (S, Msb, *) or mino vimaAri Aljan~api , (TA,) and, as some relate it, taEolaqu , (Msb, TA,) [both as meaning The souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that eat of the leaves, or fruits, of Paradise, ] but the former relation is that which should be followed, because the latter requires that one should say fiY wrq Aljn~p [or fY vmAr Aljn~p ], though the latter is said to be the more common. (Msb.) One says also, Ealiqati AlA_ibilu , aor. , inf. n. EalaqN , meaning The camels ate of the Euloqap of the trees, i. e., of the trees that remain in the winter and of which the camels are fed until they attain to the rabiyE [meaning spring, or springherbage ]; as a

2 , (S, O, Msb, K,) i. e. Al$~aYo'a , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. taEoliyqN ; (S, O, K;) and ↓ , (S, * O, * Msb,) and ↓ ; (S, O, K;) signify the same. (S, O, Msb, K.) You say, El~q Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'i , (Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. as above, He hung, or suspended, the thing to the thing; and so mina Al$~aYo'i , and Ealayohi : (TA:) [and] he made the thing to cling, catch, cleave, adhere, hold, or stick fast, to the thing; as also bihi ↓ . (Msb.) [For ex.,] one says, Eal~aqotu ri$aAy^iY biri$aAy^ika [ I have suspended my well-rope to thy well-rope ]: and ri$aA='ahu biri$aA='i Albiy^ori ↓ [ He suspended his well-rope to the rope of the well ]. (S, O.) [See also an ex. of the latter verb in a verse cited voce raAfiDN .] And El~qhu EalaY Alwatidi [ He hung it on the peg ]: and in like manner, El~q Al$~aY

; or he supplied the beast with Ealiyq , which means barley, or the like, that is hung upon the beast ]. (TA.) [And hence, as is indicated in the T and TA, El~q signifies, by a metaphor, (tropical:) He supplied with Ealiyq as meaning wine. ] And El~q raAHilatahu He loosed the halter, or leading-rope, from the muzzle of his riding-camel and threw it [or hung it ] upon her shoulders, to give her ease. (TA.) ― -b2- [The primary significations are those mentioned in the second sentence of this paragraph: and hence several other significations here following. ― -b3- El~qhu bika*aA , and EalaY ka*aA , He made it to depend upon such a thing, as a condition. ] You say, Eal~aqotu Eitoqa EabodiY bimawotiY [ I made the freedom of my slave to depend upon my death ]. He showed open enmity or hostility, with another ]. (TK.) ― -b2- Or The laying open, or manifesting, of each one to his fellow, what is in his mind. (TA.) You say, EaAlanotu bihi , [or EaAlanotuhu ,] inf. n. muEaAlanapN and EilaAnN , [ I laid open, or manifested, to him what was in my mind, he doing the same to me, ] i. e. each of us laid open, or manifested, to the other, what was in his mind. (Msb.) ― -b3- See also the next paragraph.

4 I laid it open, manifested it, revealed it, made it public, or published it; namely, an affair, a case, or an event; (S, Msb, K, TA;) as also AElnt bihi ; and ↓ , (K, TA,) [for which latter the CK has Ealanotuhu , but it is] with teshdeed, (TA,) inf. n. taEoliynN ; (TK;) [and ↓ , for] EaAlanahu , (K,) or [rather] EAlnhu AlA^amora , (TK,) means AEln A_ilayohi AlA^amora [ He laid open, &c., to him, the affair, or case, or event ]. (K.) ― -b2-

Hence, A^aEolanato , occurring in a trad., as said of a woman [accused of adultery], She revealed [or confessed ] the enormity, or act of adultery. (TA.) ― -b3- [And AEln bihi app. signifies He made him to be, or become, publicly known: see 10; and see also A^aZoharotu bifulaAnK , in art. Zhr .] ― -b4- AEln AlA^amoru The affair, or case, or event, was, or became, notorious
; or commonly, or publicly, known; syn. Ai$otahara . (TA. [Compare
1.]) ― -b5- See also 3, first sentence.
8 see the first paragraph.

10 i. q. taEar~aDa liA^ano yuEolana bihi [app. meaning He addressed himself to being, or sought to be, made publicly known ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [And] AisotiEolaAnN signifies [or is said to signify] The seeking, or desiring, to lay open, manifest, reveal, make public, or publish. (KL.) ― -b3- [And] i. q. A_iEolaAnN [inf. n. of 4, but in what sense is not shown; perhaps of

(TA.) [It is also mentioned in art. Elw .]
part. n. of Ealina : see EaAlinN . (Msb.)

Hence, EalaAniypF meaning Openly, or publicly; and aloud: see Kur ii. 275; &c.] ― -b2- Also One's outward man; syn. bar~aAniY~N , q. v.: opposed to sariyrapN and jaw~aAniY~N . (T in art. br .) -A2- [And it is also used as an epithet; app. by those who hold it to be originally an inf. n.

; or rather its being thus used may be regarded as corroborating the assertion that it is originally an inf. n., like EadolN &c., though, as an epithet, it has a pl.:] one says rajulN EalaAniyapN , pl. senses.text: 1 , (Msb, K,) aor. yaEoluw , (Msb,) inf. n. Euluw~N ; (Msb, K;) and EaliYa ; and ↓ [which last see also below]; (K;) It (a thing, Msb) was, or became, high, elevated, or lofty; (Msb, K; *) syn. AirotafaEa ; (Msb;) and so ↓ : (S, K:) or you say, EalaA fiY AlmakaAni [ it was, or became, high, or elevated, in place ], aor. yaEoluw , inf. n. Euluw~N : (S:) and EaliYa fiY Al$~arafi [(assumed tropical:) he was, or became, high, or elevated, or exalted, in dignity, or nobility ], (S, Mgh,) with kesr, (S,) aor. yaEolaY , inf. n. EalaA='N ; (S, Mgh;) and also EalaA , with fet-h, aor. yaEolaY : a poet says, lam~aA EalaA kaEobuka liY Ealiytu [(assumed tropical:) When thy nobility became exalted to me, I became exalted ]; thus combining the two dial. vars.: (S:) or you say, EaliYa fiY AlmakaArimi [(as

; or overspread it; as scum, and rust, &c. And It lay on him as a burden. Hence,] one says, maA saA^alotuka maA yaEoluwka ZahorFA i. e. [(assumed tropical:) I did not ask, or demand, of thee, what would lie as a burden on thy back

; or] what would be onerous, burdensome, oppressive, or troublesome, to thee. (TA.) ― -b4- And [hence also] EalaAhu It over- topped it, rose above it, or exceeded it in height. (TA in art. dSr .) [And in like manner, ↓ Ealayohi It became elevated above it. ] ― -b5- And Ealawotuhumo biAl$~arafi and biAljamaAli [(assumed tropical:) I was, or became, superior to them in nobility and in goodliness ]. (S in art. frE .) ― -b6- And EalaAhu [(assumed tropical:) He had, or gained, ascendency over him, or it; as also EalaA Ealayohi and Elyh ↓ : and] (assumed tropical:) he overcame him

; or had, or gained, the mastery over him; (S, Msb, TA;) and subdued him; (Msb;) namely, his opponent, or adversary; as also ↓ : and in like manner, EalaA HaAjatahu and ↓ (assumed tropical:) he gained the mastery over the object of his want: and ↓ Al$~aYo'a (assumed tropical:) he prevailed against the thing, or had power over it, and overcame it; and EalaA lil$~aYo'i , aor. yaEoluw , (assumed tropical:) he was, or became, able to do, or accomplish, or to bear, the thing. (TA.) EalaA biAlA^amori means AiDoTalaEa bihi waA@sotaqal~a [i. e. (assumed tropical:) He had strength, or power, sufficient for the affair, and had absolute control over it ]: (S: [so in one of my copies: the other has AiT~alaEa , which I find also in the PS and in my copy of the TA; and which is allowed by some, but disa

4 in art. blw )]: or [perhaps a mistake for “ and ”] it is [virtually] a prayer for his continuance in life. (TA.) ― -b7- Ealawotu EalaY fulaAnK Alr~iyHa means I was [or went ] on the windward side of such a one: and one says, laA taEolu Alr~iyHa EalaY AlS~ayodi fayaraAHa riyHaka wayanofira [i. e. Go not thou on the windward side of the game, lest it scent thy odour, and take fright and flee ]. (TA.) ― -b8- Ealawotuhu biAls~ayofi means I smote him [ with the sword

; or, more properly, I set upon him therewith ]. (S, TA.) And [in like manner] one says, EalaAhu biAl$~atomi waAlD~arobi [(assumed tropical:) He set upon him, or assailed him, or overcame him, with reviling and beating ]. (S and M in art. vwl , &c.) ― -b9- EalaA fiY AlA^aroDi , (S, TA,) inf. n. Euluw~N , (S,) signifies (assumed tropical:) He exalted, or magnified, himself, [ in the earth, ] or behaved proudly, insolently, or exorbitantly. (S, * TA.) And [in like manner] laA taEoluwA EalaY A@ll~`hi , in the Kur xliv. 18, (assumed tropical:) Exalt not, or magnify not, yourselves against God

; or behave not proudly, &c. (Bd, Jel.) ― -b10- EalaA Eanohu [lit. signifies It rose from it: and hence,] it recoiled from it, i. e., a thing from another thing; it did not cleave to it: and taEoluw Eanohu AlEayonu means (assumed tropical:) The eye recoils from him. (TA.) ― -b11- AuEolu Ean~iY : see
3. ― -b12- EalaA bihi as syn. with A^aEolaAhu : see expl. with the latter below.

4. ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, Eal~ayotu bihi EalaY AlbaEiyri [ I raised it, and put it, upon the camel ]: (S:) [and so ↓ ; as in a verse cited voce raAy^iHN , in art. rwH ; in which, and in the present art., it is cited in the S and TA: and ↓ bihi ; as in a verse cited voce A_ilaY in the sense of mino , in art. Alw :] and EalaY~a ↓ means AiHomilo [i. e. Put thou upon me such a thing to be carried by me

; or load thou me ]. (S, K.) ― -b3- And Eal~ayotu AlHabola , inf. n. taEoliyapN , I raised the cord to its proper place in respect of the channel of the sheave, and in respect of the [ main ] well-rope. (S.) ― -b4- And El~Y Ald~alowa , inf. n. as above, He raised the bucket from a stone projecting in the lower part of the casing of a well [ and impeding its ascent ]; he having descended the well for that purpose: [or simply he raised the filled bucket; for] some say that ↓ signifies he who raises the filled bucket; i. e., who draws water thereby. (TA.) ― -b5- And El~Y AlmataAEa Eani Ald~aAb~api He put down the goods, or furniture and utensils, from the beast: [app. because he who does so lifts them off the beast:] (K, TA:) A^aEolaAhu in this sense is disapproved. (TA.) ― -b6- See also 1, f
3 signifies (assumed tropical:) The vying, competing, or contending for superiority, in highness, loftiness, elevation, or eminence. (KL.) You say, EaAlaAhu , meaning saAmaAhu . (M in art. smw . [See

3 in that art. in two places.]) ― -b2- See 4, in two places. ― -b3- EuwliYa , said of clarified butter, and of the fat of anything having fatness, means It was wrought ( SuniEa [app. over a fire ]) until it rose in the operation. (TA.) ― -b4- EaAlawoA naEiy~ahu (assumed tropical:) They manifested the announcement of his death: (K, TA:) [as though meaning they raised the report of his death: ] one should not say A^aEolawohu nor Eal~awohu . (TA.) ― -b5- See 2, in three places. ― -b6- EaAlati Albayoquwra , occurring in a verse of Umeiyeh Ibn-Abi-s-Salt, is mentioned and explained in the S in this art. and in art. Ewl : see the latter art. [to which it seems more properly to belong]. ― -b7- See 1, former half, in two places. ― -b8- EaAli Ean~iY Remove thou, or go thou away or aside, from me; a

; or made it high, or lofty; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ , (K,) with teshdeed, (TA,) and bihi ↓ [without teshdeed]: (K:) it is [also] said of God, meaning (assumed tropical:) He elevated, or exalted, him; and ↓ is like it [in meaning]: (S:) and bifulaAnK ↓ signifies the same as A^aEolayotuhu [(assumed tropical:) I elevated, or exalted, such a one; as also, app., (see
4 in art. Zhr ,) A^aEolayotu bifulaAnK ]. (Ham p.

175.) Hence one says, A^aEolaY A@ll~`hu kaEobahu [(tropical:) God exalted, or may God exalt, his nobility ]. (TA.) ― -b2- See also 1, former half. ― -b3- A^aEoli AlwisaAdapa means Sit thou upon the cushion. (TA.) ― -b4- And A^aEoli Eani AlwisaAdapi Rise thou from the cushion; syn. qumo : (TA in art. dk :) or descend thou from it. (S * and TA in the present art.) And AElY Eani Ald~aAb~api He alighted from the beast. (K, TA.) ― -b5- See also 3, latter half, in three places.

5 : see 1, first sentence. ― -b2- Also (K) He, or it, was, or became, high, elevated, or lofty, gently, or leisurely. (S, K.) ― -b3- And He came upon a party of men suddenly, or at unawares, without permission. (TA.) ― -b4- taEal~ato mino nifaAsihaA (assumed tropical:) She (a woman) became free, (S, Mgh, K,) and passed forth, (Mgh,) from her state of impurity consequent upon childbirth; (S, Mgh, K;) as also ↓ ; (Mgh; and TA in art. El ;) and so taEaAl~ato , as well as taEal~alato : (K and TA in that art.:) or mino maraDihaA from her disease: (K:) or you say of a woman, tEl~t mn nfAshA meaning [as above or] she became pure from the effects of her childbirth: (TA:) and of a man you say, tEl~Y mino Eil~atihi (S, TA) he recovered from his disease. (TA.)

6 : see 1, first sentence. ― -b2- Addressing a man, (S, Msb,) using the imperative form, you say, taEaAla , (S, Msb, K,) with fet-h to the l , (S, K,) originally meaning Be thou elevated, (S, Msb,) and said by a man in a high place in calling a man in a low place; (Msb;) then, by reason of frequency of usage, employed in the sense of halum~a [meaning Come thou ], (S, Msb,) absolutely, whether the place of the person called be high or low or on the same level; so that it is originally applied to denote a particular meaning, and then used in a general meaning: (Msb:) and to a woman one says, taEaAlaYo ; (S, K;) and to two women, (S,) or two persons, (TA,) taEaAlayaA ; (S, TA;) and to a pl. number of men, taEaAlawoA ; (Msb, TA;) and to a pl. number of women, taEaAlayona ; (S, Msb, TA;) and so
; or simply, was, or became, above it, i. e. too elevated in character for it: and also, exalted himself above such a thing
; or held himself above it. ] Said of God, in the Kur xx.

113 [and in other instances therein], it means [(assumed tropical:) Exalted, or supremely exalted, is He ] in his essence and his attributes, above the created beings. (Bd.) [But in common speech, it is generally used as an ejaculation of praise, meaning (assumed tropical:) Exalted or extolled, or supremely exalted or extolled, be He, or his greatness or majesty or glory, or his name

; or acknowledged be his absolute supremacy. And the common expression (used in citing words of the Kur-án) qaAla taEaAlaY means (assumed tropical:) He saith, or hath said, exalted or extolled, or supremely exalted or extolled, be He; &c.] ― -b4- See also

10 see 1, in seven places. [The inf. n. AisotiEolaA='N , properly denotes Superiority that is perceptible by sense: and tropically, such as is ideal, or perceived by the intellect: see EalaY , below.] ― -b2- One says also, h`*ihi Alkalimapu tasotaEoliY lisaAniY , meaning [(assumed tropical:) This word, or sentence, ] is often current upon my tongue. (TA.) ― -b3- And AisotaEolaY EalaY AlgaAyapi , said of a horse in the contending to outstrip in a race, means (assumed tropical:) He reached the goal. (TA.)
12 : see 1, former half.
