: see the next paragraph. It also signifies, simply, Above him or it

; or in the higher, or highest, part of him or it: thus in a hemistich cited voce taHot . (Mughnee.) [In all cases,] Ealu is determinate, and indecl., with damm for its invariable termination: (Mughnee, TA:) [for it is regarded as a prefixed noun of which the complement is to be understood as to the meaning but not as to the letter:] in the saying of Ows, kagiroqiy^i bayoDK kan~ahu AlqayoDu mino Ealuw [ Like the thin pellicle of eggs, which the shell covers above ], the w [in Ealuw ] is augmentative, being added to render the rhyme unrestricted: (S, TA:) and in the instance of mino Ealuho , likewise ending a verse, the h is that of pausation: for if Ealu were [really] a prefixed noun, it would not be thus indecl. (Mughnee, TA.)

You say, qaEadotu Eulowahu and ↓ and fiY Eulowihi and ↓ [i. e. I sat in the higher, or highest, part of it ]. (TA.) And Aashà-Báhileh says, A_in~iY A^atanoniY lisaAnN laA A^usar~u bihaA laA EajabN minohaA walaA suxuru ↓ mino Ealowa (S,) or, as in one of my copies of the S, A^asur~u and saxaru ,) i. e. Verily information has come to me [ by which I shall not be rejoiced (or by which I shall not rejoice others, accord. to the latter reading mentioned above,)] from the higher, or highest, parts of Nejd, ( mino A^aEolaY najodK , thus in some copies of the S and in the TA, but in other copies of the S

is a particle and a noun (Mbr, S, Mughnee, K) and a verb; (Mbr, S;) though some assert that it is only a noun, and ascribe this assertion to Sb: (Mughnee:) its alif, (Sb, S, Msb,) [which, when it has no affix, is written Y , and] which is originally w , (Sb, S,) [like that of A_ilaY , q. v.,] is changed into [what is properly] Y when it has a pronominal affix, (Sb, S, Msb,) as in Ealayoka , (Sb, S,) and Ealayohi ; (Msb;) but some of the Arabs [in this case] leave it unchanged, as in the saying of a rájiz, TaAruwA EalaAhun~a faTiro EalaAhaA [ They fled, or have fled, upon them, (referring to camels,) and flee thou upon her ]; this, it is said, being of the dial. of Belhárith Ibn-Kaab. (Sb, S.) ― -b2- As a particle, it has nine [or more than nine] meanings. (Mughnee.) As such, (Mughnee,) or,

22 and xl. 80], waEalayohaA waEalaY A@lofuloki tuHomaluwna [ And upon them (referring to camels) and upon the ship, or ships, ye are carried ]; (Mughnee, K;) or with respect to what is near thereto, as in the saying [in the Kur xx. 10], A^awo A^ajidu EalaY A@ln~aAri hudFY [ Or I shall find near upon the fire, i. e. at the fire, a right direction ]: (Mughnee:) and using it to denote AlAstElA=' properly thus termed, you say, kunotu EalaY Als~aToHi [ I was upon the flat house-top ]: (Msb:) [in like manner also,] as denoting AlAstElA=' that is perceptible by sense, it occurs in the saying [in the Kur lv. 26], kul~u mano EalayohaA faAnK [ Every one that is upon it (referring to the earth) is transitory ]: (Es-Subkee, TA:) and you say, EalaY zayodK vawobN [ Upon Zeyd is, or was, a garment ], Eal

254 and xvii. 22], faD~alonaA baEoDahumo EalaY baEoDK (tropical:) [ We have made some of them to have superiority over some ]. (Es-Subkee, Mughnee, TA.) [See also A^anota EalaY EayoniY , and and A^anota EalaY raA^osiY , voce EayonN , first quarter.] ― -b3- It also denotes concomitance, like maEa ; as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 172], waA=taY AlmaAla EalaY Hub~ihi [ And giveth property with (or notwithstanding ) the love of it ]; (Mughnee, K;) and so it is said to be used in the phrase, in a trad. respecting the alms of the breaking of the fast [of Ramadán], EalaY kul~i Hur~K waEabodK SaAEN [ With every free man and slave, a sáa ], because the alms-gift of the breaking of the fast is not incumbent on the slave, but only on his master; (IAth, TA;) and so it is used in the [common] phrase,

13.) ― -b4- It also denotes transition, (Mughnee, K,) like Eano ; (Mughnee;) as in the saying (of El-Koheyf El- 'Okeylee, TA), A_i*aA raDiyato EalaY~a banuw qu$ayorK laEamoru A@ll~`hi A^aEojabaniY riDaAhaA [ When the sons of Kusheyr shall be pleased, or well pleased, or content, with me, (or rather, if EalaY~a here denote transition, with what will proceed from me, ) by the everlasting existence of God, their being pleased, &c., will induce in me admiration, or pleasure ], (Mughnee, K, * TA,) i. e. Ean~iY ; (Mughnee, TA;) or it may be that raDiYa is made to imply the meaning of EaTafa [which is trans. by means of EalaY ]; (Mughnee;) or, as Ks says, it is made to accord with its contr. saxiTa , (Mughnee, TA,) by its being made trans. by means of EalaY : (TA:) and so in the saying, fiY layol

; or it may be said that yaHokiY is [here] made to imply the meaning of yanuim~u . (Mughnee.) ― -b5- It is also used to assign a cause, like l ; as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 181], walitukab~iruwA A@ll~`ha EalaY maA hadaAkumo , (Mughnee, K,) meaning lihidaAyatihi A_iy~aAkumo [i. e. And that ye should magnify God for, or on account of, his rightly directing you ]; (Mughnee;) [and in the same, vi. 90, &c., laA A^asoA^alukumo Ealayohi A^ajorFA i. e. I will not ask of you for it, or on account of it, a recompense; ] and as in the saying of Rabee'ah Ibn Makroom Ed-Dabbee, fadaEawoA nazaAli fakunotu A^aw~ala naAzilK waEalaAma A^arokabuhu A_i*aA lamo A^anozili i. e. [ And they called out, “ Alight; ” and I was the first of any alighting: ] and for what [or wherefore ] do I ride him if I do not

[ EalaAma is here, as usually, for EalaY ma .]) ― -b6- It is also used in the sense of fiY [generally followed by a noun significant of time]; (S, Mughnee, K; *) as in the saying [in the Kur xxviii. 14], wadaxala A@lomadiynapa EalaY Hiyni gafolapK [ And he entered the city in, or during, a time of inadvertence ]; (Mughnee, K;) and in the saying [in the same ii. 96], waA@t~abaEuwA maA tatoluw A@l$~ayaATiynu EalaY muloki sulayomaAna , meaning, fiY zamani mulki slymAn [i. e. And they followed what the devils related, or recited, in the time of, or during, the reign of Suleymán (or Solomon )]; (Mughnee;) and in the phrase, kaAna ka*aA EalaY Eahodi fulaAnK , meaning, fiY Eahodihi [i. e. It was thus, or such a thing was, in the time of such a one ]: (S:) [and in like manner it is used in the

180 &c. of the same, i. e. In (or, as we also say, on ) a journey: in like manner also] laqado sarayotu EalaY AlZ~alaAmi , in a verse of Aboo-Kebeer El-Hudhalee, means, fiY AlZ~alaAmi [i. e. Hence, EuwjN signifies The legs of a horse or similar beast; (O, TA;) as ISd says, thus used as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates [app. implying their having that bending, or curving, and tension of the sinews, termed tajoniyb , agreeably with what here follows]. (TA.) ― -b7- And hence also, (TA,) xayolN EuwjN meaning Horses that have, in their hind legs, the quality termed tajoniyb . (O, K.) ― -b2- And He did it a second time: (S, Msb:) he repeated it, or iterated it; syn. kar~arahu ; namely, speech; (K;) as also lahu ↓ ; he said it a second time; (Mgh;) and A_ilayohi ↓ and Ealayohi [likewise] signify the same as AEAdhu : (TA:) but Aboo-Hilál El-'Askeree says that kar~arahu signifies he repeated it once or more than once; whereas AEAdhu signifies only he repeated it once: (MF, TA:) AEAd AlkalaAma mean he repeated the speech [ saying it ] a second time; syn. rad~adahu vaAniyFA . (O.) One says, AEAd AlS~alaApa He said the prayer a second time. (Msb.) And maA yubodiy^u wamaA yuEiydu signifies mA yatakal~amu bibaAdiy^apK walaA EaAy^idapK , (Lth, A, O,) i. e. He does not say any

; or anything original, nor anything in the way of repetition; baAdiy^apu AlkalaAmi signifying what is said for the first time; and AlkalaAmi ↓ , what is said for the second time, afterwards: (TA in art. bdA^ :) or he says not anything: (A:) and he has no art, artifice, or cunning. (IAar, TA; and A in art. bdA^ ; q. v.) ― -b3- [Also He returned it, or restored it, to a former state: and hence, he renewed it: he reproduced it. ] One says of God, yubodiy^u Alxaloqa vum~a yuEiyduhu , meaning [ He createth, or bringeth into existence, mankind: ] then He returneth them, after life, to lifelessness, in the present world; and after lifelessness, to life, on the day of resurrection. (TA.) ― -b4- See also

; or made to be, or become; (like jaEala ;) in which sense it is doubly trans.: see an ex. in a verse cited voce EasiyfN .]

8 : see 1, near the beginning. -A2- AEtAdhu He frequented it

; or came to it and returned to it; namely, a place. (T in art. ArY .) ― -b2- And He looked at it time after time until he knew it. ; or he accustomed, or habituated, himself to it

; or made it his custom, or habit. (S, O, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad., Alxayora ↓ faA_in~a Alxayora EaAdapN waAl$~ar~a lajaAjapN , meaning Accustom yourselves to good; for good becomes a habit, and evil is persevered in. (A.) And one says, ↓ Alkalobu AlS~ayoda The dog became accustomed, or habituated, to the chase. (S.) ― -b4- See also 1, latter half, in two places.

10 He asked him to return. (O, Msb, K.) ― -b2- And AstEAdhu Al$~aYo'a He asked him to repeat the thing; to do it a second time: (S, O, Msb, K:) and AstEAdhu minohu [ He asked for the repetition of it from him ]. (Har p.
28.) ― -b3- See also

: see EaAdapN . -A2- maA A^adoriY A^aY~u EaAda huwa , (S, O, K,) EAd being in this case imperfectly decl., (S, O, [but in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K it is written EAdK ,]) means I know not what one of mankind he is. (S, O, K.) [Perhaps it is from EaAdN the name of an ancient and extinct tribe of the Arabs.]

, indecl., with kesr for its termination, is a particle in the sense of A_in~a , governing an accus. case, on the condition of its being preceded by a verbal proposition and a conjunction; as in the saying, raqadotu waEaAdi A^abaAka saAhirN [ I slept, and verily thy father was waking, or remaining awake, by night ]: ― -b2- it is also an interrogative particle in the sense of halo , indecl., with kesr for its termination, requiring an answer; as in the saying, EaAdi A^abuwka muqiymN [ Is thy father abiding? ]: ― -b3- it also denotes an answer, in the sense of a proposition rendered negative by means of lm or of mA , only; indecl., with kesr for its termination; and this is when it is conjoined with a pronoun; as when an interrogator says, halo Sal~ayota [ Didst thou perform, or hast thou pe

an inf. n. of 1, as also ↓ , (S, O, K,) and ↓ , and ↓ . (K.) [Hence,] one says, laka AlEawodu and ↓ and ↓ It is for thee to return (Lh, K, TA) fiY h`*aA AlA^amori in this affair. (TA.) And ↓ and ↓ (A, TA) O God, grant us a return to the House [i. e. the Kaabeh, called “ the House” as being “ the House of God”]. (TA.) And rajaEa Eawodahu EalaY badoy^ihi , (Sb, K,) [expl. in the TA in art. gbr as meaning He returned without his having obtained, or attained, anything, ] and EawodFA EalaY bado'K : (K:) and rajaEotu EawodiY EalaY badoy^iY : (Sb:) expl., with other similar phrases, in art. bdA^ , q. v. -A2- See also EaAy^idN . -A3- Also A camel, (IAar, S, O, Msb, K,) and a sheep or goat, (IAar, O, K,) old, or advanced in age: (S, O, Msb, K:) applied to the former, that has passed the ages at whi

586.] ― -b3- And (tropical:) An old road: (S, O, K:) from the same word as an epithet applied to a camel. (O.) A poet says, (S, O,) namely, Besheer Ibn-En-Nikth, (TA, and so in a copy of the S,) EawodN EalaY EawodK liA^aqowaAmK A^uwalo yamuwtu biAlt~aroki wayaHoyaA biAlEamalo (S, * O, TA) i. e. An old camel upon an old road [ belonging to prior peoples ], (S, O, TA,) a road that dies away by being abandoned and revives by being travelled. (TA.) And another says, EawodN EalaY EawodK EalaY EawodK xalaqo i. e. An old man upon an old camel upon an old worn road. (IB, TA.) [See also muEiydN .] ― -b4- And suwdadN EawodN means (tropical:) Old [ lordship, or glory or honour or dignity ]. (S, A, O, K, TA.) [See also EaAdiY~N .] ― -b5- And A_in~aka latamut~u biraHimK EawodapK occurs in a trad., as s

Wood; timber; syn. xa$abN : (Mgh, O, K:) any slender piece of wood or timber: (Lth, TA:) or a piece of wood of any tree, whether slender or thick: or a part, of a tree, in which sap runs, whether fresh and moist or dry: (TA:) a staff; a stick; a rod: and also a sprig: (the lexicons &c. passim:) a branch

; or twig; properly, that is cut off; but also applied to one not cut off: (Har p. 499:) [and the stem of the raceme of a palm-tree, and the like: (see faj~aAnN , in art. fj :)] pl. [of mult.] EiydaAnN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) originally EiwodaAnN , (Msb,) and [of pauc.] A^aEowaAdN . (S, O, Msb, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] rak~aba A@ll~`hu EuwdFA EuwdFA , (A,) or EuwdFA EalaY EuwdK , (TA,) God caused the arrow to be put upon the bow, for shooting; (A;) meaning that civil war, or conflict, or faction, or sedition, became excited. (A, TA.) ― -b3- And sabiylu *iY AlA^aEowaAdi (assumed tropical:) Death: AlAEwAd meaning the pieces of wood upon which the dead is carried: (El-Mufaddal, Az, L:) for the Arabs of the desert, having no biers, put two pieces of wood together, and on them carry the dead to the g

, originally EiwodN , the w being changed into Y because of the kesreh before it, (Az, TA,) An occurrence that befalls, or betides, one, or that happens to one, [or returns to one, of some former affection of the mind or body, i. e.] of anxiety, (S, O, K,) or of some other kind, (S, O,) of disease, or of grief, (O, K,) and the like, (K,) of affliction, and of desire: and accord. to Az, the time of return of joy and of grief. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence, A festival

; or periodical festival; ] a feast-day; (KL;) i. q. mawosimN ; (Msb;) any day on which is an assembling, or a congregating; (K;) [and particularly an anniversary festival: ] so called because it returns every year with renewed joy: (IAar, TA:) or, from EaAda , because people return to it: or from EaAdapN , “ a custom,” because they are accustomed to it: (TA:) pl. A^aEoyaAdN ; the Y being retained in the pl. because it is in the sing., or to distinguish it from A^aEowaAdN the pl. of EuwdN ; (S, O, Msb;) for regularly its pl. would be A^aEowaAdN , like as A^arowaAHN is pl. of riyHN . (TA.) [The two principal religious festivals of the Muslims are called Eiydu AlA^aDoHaY The festival of the victims (see art. DHw and DHY ) and Eiydu AlfiTori The festival of the breaking of the fast after Rama

Also, A certain sort of mountain-tree, (K, TA,) that produces twigs about a cubit in length, dust- coloured, having no leaves nor blossoms, but having much peel, and having many knots: fresh wounds are dressed with its peel, and close up in consequence thereof. (TA.)

A custom, manner, habit, or wont; syn. daA^obN , and watiyrapN , (MA,) or dayodanN : (K:) so called because one returns to it time after time: it respects more especially actions; and EurofN , sayings; as in indicated in the Telweeh &c.

; or, accord. to some, EurofN and EaAdapN are syn.: (MF, TA:) and accord. to El-Mufaddal, [↓ signifies the same as EaAdapN ; for he says that] EaAdaniY EiydiY means EaAdatiY [i. e. My habit returned to me: but see the next preceding paragraph, first sentence]: (L, TA:) the pl. of EaAdapN is EaAdaAtN (S, O, Msb) and ↓ , (S, O, Msb, K,) or rather this is a coll. gen. n., (TA,) and ↓ , (L, K, TA,) mentioned by Kr, but not of valid authority, (L, TA,) [app. a mistranscription for EiyadN , like HiwajN , a pl. of HaAjapN ,] and EawaAy^idu , (Msb, TA,) like as HawaAy^iju is pl. of HaAjapN ; but, accord. to Z and others, this last is pl. of EaAy^idapN , not of EaAdapN . (TA.)
: see EawodN , first three sentences.

An old, or ancient, thing: (S, A, Mgh, * O, Msb, * K:) as though so called in relation to the [ancient and extinct] tribe of 'Ád ( EAd ). (S, A, O, Msb.) One says xaribN EaAdiY~N Old, or ancient, ruins. (Mgh.) And biy^orN EaAdiy~apN An old, or ancient, well: (O:) or a well strongly cased with stone or brick, and abounding with water, the origin of which is referred to [ the tribe of ] 'Ád. (Msb.) And binaA='N EaAdiY~N A firm, or strong, building, the origin of which is referred to [ the tribe of ] 'Ád. (Msb.) And EaAdiY~u A^aroDK Land possessed from ancient times. (Msb.) And mulokN EaAdiY~N Dominion of old, or ancient, origin. (Msb.) And majodN EaAdiY~N Old, or ancient, glory. (A.) [See also EawodN .]

an appellation given to Certain excellent she-camels; (S, O, K;) so called in relation to a stallion, (S, O, K,) well-known, (K,) that begat an excellent breed, (S, O,) named EiydN : (O, K:) [so some say:] but ISd says that this is not of valid authority: (TA:) or so called in relation to El-'Eedee Ibn-En-Nadaghee Ibn-Mahrah-Ibn- Heidán: (Ibn-El-Kelbee, O, K:) or in relation to 'Ád Ibn-'Ád: or 'Ádee Ibn-'Ád: (K:) but if from either of the last two, it is anomalous: (TA:) or in relation to the Benoo-'Eed-Ibn-El- 'Ámiree: (O, K:) Az says that he knew not the origin of their name. (L.) ― -b2- And accord. to Sh, [ A female lamb; ] the female of the buroqaAn [pl. of baraqN ]; the male of which is called xaruwf until he is shorn: but this was unknown to As. (L.)

Tall palm-trees: (As, S, O, K:) or the tallest of palm-trees: (K in art. Eyd :) but not so called unless the stumps of their branches have fallen off and they have become bare trunks from top to bottom: (AHn, M, TA in art. Eyd :) or i. q. raqolapN [q. v.]: (AO, TA in art. Eyd :) [a coll. gen. n.:] n. un. with p : (S, O, K:) which As explains as applied to a hard, old tree, having roots penetrating to the water: and he says, wmnh hymAn wEylAn : [but what these words mean, I know not:] (TA:) the word belongs to this art. and to art. Eyd : (K in art. Eyd :) or it may belong to the present art., or to art. Edn [q. v.]. (Az, S, O.) The Prophet had a bowl [made of the wood] of an EayodaAnap , (K, TA,) or, accord. to some, it is preferably written with kesr [i. e. EiydaAnap ], (TA,) in which he v

: see EuwaAdapN . ― -b2- Eudo faA_in~a laka EinodanaA EawaAdFA HasanFA , (S, O, K,) as also EuwaAdFA and EiwaAdFA , (O, K,) these two only, not the first, mentioned by Fr, (O,) means [ Return thou, and thou shalt have with us ] what thou wilt like: (S, O, K:) or kind treatment. (TA.)
, [an imperative verbal noun,] like nazaAli (S, O) and taraAki , (S,) means Return thou; syn. Eudo . (S, O, K.)
dim. of EiydN , q. v. (TA.)
: see EawodN , first and second sentences. ― -b2-

Also, (S, O, K,) and if you elide the p you say ↓ , like lamaAZN and qaDaAmN , (Az, TA,) [in the O EawaAdapN and EuwaAdapN with damm, (but the former is probably a mistranscription,)] Food brought again after its having been once eaten of: (S, O:) or food brought again for a particular man after a party has finished eating. (A, K.)
A player upon the Euwd [or lute ]: (K:) or one who makes, ( yat~axi*u ,) the stringed Euwd [or lute ]; (O;) or a maker ( mut~axi* ) of EiydaAn [or lutes ]. (TA.) [Fem. with p .]

A visiter of one who is sick: (Msb, TA:) thus it more commonly and especially means: but it also signifies any visiter of another, who comes time after time: (TA:) pl. Euw~aAdN (Msb, K) and ↓ , (K,) or [rather] EawodN and Euw~aAdN signify the same, like zaworN and zuw~aArN , (Fr, O, TA,) but EawodN is a quasi-pl. n. like as SaHobN is of SaAHibN : (TA:) the fem. is EaAy^idapN , of which the pl. is Euw~adN , (Az, Msb, TA,) incorrectly said in the K to be a pl. of EaAy^idN ; and EawaAy^idu also is a pl. of the fem. (TA.)
fem. of EaAy^idN [q. v.]. (Az, Msb, TA.) ― -b2- EaAy^idapu AlkalaAmi : see

4. ― -b3- EaAy^idapN also signifies Favour, kindness, pity, compassion, or mercy: (S, O, K:) a favour, a benefit, an act of beneficence or kindness: a gratuity, or free gift: (K:) and [ a return, i. e.] advantage, profit, or utility

; or a cause, or means, thereof: (S, O, K:) a subst. from EaAda bimaEoruwfK : (Msb:) pl. EawaAy^idu . (A.) One says, fulaAnN *uw SafoHK waEaAy^idapK Such a one is a person of forgiving disposition, and of favour, kindness, or pity. (S, A, O.) And A_in~ahu lakaviyru AlEawaAy^idi EalaY qawomihi [ Verily he is one who confers, or bestows, many favours, or benefits, upon his people ]. (A.)

senses.text: means This thing is more remunerative, advantageous, or profitable, to thee than such a thing: (S, O, K: *) or more easy, or convenient, to thee. (A, * TA.)

, signifying Return, is originally maEowadN . (IAth, TA.) See EawodN , first and third sentences. ― -b2- Also A place to which a person, or thing, returns: a place, state, or result, to which a person, or thing, eventually comes; a place of destination, or an ultimate state or condition: syn. marojiEN : and maSiyrN . (S, A, O, K.) ― -b3- [Hence,] AlmaEaAdu signifies [particularly] The ultimate state of existence, in the world to come; syn. AlA=xirapu ; (M, K, TA;) [and] so maEaAdu Alxaloqi : (S, O:) the place to which one comes on the day of resurrection. (TA.) And Paradise. (K.) And Mekkeh: (O, K:) the conquest of which was promised to the Prophet: (TA:) so called because the pilgrims return to it. (O.) laraAd~uka A_ilaY maEaAdK , in the Kur [xxviii. 85], is expl. as meaning will assuredl
and maEowuwdN , (K,) the latter anomalous, (TA,) A sick person visited. (K.)

A stallion-camel that has covered repeatedly; (S, M, O, K;) and that does not require assistance in his doing so. (Sh, O.) ― -b2- And hence, (Sh, O,) applied to a man Acquainted with affairs, (Sh, O, K,) not inexperienced therein, (Sh, O,) possessing skill and ability to do a thing. (O, K. *) One says, fulaAnN muEiydN lih`*aA AlA^amori , meaning Such a one is able to do this thing: (S, O, Msb, K: *) because accustomed, or habituated, to it. (Msb.) ― -b3- And hence, (O,) or because he returns to his prey time after time, (TA,) The lion, (O, K, TA.) ― -b4- Almubodiy^u AlmuEiydu applied to God: ― -b5- and mubodiy^N muEiydN applied to a man, and to a horse: see art. bdA^ . ― -b6- muEiydN also signifies A road travelled and trodden time after time. (TA.) [See also EawodN .]
: see maEaAdN , last two sentences.
Persevering; (Lth, A, K;) applied to a man. (Lth, A.) ― -b2- A courageous man; (S, O, K;) because he does not become weary of conflict. (S, O.) ― -b3- And One skilful in his work. (A.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. yaEuw*u , (S, A, O, L, Msb,) inf. n. Eawo*N (O, L, K) and EiyaA*N and maEaA*N (O, L, Msb, K) and maEaA*apN ; (O, K;) and bihi ↓ ; (O, L, Msb, K; *) and bihi ↓ ; (S, A, O, L, Msb, K; *) He sought protection, or preservation, by him; sought, or took, refuge in him; had recourse to him for protection, preservation, or refuge; sought his protection, or preservation; confided or trusted or put his trust in him, or relied upon him, for protection, or preservation; (S, A, O, L, Msb, K;) namely, God, (S, A, O, L, Msb,) or a man; (S, O;) [and in like manner used in relation to a place; mino ka*aA and Eanohu from such a thing

; or followed by mino A^ano , or only A^ano , and a mansoob aorist.] ↓ , occurring in a trad., means He only said it (referring to the profession of the faith) to seek protection, or preservation, thereby from slaughter; not being sincere in his profession of El-Islám. (L.) And one says, maEaA*a A@ll~`hi , (S, A, O, L, K,) and maEaA*apa A@ll~`hi , (S, O, L, K,) and maEaA*a wajohi A@ll~`hi , and maEaA*apa wajohi A@ll~`hi , (S, O, L,) and EiyaA*a A@ll~`hi , (A,) meaning A^aEuw*u biA@ll~`hi maEaA*FA [ I seek protection, or preservation, by God; &c.; which is equivalent to the saying may God protect me, or preserve me ]: (S, A, O, L, K:) maEaA*FA [as also maEaA*apF ] being here used instead of the verb because it is an inf. n., though [accord. to some] not employed as such [in other cases], li
; or that of having recently brought forth. (S, O, L, K.) One says, hiYa fiYEiyaA*ihaA She is in the early stage of the period after having brought forth. (S, O, L.)

2 , and bihi ↓ , I made another to seek protection, or preservation, by such a one; to seek, or take, refuge in him; to have recourse to him for protection, preservation, or refuge; to seek his protection, or preservation; to confide, or trust, or put his trust, in him, or to rely upon him, for protection, or preservation; (S, O, * L;) [ mino ka*aA and Eanohu from such a thing: and in like manner, Eaw~a*otuhu biA@ll~`hi , and bihi ↓ , I made him to seek protection, or preservation, by God; &c.] -A2- And Eaw~a*otuhu bika*aA I prayed for his protection, or preservation, by such a thing [i. e. by invoking God, or uttering some charm; mino ka*aA from such a thing; and A^ano yafoEala ka*aA from his doing such a thing; as also bihi ↓ , of which see an ex. in art. ybs , conj. 2]. (Har p.
49.) ― -b2- And Eaw~a*ahu [and ↓ ] He charmed him [against such a thing ( mino ka*aA )]

; or fortified him by a charm, or an amulet. (L.) And Eaw~a*otuhu biA@ll~`hi and bihi ↓ I charmed him (i. e. a child) [ by invoking God ]. (Msb. [Both mentioned in the present art. thereof, and the former said in art. rqY of the same to be syn. with raqayotuhu .]) And Eaw~a*otu fulaAnFA biA@ll~`hi , and biA^asomaAy^ihi , and biAlmuEaw~i*atayoni , I said to such a one, I charm thee (↓ ) by [ invoking ] God, and by his names, and by the muEaw~i*ataAni [q. v.], against every evil person or thing, and every disease, and an envier, and destruction, or trial. (L.) It is said of the Prophet, kaAna yuEaw~i*u nafosahu biAlmuEaw~i*atayoni [ He used to charm himself against evil by reciting the mEw~*tAn ]. (L.) And Eaw~a*ataAhu , said of the muEaw~i*ataAni , means They preserved him from any evil. (M
4 see 2, in seven places: -A2- and see also 1, last sentence but one, in two places.
5 see 1, in two places.
6 They sought protection, preservation, or refuge, one of another
; or confided in, or relied upon, one another's protection, or preservation; (A, O, L, K; *) fiY AlHarobi in war. (O, L.)
10 see 1, first sentence. faA@sotaEi*o biA@ll~`hi in the Kur xvi.
100 means Then say thou A^aEuw*u biA@ll~`hi [ I seek protection, or preservation, by God; &c.]. (L.)

: see maEaA*N , in two places. ― -b2- Also A tree, or some other thing, beneath which, or in which, one takes refuge, or shelter. (L.) ― -b3- A thing, such as a stone, or trunk of a tree, surrounded by things blown against it and around it by the wind. (T, L.) ― -b4- Fallen leaves; (AHn, L, K:) so called because they shelter themselves against any rising thing, such as a building or a sand-hill or a mountain. (AHn, L.) ― -b5- Vile, or ignoble, persons
; or the worse or viler, or the worst or vilest, of mankind. (IAar, L, K.) -A2- A^afolata fulaAnN minohu Eawa*FA [ Such a one escaped from him without being beaten

; or without being killed, though beaten; ] is said when one has frightened the other; but not beaten him; (S, O, L, K; *) or beaten him, desiring to kill him, but not killed him. (S, O, L.) ― -b2- And maA tarakotuhu A_il~aA Eawa*FA minohu means I left him not save from dislike, or hatred, of him; as also mnh ↓ . (S, O, L.)

(S, A, O, L, K) and ↓ (S, O, L, K) and ↓ (S, A, L, K) are syn., (S, A, O, L, K,) signifying A kind of amulet, phylactery, or charm, bearing an inscription, which is hung upon a man [ or woman or child or horse &c. ], to charm the wearer against the evil eye and against fright and diabolical possession, and which is forbidden to be hung upon the person, (L,) unless inscribed with something from the Kur-án or with the names of God, for in this case there is no harm in it: (S and Mgh voce tamiymapN :) accord. to some of the etymologists, originally signifying an amulet, a phylactery, or a charm, upon which is [ an inscription commencing with the word ] A^aEuw*u ; and afterwards applied in a general manner [as meaning any amulet ]; (MF;) i. q. ruqoyapN , (K,) or tamiymapN : (A:) or those who i
: see Eawa*N , last sentence.

[as though fem. of A^agozaru ] is applied to a she-camel by Honeyf-El-Hanátim [as meaning Surpassingly abundant in milk ]. (IAar in TA in art. bhY .)

, and the fem. gaziyrapN , Much; abundant; copious: (S, Msb, K:) applied to water, (Msb,) and rain, (K,) and beneficence, (S,) and knowledge, (TA,) and anything. and ↓ One who gives a thing in order that he may obtain in return more than he gives. (K.) (S, K.) -A2- gazila , (S, O, K, TA,) aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. gazalN , (S, O, TA,) He talked, and acted in an amatory and enticing manner, with a woman, or with women; he practised gazal [meaning as expl. below, i. e. the talk, and actions, and circumstances, occurring between the lover and the object of love; &c.]. (S, * O, * K, * TA.) -A3- And gazila is also said of a dog, meaning He flagged, or became remiss, in the pursuit of a young gazelle; i. e., when he had come up to it, the latter uttered a cry by reason of its fright, wher

(MA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, A^aToyabu mino A^anofaAsi AlS~abaA A_i*aA gaAzalato riyaADa AlrbA (tropical:) [ More pleasant, or delightful, than the breaths of the east wind (which is to the Arabs like the zephyr to us) when it has wantoned with the meadows of AlrbA , (app. Alr~ubaA , the name of a place, mentioned in the K in art. rbw , there written Alr~ubaY , and in the TA in that art. said to occur in poetry,) so as to have brought with it the odours of flowers]. , as expl. by 'Abd-El-Muttalib El-Baghdádee, in his Exposition of the naqodu Al$iEori of Kudámeh, signifies The talk, and actions, and circumstances, occurring between the lover and the object of love; differing somewhat from ta$obiybN , which is a celebrating of the person and qualities of the beloved; and from nasiybN , which is a mentioning of the state, or condition, of the naAsib [himself], and of the object of the nasiyb , and of all the affairs, or events, occurring between them two, [in the prelude of an ode,] thus including the meaning of ta$obiybN , and being a mentioning of gazal : accord. to Kudámeh, it signifies an inclining to foolish and youthful conduct, or a manifesting of passionate love, and becoming notorious for affections to women: (TA:) or it is the subst. from

[is, by, rule, the part. n. of gazila , as such signifying Talking, and acting in an amatory and enticing manner, with a woman, or with women; &c.: but it is said that it] signifies SaAHibu gazalK ; (S, O;) or mutagaz~ilN biAln~isaA='i ; (K, TA;) by which is here meant making mention, or speaking, or one who makes mention, or who speaks, [generally in verse, ] of what is termed gazal [signifying as expl. above, i. e. the talk, and actions, and circumstances, occurring between the lover and the object of love; &c.]; thus used as being a possessive epithet, [not as a part. n. of gazila , because this differs in meaning from tagaz~ala ,] i. e. it signifies [properly] *uwgazalK : (TA:) or it means displaying amorous gestures or behaviour, and foolish and youthful conduct such as is suitable to

fem. of gazaAlN , q. v. -A2- AlgazaAlapu , also, signifies The sun; (S, O, K;) because it extends [what resemble] cords, [meaning its rays,] as though it were spinning: (K:) or the sun when rising; (Msb, K;) [therefore] one says TalaEati AlgazaAlapu , but not garabati AlgazaAlapu : (TA:) or the sun when high: (M, * K, TA:) or the Eayon [meaning the disk, or, as it sometimes means, the rays, or beams, ] of the sun. senses.text: 1 , [aor. ,] inf. n. gazowN , He willed, or desired, it; he sought it; and he aimed at it, intended it, or meant it; syn. A^araAdahu ; and Talabahu ; and qaSadahu ; [the first of which is often used in the same senses as the second and third;] as also ↓ ; (K, TA;) this last mentioned by ISd as syn. with qaSadahu . (TA.) One says, Earafotu maA yugozaY mino h`*aA AlkalaAmi i. e. [ I knew, or, emphatically, I know, ] what is willed or desired ( maA yuraAdu ) [ from this speech ]. (S.) And gazowiY ka*aA My aim, or intention, or meaning, is such a thing. (K.) ― -b2- [

Hence, app.,] gazaA AlEaduw~a , inf. n. gazowN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and gazawaAnN , (K, TA,) or, as some say, gazowaAnN , mentioned by Sb, (TA,) and gazaAwapN , (K,) [but see what is said of this last at the close of this paragraph,] He went forth, (Er-Rághib, TA,) or repaired, or betook himself, (Mgh,) to wage war, (Er-Rághib, TA,) or to fight, (Mgh,) with the enemy; (Er-Rághib, Mgh, TA;) or he went to fight with, and plunder, the enemy; (K, TA;) in the country of the latter. (Msb.) [And gazaA alone, the objective complement being understood, often signifies the same

; or He engaged in a warring, or warring and plundering, expedition, or in such expeditions. ] ― -b3- And gazaA A_ilayohi , inf. n. as above, He tended, repaired, betook himself, or went, to, or towards, him, or it; syn. qaSadahu . (TA.) -A2- gazaAwapN , mentioned above, is of a measure which in most instances is that of an inf. n. of an intrans. verb, and it seems to be an inf. n. of which the verb is gazuwa , meaning jaAda gazowuhu [i. e. Excellent, or how excellent, is his engaging in a warring, or warring and plundering, expedition, or in such expeditions! ]; and to be similar to qaDuwa meaning jaAda qaDaA='uhu , and Darubato yaduhu meaning jaAda DarobuhaA . (TA.)
2 see what next follows.

(K.) -A2- A^agozato , said of a woman, (Mgh, K,) Her husband was absent [ engaged in a warring, or warring and plundering, expedition, in the country of the enemy ]; (Mgh;) or her husband went [or had gone ] to fight with, and plunder, the enemy. (K.) ― -b2- And, said of a she-camel, Her impregnation was, or became, difficult. (S, K.) -A3- And AgzAhu He granted him some delay, and deferred [ the exacting of ] the debt that he owed. (S, K.)

i. q. TilobapN [app. as meaning A mode, or manner, of seeking, &c. ]. (TA.)

and AlmgzY [app. AlA^agozaA='u and ↓ , the former a pl. of which the sing. is not mentioned, and the latter a quasi-pl. n. like Almarojalu from Alr~ajulu ,] The offspring ( nataAy^ij [more properly nitaAj , which agrees with the context,]) of the [ season called ] Sayof , on the authority of IAar, [meaning such offspring of camels, for it is added,] which are discommended, the young camel thereof being always weak. Hence, in a trad., gasaqa All~ayolu EalaY AlZ~iraAbi i. e. The night poured down upon the small mountains and covered them with its darkness. (TA.) ― -b2- And, said of the moon, It lost its light, and became black and dark. (TA.) ― -b3- And gasaqato Eayonuhu , (S, O, K,) aor. ; (O, K;) and gasiqato , aor. ; (K;) inf. n. gasoqN , (S, O,) or gusuwqN , (K,) or both, (TA,) and gasaqaAnN ; (K, TA;) (assumed tropical:) His eye became dark: (S, O, K, TA:) or (assumed tropical:) shed tears: (K, TA:) or (tropical:) poured forth [ tears ]: (TA:) or gsqt AlEayonu means (assumed tropical:) the eye overflowed with water. (AZ, TA.) ― -b4- And gasaqa AljuroHu , inf. n. gasaqaAnN (S, O, K) and gasoqN also, (TA,) The wound had yellow water flowing from it; (S, O, K;) and so gasiqa . (K, by implication.) An

; or let fall a little rain, such as is termed ra$~N : (O, K, TA:) and [ the rain ] poured forth; syn. AinoSab~at : (TA:) [and in this latter sense gasaqa is app. said of any fluid; for,] accord. to Th, (O, TA,) gasaqaAnN is syn. with AinoSibaAbN . (O, K, TA.) A drowning; being drowned: so in the phrase mawotu Algamari Death by drowning. (TA.) -A2- See also gamorN . -A3- The foul smell of flesh-meat, (S, Mgh, K,) and its grease adhering to the hand: (K:) and the smell of fish. (S.)
Hence, minodiylu Algamari (S, Mgh) The napkin, or rough napkin, with which the hand is cleansed therefrom. (L, TA.) -A4- See also gumorN , in two places.

[part. n. of gamira ]. You say yadN gamirapN A hand foul with the smell of flesh-meat, (S, K,) and with the grease thereof adhering to it. (K.) [See also sahikN .] -A2- See also gumorN , in two places. -A3- gamirapN as an epithet applied to a she-camel, see voce gabirN .

A small drinking-cup or bowl, (S, K,) with which people divided the water among themselves in a journey when they had little of it; and this they [sometimes] did by putting a pebble into a vessel, and then pouring into it as much water as would cover the pebble, and giving it to each man among them: (TA:) or the smallest of drinking-cups or bowls: (K:) [see qaEobN ; and tibonN :] accord. to ISh, it contains twice or thrice the quantity of the measure called kiylajap : [but this seems to be a large gmr , used for watering a horse; and the words which here immediately follow are app. not added by ISh, but relate to the gmr used by a man for himself or for another man:] the qaEob is larger than it, and satisfies the thirst of a man: the pl. is A^agomaArN . (TA.) El-Aashà of Báhileh says, in a
Water that rises above the stature of a man. (Bd in xxiii.
56.) See also gamorN , first sentence. ― -b2-

Hence, (Bd,) fa*arohumo fiY gamoratihimo , in the Kur xxiii. 56, (tropical:) Therefore leave thou them in [ the submerging gulf, or flood, of ] their ignorance; (Fr, Bd;) or in their error: (Jel:) or in their error and obstinacy and perplexity: (Zj, in explanation of another reading, fY gamaraAtihimo :) and in like manner, fiY gamorapN , in the same chap., verse 65, signifies in overwhelming heedlessness: (Bd:) or in ignorance: (Jel:) and in the Kur li. 11, in overwhelming ignorance: (Bd, Jel:) or gamorapN signifies [here] a state of obstinate perseverance in vain or false affairs: (Lth, Msb, TA:) and gamaraAtN is the pl. (Msb.) You say huwa fiY gamorapK mino lahowK , and $abiybapK , and sukorK , (tropical:) [ He is in a submerging gulf, or flood, of frivolous diversion, and of youthful fo

; or] the places, of Hell, that abound with fire. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence] gamorapu AlxuSuwmapi (assumed tropical:) The main part of the contention. (TA.) [And gamorapu AlHarobi (assumed tropical:) The main part, i. e. the thick, or thickest, of the fight or battle. (See also gamaraAtu AlHarobi in what follows.)] ― -b4- Hence likewise, gamorapN signifies also (tropical:) Difficulty, trouble, distress, or rigour, (S, Msb, K,) and pressure, of a thing: (K:) pl. gamaraAtN (S, Msb, K) and gimaArN (K) and gumarN . (S.)

Hence, (Msb,) gamaraAtu Almawoti (tropical:) The rigours, or pangs, ( $adaAy^idu ,) of death: (S, Msb:) or gamorapu Almawoti signifies the agony, i. e. the vehemence of the troubles or disquietudes, of death: (TA:) and gamaraAtu AlHarobi , and gimaAruhaA , (assumed tropical:) the rigours of war. (TA.) ― -b5- See also gamorN again, latter half, in three places.

A kind of liniment, made from [ the plant called ] waros , (S, TA,) used by a bride, for her person: (TA:) or [the plant ] wrs [ itself ]: (TA:) or saffron; as also ↓ : (K:) or kurokumN [which also means saffron and bastard saffron ]: or gypsum; syn. jiS~N : or, accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed, a mixture of dates and milk, with which the face of a woman is smeared, to render her skin fine: and the pl. is gumarN . (TA.) [See also xumorapN .]
, [thus in the TA, app. gumarapN , of the class of SuraEapN &c.,] as an epithet applied to a man, Valid in judgment or opinion, in cases of difficulty. (TA.)

: see gamorN , in two places. -A2- Also A certain plant: (K:) or green herbage that is overtopped, or covered, and concealed, by what is dried up: (S, K: *) or herbage growing in the lower part, or at the root, of [ other ] herbage, (K, * TA,) so that the first [ in growth ] overtops, or covers, and conceals, it: (TA:) or any verdure that is little in quantity, (L, K, TA,) either ryHp [i. e. ray~iHap , meaning what becomes green after the upper parts have dried, ] or nbAt [app. meaning herbage in general ]: (L, TA:) or the grain of the [ species of barley-grass called ] buhomaY , (K, TA,) that falls from the ears thereof when it dries; so says AHn: or somewhat that comes forth in the buhomaY in the first of the rain, succulent, or sappy, amid such as is dry; and gamiyr is not known in anyt
: see what next precedes.
Much, or abundant: applied in this sense to property. (Ham p.

593.) [See also gamorN .] -A2- [ In a state of immersion; immerged. (See A^ataAnN ; and see also a verse cited voce A^ano , p. 106, first col.)] ― -b2- And [hence, perhaps,] gaAmirapN signifies Palm-trees ( naxolN ) not requiring irrigation: (AHn, K:) but Az did not find this to be known. (TA.) [See also mugotamirN .] ― -b3- Applied to land, (S, Msb, TA,) and to a house, (TA,) [but written with p when A^aroDN is mentioned, or daArN ,] it signifies the Contr. of EaAmirN ; (S, TA;) and thus, (TA,) waste; desolate; in a state the contrary of flourishing; in a state of ruin; syn. xaraAbN : (Msb, K, TA:) [land to which this term is applied is thus called] because overflowed by water, so that it cannot be sown
; or because it is covered with sand or dust

; or because water generally exudes from it, so that it produces only reeds and the barodiY~ [i. e. papyrus or other rushes]: by gaAmirN is meant *uw gamorK ; like as one says ham~N naASibN , meaning *uw naSabK : (TA:) or any land that is not tilled ( lamo yusotaxorajo ) so as to be fit for sowing (K, TA) and planting: (TA:) or land that is unsown, but capable of being sown: so called because the water reaches it and comes over it: of the measure faAEilN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN ; (S, Msb;) like the epithets in sir~N kaAtimN and maA='N daAfiqN ; and made of the measure fAl only to correspond to EaAmirN as its opposite: (S, TA:) waste land which water does not reach is not called gaAmirN ; (S;) but such is called qaforN . (Msb.) It is said in a trad., [which shows that the last

[ More, or most, abundant, copious, or deep: applied to water. ― -b2- ] More, or most surpassing, or excelling: so in the saying, huwa A^agomaruhumo biTuwli qawaAmihi He is the most surpassing of them by the tallness of his stature. (TA.)
A garment, or piece of cloth, dyed with [ gumorap , or] saffron. (M, TA.) ― -b2- mugom~arapN and ↓ and ↓ A girl having her face smeared with gumorap . (TA.) -A2- See also gumorN .

You say also, fulaAnN mgomuwru Aln~`asabi (assumed tropical:) Such a one is of obscure race. (TA.)

(assumed tropical:) One who plunges, or rushes without consideration, into places of peril: (S:) one who throws himself into difficulties, troubles, or distresses; as also ↓ : (K:) or one who enters into difficulties, troubles, or distresses, and makes another, or others, to do so; like mugaAmisN . (Ham p.

338.) Applied to a courageous man as meaning (assumed tropical:) One who incurs the rigours, or pangs, of death. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) One who contends in an altercation, or a dispute: or who enters into the main part [or the thick or thickest ] of an altercation or a dispute: and some say that it is from Algimoru , and means regarding, and regarded, with rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite. (TA.)

Palm-trees ( naxolN ) imbibing water from a copious source. (AHn, K.) [See also gaAmirapN , voce gaAmirN .] ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) A drunken man: (Sgh, K, TA:) as though intoxication had drowned his reason. (TA.) -A2- See also mugam~arN .

senses.text: 1 , (S, A, K,) or gamazahu biyadihi , (Msb,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. gamozN , (TA,) He felt him, (namely, a ram,) to know if he were fat: (S, A, Msb, K:) and gamazahaA he put his hand upon her (a camel's) back, to see how fat she was. (TA.) ― -b2-

Hence, (Msb,) gamazahu biyadihi , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. gamozN , (A, K,) He pressed, or squeezed, it, [ with his hand, ] namely, a limb, (A, K, TA,) and a man's back. (TA.) So in a trad. of 'Omar: daxala Ealayohi waEinodahu gulayomN yagomizu Zahorahu [ He went in to him, and with him was a little boy pressing, or squeezing, or kneading, his back ]. (TA.) And in a trad. respecting the ablution termed Algusol , it is said, AigomiziY quruwnaki , meaning Press thou, or squeeze thou, the locks of thy hair, in washing. (TA.) You also say, gamaza Alv~iqaAfu AlqanaApa The straightening-instrument pinched and pressed the spear. (A, * Mgh, TA. *) A poet (namely Ziyád El-Aajam, TA) says, wakunotu A_i*aA gamazotu qanaApa qawomK kasarotu kuEuwbahaA A^awo tasotaqiymaA [ And I used, when I pin

4 lee made a sign to me with the eye, or eyebrow, meaning, Say thou Yes. (Mgh.) The people of the West say, gamazahu fulaAnN bifulaAnK , meaning, (tropical:) Such a one blinked towards such a one, to instigate him against him, or in order that he should have recourse to him for protection or the like, or seek aid of him. (Mgh.) ― -b2-
Hence, Algamozu biAln~aAsi : (S:) you say, gamaza biAlr~ajuli , aor. , (K,) inf. n. gamozN , (TA,) (tropical:) He calumniated, or slandered, the man. (K.) [See also

4.] ― -b3- You say also, gumizato $ahaAdatahu [(assumed tropical:) His testimony was suspected (see magomuwzN ), or impugned ]. (TA in art. zwr .) -A3- gamazati Ald~aAb~apu , (K,) or gamaza fiY ma$oyihi , (Msb,) or mino rijolihi , (S,) aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. gamozN , (S, Msb,) (assumed tropical:) The beast limped, or it halted, with its hind leg; had a slight lameness thereof: (K, * TA:) or he had what resembled Earaj [or natural lameness ] in his gait: (Msb:) or, as IKtt says, gamazati Ald~aAb~apu birijolihaA the beast gave an indication of a limping, or halting, or slight lameness, in its hind leg: whence it appears that this signification may be tropical. (TA.) -A4- gamaza said of a disease, or of a vice, or fault, of a man, It appeared. (AA, K.) -A5- See also
3 [This verb is mentioned by Golius as syn. with EAyb , a verb for which I find no authority: and Freytag renders it “ Vitii arguit, ” and refers to a passage in Har (p.
427 of the see. ed.) where (like as is done by Golius) AlmugAmiz and AlmuEAyib , as syn., are erroneously put for AlmagAmiz and AlmaEAyib .]

4 She (a camel) had fat, (O, K,) or a little fat, (ISd, IKtt, TA,) in her hump. (ISd, IKtt, O, K.) Hence the epithet ↓ , applied to her. (TA.) -A2- Agmz fiY fulaAnK (tropical:) He blamed, or found fault with, such a one; attributed or imputed to him, or charged him with, or accused him of, a vice, or fault; (S, IKtt, K, TA;) deemed him weak; (TA;) lessened his rank, or dignity: (S, IKtt, K, * TA:) he found in him that for which he should be deemed weak: (A, TA:) and ↓ he impugned his character; blamed him; censured him

; or spoke against him. (K.) You say, fulaAnN ↓ (tropical:) I did a thing, and such a one impugned my character, or found in it that by which my character was impugned. (S, TA.) And samiEa min~iY kalimapF fiY Eaqolihi ↓ (tropical:) He heard from me a saying, and deemed it weak: (A, TA:) and in like manner, A^agomaza fiyhaA found in it that for which it was to be deemed weak. (TA.) -A3- A^agomazaniY AlHar~u (tropical:) The heat remitted, or abated, to me, so that I became emboldened to encounter it, and went upon the road: (AA, ISk, S, IKtt, K, * TA:) Az says ↓ AlHar~u , on the authority of AA: (TA:) and AA mentioned AgmrnY AlHr~ in this sense, but afterwards doubted, and said, I think that it is with zAY . (TA in art. gmr .) ― -b2- And A^agomaza (assumed tropical:) He (a man) became gentle
5 [This verb is said by Freytag to have a signification belonging to tagam~ara .]

6 They made signs, one to another, with their eyes, (S, A, K, B,) or with the eyebrow, (A,) or hand, indicating something blameable or faulty. (B.) In this sense it is expl. as used in the Kur lxxxiii.

Cattle (i. e. camels, and sheep or goats, TA) of a bad quality. (As, S, O, K.) ― -b2- And A weak man: (S, O, K:) like qamazN : pl. A^agomaAzN , like A^aqomaAzN of qamazN . (TA.)
A she-camel of which one doubts whether she be fat or not and therefore feels the hump: (A'Obeyd, S, K:) pl. gumozN [or gumuzN , or both?]. (TA.) See 4, first sentence.
: see the next paragraph, in two places.

(tropical:) A thing for which one's character is to be impugned; for which one is to be blamed, censured, or spoken against; a vice, or fault; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ (TA) and ↓ (S, A, Mgh, K) or ↓ : (Msb:) and weakness in work, and impotence of mind, (TA,) and ignorance: (T, TA:) the pl. of ↓ is magaAmizu , (TA,) syn. with maEaAyibu . (S.) You say, layosa fiyhi gamiyzapN , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ , (TA,) and ↓ , (A, Mgh, K,) or ↓ , (Msb,) (tropical:) There is not in him anything for which his character is to be impugned

; or for which he is to be blamed; &c.: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) or there is not in it anything for which it is to be coveted: (K:) or ↓ has both of the above-mentioned significations. (A.) And fiY jam~apN ↓ (tropical:) In such a woman are many vices, or faults. (A.) [See magomazN , below.]

A girl who presses, or squeezes, or kneads, the limbs well with the hand. (A, K, * TA.) -A2- AimoraA^apN gam~aAzapN (tropical:) A woman who makes frequent signs with the eye, &c.; who has a habit of doing so; syn. ram~aAzapN . (TA in art. rmz .) ― -b2- gam~aAzN One who blames, or finds fault with, others, much, or habitually. (TA in art. hmz .)
[meaning Limping, or halting, &c., and having a limping, or halting, &c.,] is like ZaAliEN : sometimes used as a possessive noun; and [therefore] one does not say gaAmizapN . (O and TA in art. ZlE .)

[should by rule be magomizN : its primary signification is A place of feeling, to know if an animal be fat: hence, a place of pressing or squeezing a limb &c.: and a place of pinching and pressing a spear, to straighten it]. ― -b2- nukotapN laAmagomaza liqanaAtihaA walaA maqoraEa liSafaAtihaA (tropical:) [lit. A nice or subtile saying, the spear of which has no place where it requires to be pinched and pressed to straiten it, and the rock of which has no rough place requiring to be beaten, or for the rock of which there is no beating, ] means, (assumed tropical:) that has no crookedness: mqrE is an inf. n., or means “ a place of beating, ” and SfAp is “ a rock; ” and the above-mentioned use of these two words is borrowed from the phrase qaraEa SafaAtahu , meaning (tropical:) “ he impugned
; or spoke against him. ” (Mgh.) ― -b3- See also gamiyzapN , in five places.
: see gamiyzapN , in two places.

senses.text: 1 , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. gamosN , (Msb, TA,) He immersed, immerged, dipped, plunged, or sunk, him or it, (JK, TA,) syn. maqalahu , (S, A, K,) in water, (JK, S, A, Msb, K,) or other fluid; (JK, * TA;) as, for instance, a morsel of food in vinegar, and the hand in Hin~aA=' , (A,) and a garment, or piece of cloth, [for Alv~adoY in the TA, I read Alv~awob ,] in water or in dye. (TA.) ― -b2- AixotaDabato gamosFA , so in the T and the Tekmileh; [and so in the JK;] but in the [O and] K, gamosFA ↓ ; (TA;) She (a woman, O, TA) immersed her hand, (K,) or, as in the [O and other] correct lexicons, her hands, (TA,) [ in the Hin~aA=' ] so as to dye [ it or them ] uniformly, without taSowiyr [or figuring ], (O, K,) for which last word Sgh [in the TS] writes tSryr , and for which we f
2 signifies The making a drinking to be little in quantity: (O, K, TA:) or, accord. to Kr, a man's watering his camels and then going away. (TA.)

3 [ gAmshu , inf. n. mugaAmasapN , He vied, or contended, with him in plunging, or diving, in water:] mugaAmasapN is syn. with mumaAqalapN . (S, TA.) ― -b2- mugaAmasapN also signifies (tropical:) The throwing one's self into the midst of war or fight. (S, TA,) or of an affair or a great affair or an affliction: (TA:) and the mixing, or engaging, in fight or conflict. (TA.) You say, gaAmasa fiY AlqitaAli (tropical:) He plunged, or threw himself, into the midst of fight or conflict
; or he rushed headlong into it. (TA.) And gaAmasahumo (tropical:) He mixed, or engaged, with them in fight or conflict. (TA). [See also mugaAmisN ].
6 They two vied, or contended, each with the other, in plunging, or diving, in water; syn. tamaAqalaA and tagaATasaA . (TA in art. gTs .)

7 (S, A, Msb) and ↓ (S, A) He, or it, became immersed, immerged, dipped, plunged, or sunk, in water: or he immersed or immerged himself, plunged, or dived, in water: (S, A, Msb:) or he did so remaining long therein. (TA in this art. and in art. rms .) [See Artms .] ― -b2- [Hence,] ↓ the latter also signifies, [and so app. the former,] (assumed tropical:) He hid, or concealed, himself. (T, O.)

, [like nafaDN in the sense of manofuwDN , &c., or perhaps a mistranscription for gamosN , like garosN in the sense of magoruwsN , and many other instances,] Immersed, immerged, dipped, plunged, or sunk. (TA.)

(tropical:) A spear-wound, or the like, that passes through: (S, A, Msb, K:) the epithet properly applies to the person who inflicts the wound, because he thrusts in ( yagomis ) the spearhead so that it passes through, or so that its extremity protrudes: and it is such as cleaves the flesh: (A:) or wide, and passing through; that plunges into the flesh. (ISd, TA.) ― -b2- A^amorN gamuwsN (tropical:) A difficult, or distressful, affair; (S, A, Msb, K;) that plunges people into trial, or affliction. (A, K. *) ― -b3-

Hence, (A,) yamiynN gamuwsN (tropical:) An oath that plunges its swearer ( tagomisuhu ) into sin, (S, K,) and then into the fire [ of Hell ]: (K:) or a false oath, (Mgh, Msb,) known by its swearer to be so; (Msb;) so called because it plunges its swearer into sin, (A, Mgh, Msb,) and then into the fire [of Hell]: (A, Mgh:) or a false oath which one purposely swears, knowing the case to be the contrary thereof, (K, TA,) in order to cut off the rights of others: (TA:) or an oath by which one cuts off for himself the property of another: (K:) or an oath in which there is made no exception [by saying A_ino $aA='a A@ll~`hu (if God will), or the like]. (TA.) [See also Algamiysap .] ― -b4- rajulN gamuwsN (assumed tropical:) A strong, courageous man; as also ↓ : which latter epithet is also applied

Such as is termed gamiyr [q. v.] of herbage; (S, O, K, TA;) i. e. such as has become green in consequence of rain, in the lower parts of that which is dry. (O.) See also gamiymN . ― -b2- And A thing that has not appeared to men, and that is not known, as yet: whence the phrase qaSiydapN gamiysN [ an ode that has not become known: the epithet being masc. and fem.]. (O, K.) ― -b3- And i. q. (TA.) ― -b4- And A water-course, or channel in which water flows, (S, O, K, TA,) or (TA) such as

; or a bed, or place of growth, thereof. (TA. [See also gamiysN .]) -A2- Halafa EalaY Algamiysapi He swore a false oath. (TA. [See gamwusN .])

[or rather coll. gen. n.] ↓ : (K, TA: [in the CK, erroneously, gum~AsN :]) IDrd says, the ↓ is a wellknown bird. (O.)

One who plunges into wars, or battles, ( yago$aY AlHuruwba ,) and engages in them repeatedly: (Ham p. 27:) or one who enters into difficulties, troubles, or distresses, and makes another, or others, to do so; like mugaAmirN . (Id. p.

alphabetical letter The eighteenth letter of the alphabet: called EayonN . It is [one of the letters termed majohuwrap , or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, not with the breath only; and] of the letters termed Haloqiy~ap [or faucial]; these being E and H and h and x and g [and A^ ]; the lowest of which in its place of utterance is E ; wherefore Kh [in the composition of his lexicon entitled “ Kitáb el-'Eyn ”] and several other lexicographers [after him] began their books with [words having] this letter [in their roots], giving the next place to H , the next to h , the next to x , and the next to g . (L, TA.) It is substituted for ' [in what is termed the EanoEanap of Temeem]; as in Eano for A^ano : and for H ; as in Eat~aY for Hat~aY , and SuboEN for SuboHN : and for g ; as in EulaA
